Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Talks Legacy Before Finishing Wardley Business
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois expects a smoother win over Fabio Wardley on October 17, but his talk of becoming a heavyweight legend runs ahead of what he has established. Wardley dropped him twice in their first fight, giving the challenger good reason to believe the rematch can end differently.

“Even better and even smoother than last time,” Dubois told Queensberry. “I feel like I’ve improved and, having been the champion, I’ve improved double. That’s some boxing history I’ve got—a two-time world champion—and now I need to go down as a legend.”

Dubois earned credit for recovering to stop Wardley in the 11th round in May. That showed toughness, stamina, and the power to turn a dangerous fight around. It also showed that Wardley can put him on the floor. Claiming substantial improvement is easy; showing how he will prevent Fabio from landing those damaging punches is the test.

The wins over Jarrell Miller and Filip Hrgovic required Dubois to work through difficult stretches, too. Joe Joyce stopped him, and Oleksandr Usyk beat him twice inside the distance. Those results do not erase his achievements, but they give little support to the idea that beating Wardley once makes the return fight straightforward.

His knockout of Anthony Joshua remains his biggest-name victory. Still, Joshua’s vulnerability to heavy punches limits how much that performance tells us about Dubois against the other leading heavyweights. Flattening Joshua did not translate into solving Usyk.

Dubois has a decent chin, but shots he does not see coming can hurt him. Wardley already knows he has the power to exploit that vulnerability, and he does not need to win every round to threaten the champion. Dubois needs to beat Wardley again, then pursue the other champions.

Unification victories and successful defenses would build the record behind his ambition. Right now, he is discussing his place in heavyweight history while preparing to face a man who nearly ended his latest title run before it began.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez’s Kovalev Win Deserves a Rehydration Footnote
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez’s knockout victory against Sergey Kovalev deserves an official notation detailing the morning weigh-in cap attached to their November 2, 2019 meeting. Canelo captured the WBO light heavyweight belt, yet the terms he secured belong right beside that win in the history books.

The contest occurred at the full 175-pound championship limit, but contract terms barred either man from exceeding 185 pounds during a second check on fight morning. Skipping a traditional catchweight did not grant Kovalev full freedom to refuel after stepping off the primary scale.

That detail matters when evaluating Canelo stepping up two divisions to topple an established champion. While the 185-pound rule looked balanced on paper, flat limits rarely demand equal sacrifice from competitors carrying naturally different frames.

Canelo commanded immense leverage at the negotiating table. A standard challenger could never extract such a concession from a reigning light heavyweight king. His massive box-office draw unlocked clauses designed to soften the exact size deficit observers praised him for facing.

Canelo-Kovalev Win Deserves Roger Maris Treatment

Major League Baseball established a precedent for documenting altered competitive environments. Roger Maris never received a literal asterisk for his 61 home runs in 1961, yet record-keepers tracked his 162-game campaign separately from Babe Ruth’s 154-game run until 1991. The basic lesson holds: record books can preserve the outcome while noting the specific boundaries surrounding it.

A clean entry beside Canelo’s win could state: “Contractual 185-pound morning weigh-in cap.” That simple line flags a verified contractual stipulation without trying to calculate its physical toll on Kovalev.

Nobody needs to argue that Kovalev would have retained his belt without that restriction. Kovalev still had time to gain additional pounds before walking to the ring. The key point rests on the concession itself: Canelo secured an advantage through negotiations, so that detail belongs in the public record.

Critics who scrutinize other champions for imposing rehydration rules ought to use that identical metric here. Canelo closed the show between the ropes, but business clout helped set the ring conditions beforehand. The final ledger should reflect both realities.

Sports.title: George Groves Questions Ben Whittaker’s Knockout Power
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s recent knockouts built an image that Conor Wallace put under pressure on Saturday. Against an opponent who kept answering, the 29-year-old Olympic silver medalist could no longer rely on speed and clean punches to control the exchanges.

Whittaker won a unanimous decision in Birmingham and secured the IBF mandatory position for Dmitry Bivol. His desperate final round nevertheless raised questions about how much his earlier stoppages had demonstrated.

“The knockout wins of late – are they a tiny bit generous in what they now spell? Maybe he’s not the murderous puncher that the record suggests,” George Groves said on his YouTube channel.

Matchroom and Boxxer before them repeatedly placed Whittaker in showcase fights. Those bouts gave him opportunities to display his movement and finishing punches, but offered limited preparation for sustained resistance. At 29, with extensive amateur experience, he needed a more demanding progression.

Braian Nahuel Suarez had lost three of his previous six fights. Richard Rivera arrived after roughly 17 months out, with his two most recent victories coming against Roger Guerrero and Devaun Lee. Their records entering those fights were 17–8–1 and 11–11–1, respectively.

The warning had already appeared against Liam Cameron in their first meeting. Before both fighters went over the ropes, Whittaker was struggling with Cameron’s pressure. The fall and injury dominated the aftermath, overshadowing the uncomfortable exchanges that preceded them. Cameron was below world level, yet he had disrupted Whittaker’s control.

Wallace brought that concern back. As Groves observed, he threw alongside Whittaker rather than waiting for the faster fighter to finish and escape. Landing first did not prevent Whittaker from being hit in return.

His upright retreats and reliance on holding became liabilities as Wallace closed the distance. Too little short offense discouraged the Australian from continuing forward, while retreating toward the ropes reduced Whittaker’s room to escape.

That is the developmental cost of repeated showcases: weaknesses can remain unresolved while expectations rise. Whittaker has earned his mandatory position, but Wallace showed how much work remains before a Bivol fight.

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr Faces Smaller Money Beyond Benn
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr’s possible fight with Michael Zerafa presents a funding problem after two lucrative bouts against Conor Benn. Zerafa accuses him of pricing himself out, but matching Eubank’s financial expectations could be difficult for a fight without the same commercial appeal.

A promoter would have to make the numbers work. Without Saudi backing, that means relying on ticket sales, broadcast revenue, sponsorship and any outside funding secured in Australia. A $10 million purse for Eubank would be difficult to justify against Zerafa, however competitive the fight might be.

“We want the Eubank fight. Our teams have been back and forth. I believe I beat him. I believe that love for the sport’s not there anymore. He’s chasing just money fights,” Zerafa told iFL TV. “I feel like he knows I’m a risk … that’s why he’s pricing himself out a little bit.”

Zerafa’s view of Eubank’s motivation is his own. Waiting for another Benn payday would make financial sense, particularly when Zerafa offers a potentially difficult fight for less money. Eubank could lose and damage the appeal of a trilogy before getting back to the opponent who produced his biggest earning opportunities.

The Australian acknowledges that Benn is competing for the fight, accusing him of trying to prevent their matchup by pursuing a third meeting with Eubank.

Zerafa also claims his team and Matchroom have pursued government support to stage the contest in Melbourne. That suggests they are seeking additional money to meet Eubank’s demands, although Zerafa confirms that official contracts have not been completed. He provides no agreed purse or confirmed funding amount.

Two large paydays can change what a fighter considers an acceptable offer. Eubank may still want to compete, but returning to smaller money against a dangerous opponent is a harder proposition when Benn remains a possibility.

Zerafa can push for the opportunity. Getting Eubank to accept it requires an offer attractive enough to compensate him for risking his next bigger payday.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Pushes Zuffa to Fund Costly Opponents
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson wants Zuffa Boxing to pay for fights against Gary Antuanne Russell or Raymond Muratalla, claiming on X that both want $3 million to face him. That would leave the promoter with a substantial opponent bill before covering its own headliner.

“Gary & Muratalla want 3ms to get in the ring with me.. I would love to fight both them guys tho Zuffa gotta cough that 💰 up!” Shakur wrote on X. “I’m the biggest risk in the sport the Teo fight didn’t do nun but make it worst lol.”

The $3 million figures are Shakur’s account of their demands. His post does not reveal his own purse or establish how close Zuffa is to securing either opponent.

That missing number is significant. If Shakur’s payday exceeds what Russell or Muratalla would receive, Zuffa could face more than $6 million in main-event purses alone. The undercard, production, and other event expenses would increase the cost further.

Neither matchup looks like an obvious pay-per-view seller. Russell and Muratalla offer credible opposition, but neither has established himself as a major commercial attraction. Shakur has yet to demonstrate that he can consistently generate the paying audience needed to make purses at that level profitable.

The sporting appeal is easier to explain. Either opponent would give Shakur a meaningful fight at light welterweight and give Zuffa something substantial to promote. Turning that quality into enough revenue to cover the bill is the harder task.

Zuffa could still justify the expense through subscriptions, audience growth, and establishing Shakur as a regular headliner. An individual event does not necessarily have to turn a profit to serve those goals.

Even so, willingness to spend heavily does not make every asking price worthwhile. Shakur has publicly identified two opponents he would accept. Now Zuffa must decide whether the business either fight could generate supports the money required to deliver it.

Sports.title: Four Perfect Boxing Records Leave Unanswered Questions
Sports.content:
Rocky Marciano, Floyd Mayweather Jr., Joe Calzaghe and Terence Crawford each reached retirement with at least 40 professional victories and no losses or draws. Those records deserve recognition, but they cannot answer what would have happened against the dangerous opponents each left unfought.

An unbeaten record reflects completed fights. Retirement closes the book before another challenger can change it. The question is how much the zero tells us when assessing these four champions.

Rocky Marciano: 49-0, 43 Knockouts

Marciano won the heavyweight championship by knocking out Jersey Joe Walcott in the 13th round in September 1952. He made six successful defenses before retiring in 1956, including victories over Walcott, Roland LaStarza, Ezzard Charles and Archie Moore.

Floyd Patterson subsequently won the vacant championship, while Sonny Liston developed into the division’s most destructive challenger. Patterson’s speed and combinations would have presented a different test for Marciano. Liston’s jab, reach, and power make him an especially difficult hypothetical opponent.

The timing needs qualification. Liston was still an inexperienced professional and was inactive when Marciano retired. Marciano would have needed to extend his career for several years to face the Liston who later dominated the division. That remains an unanswered matchup, rather than evidence that Marciano avoided an established challenger.

Floyd Mayweather Jr.: 50-0, 27 Knockouts

Mayweather’s five-division championship career included immediate rematches against Jose Luis Castillo and Marcos Maidana, two opponents who troubled him in their first meetings. Those return victories strengthened his unbeaten record.

However, Keith Thurman remained an unanswered welterweight test when Mayweather stepped away from conventional championship boxing. Crawford and Errol Spence also became formidable champions, although their strongest claims emerged later. Facing them would have required Mayweather to continue competing against the next generation as he aged.

Instead, his 50th victory came against Conor McGregor, a UFC champion making his professional boxing debut. It extended the number beyond Marciano’s famous 49-0, but offered less evidence about Mayweather’s ability to beat the leading active boxers. His subsequent announcement of a professional comeback also complicates describing his retirement as final.

Joe Calzaghe: 46-0, 32 Knockouts

Calzaghe made 21 successful defenses of his WBO super middleweight title and defeated Jeff Lacy, Mikkel Kessler, Bernard Hopkins and Roy Jones Jr. before retiring in February 2009.

Carl Froch and Chad Dawson were younger opponents who could have tested him further. Froch offered durability, pressure and a willingness to sustain a physical fight. Dawson presented a different challenge through his size, southpaw stance, and boxing ability at light heavyweight.

Calzaghe had already achieved enough to justify retirement. Nevertheless, beating Hopkins and Jones did not settle how he would have handled those younger challengers. His perfect record leaves that debate open.

Terence Crawford: 42-0, 31 Knockouts

Crawford’s unanimous decision victory over Canelo Alvarez in September 2025 completed a remarkable climb through five championship divisions. He announced retirement that December after becoming undisputed champion in three weight classes.

Yet Christian Mbilli, Osleys Iglesias, Lester Martinez and Hamzah Sheeraz offered further potential tests at super middleweight. Jaron Ennis remained another compelling possibility, subject to an agreement on weight.

Those opponents would have asked different questions. Sustained pressure, punching power, size, and youth could have forced Crawford into fights unlike the one he won against Canelo. None was guaranteed to beat him, but defeating one champion did not establish that he would defeat every challenger around that division.

All four fighters earned their perfect records. The limitation comes when those records are treated as proof of invincibility. Retirement preserved the zero while leaving difficult fights unresolved, and those unanswered tests belong in any assessment of their careers.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Sr. Questions Chicago’s Title Fight Weight Restriction
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield Sr. is questioning how his son’s team allowed Kid Austin to approach his Chicago title fight against Lucas Bahdi without explaining Illinois’ 10-pound weight restriction. He claims the fighter discovered the requirement online himself rather than hearing it from the people handling his career.

“My whole team, nobody said, ‘Yo, listen.’ It wasn’t in the contract. Nothing. So to me, you know, it’s like, ‘All right, cool. I understand the playing field now.’ You know, luckily Kid went online yesterday, and he found out himself,” Schofield Sr. said to MillCity Boxing.

Illinois’ boxing rules limit contestants in title bouts to gaining no more than 10 pounds above their official weight by the fight-day weight check. A fighter recording 135 pounds would therefore have a 145-pound limit at that check. This is a state requirement that applies to both contestants.

Sr. argues that Chicago was a questionable choice for a large lightweight, particularly when neither fighter has an established following there, in his view. He also claims Oscar De La Hoya’s side told him they were unaware of the restriction.

The strongest complaint is the alleged failure to communicate. A second weight requirement affects how a fighter plans his recovery after making the lightweight limit. Discovering it late creates an avoidable complication during the final preparations, even if the team can comfortably meet it.

However, Sr.’s suggestion that the location was deliberately selected to disadvantage his son is unsupported by evidence in the interview. The restriction itself does not establish that anyone targeted Kid Austin.

Sr. also insists the limit will have no effect, claiming his son is already 146 pounds, fully hydrated, and completing 15 rounds in training. That makes this primarily a dispute over preparation and trust.

If Kid Austin is as close to the required weight as his father claims, the team can manage the restriction. What Sr. wants explained is why his son had to discover it himself.

Sports.title: Jermall Charlo Targets Jaime Munguia for Houston Fight
Sports.content:
Jermall Charlo wants Jaime Munguia in Houston as he pursues a world title at super middleweight. The matchup gives Charlo a recognizable opponent with an attacking style that would test whether his confidence at 168 is backed by enough remaining ability to contend.

“The fight with [Munguia] makes the most sense,” Charlo said to Fight Hub TV. “I’d love to fight him right here in Houston. Mexican crowd, sold out.”

Charlo also floated appearing on a Canelo Alvarez card in Mexico, although he gave no indication that negotiations with Munguia have begun. Houston is his preferred location, and the appeal is straightforward: a hometown appearance against a popular Mexican fighter offers a bigger occasion than another routine comeback bout.

The harder question is what Charlo would have to produce once the punches start flying. Munguia’s willingness to exchange would give him opportunities to land his jab and right hand, but it would also demand sustained work. Charlo could not count on controlling the fight through isolated bursts if Munguia kept pressing and throwing combinations.

That makes this a useful test of Charlo’s stated ambition. He insists he feels stronger and mentally focused, but a busy opponent would require him to demonstrate those qualities across rounds. Looking sharp early would only be part of the job; maintaining his timing and output as the pressure builds would be more revealing.

Charlo clarified that his description of a “last run” refers to pursuing another world title, rather than announcing that retirement is approaching. He wants to become a champion in a third division and has no intention of moving to light heavyweight.

A Munguia fight fits that goal, provided Charlo can earn it with his performances. Winning would strengthen his case for a title opportunity at 168. Merely securing the Houston date would deliver the occasion he wants, while leaving the toughest part of his comeback to be settled in the ring.

Charlo’s prolonged inactivity makes his championship talk impossible to take seriously. At 36, he crawls back from a 17-month layoff following his May 2025 mismatch against Thomas LaManna. That blowout was supposed to launch a real schedule, yet he immediately went missing again. Managing three fights since 2021 tells fans everything about his reliability against live contenders at super middleweight.

Munguia demands more than empty talk about feeling rejuvenated. Relentless pressure and combination punching will expose whether Charlo possesses the engine to survive deep water after wasting prime years on the sofa. Title dreams require round-by-round ring work, not endless vacations between appearances.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s Rabiu Alhassan joins board of International Fact-Checking Network, IFCN
Ghana News.content:
Founding Executive Director of FactSpace West Africa, Rabiu Alhassan.

The Founding Executive Director of FactSpace West Africa, Rabiu Alhassan, has been elected to the board of the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN), effective October 1.

The IFCN at the Poynter Institute in the USA connects more than 170 fact-checking organisations worldwide to promote high standards, accountability in journalism and information integrity initiatives.

“I hope to promote equitable partnerships in the face of major power imbalances in the information integrity ecosystem, highlight the severe lack of local-language AI moderation tools, particularly in this part of the world and help build sustained public trust in fact-checking,” Rabiu Alhassan stated in an interview.

For a 3-year term, he will be representing Africa on the advisory board, which is expected to guide the IFCN through a time of uncertainty, innovation, and renewal, and will vote on all significant matters of IFCN direction, including approving verified member applications and renewals.

As part of the exhaustive, multi-round voting process, there were regional and all-signatories global votes to determine candidates who had majority support (50%+1) of the voting community.

Despite two available board seats for Africa, Alhassan emerged as the only finalist who cleared the 50%+1 threshold after the first round of voting in a contest that involved five other candidates - the IFCN will be expected to organise another election for the one extra Africa seat in 2027.

Other newly elected board members include Ritu Kapur representing South Asia, Masato Kajimoto representing Asia Pacific, Europe will be represented by Thanos Sitistas. Latin America has two representatives, Daniel Bramatti and

Olivia Sohr, Aws al-Saadi will be representing the MENA region, and Lori Robertson will be representing North America.

Rabiu Alhassan’s board seat win is a testament to his continued contribution to the global fact-checking community, which has involved serving on several IFCN working groups over the years that have resulted in important outputs for global fact-checking efforts, including the IFCN Anti-Harassment Working Group, IFCN YouTube Working Group, and the IFCN Financial Sustainability Working Group.

On the African continent, he has led FactSpace West Africa to become a recognisable contributor to the information integrity ecosystem, providing mentorship and training to several organisations and journalists, which culminated in the co-hosting of the 2024 Africa Facts Summit, the Africa Check-led annual Fact-Checking Conference in Accra, Ghana.

Rabiu Alhassan is a journalist and media entrepreneur with 17 years of experience working across media channels – television, radio, print and digital platforms.

After launching FactSpace West Africa in 2019 and guiding the organisation to become a signatory to the IFCN code of principles, which is the gold standard in fact-checking, he has invested in media innovation and the design of products at the intersection of technology and journalism, with a focus on information disorder.

FactSpace West Africa has footprints in Nigeria, Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and The Gambia, contributing to localised efforts to tackle digital threats and the weaponisation of disinformation in the subregion.

Alhassan holds an Erasmus Mundus master’s degree in Journalism, Media and Globalisation, specialising in Business and Finance from City St. George’s University of London (UK) and Aarhus University (Denmark).

Ghana News.title: Argentina hit 7 as Burkina Faso land five hours before kick-off
Ghana News.content:
Alvarez was one of the goal scorers

Argentina produced a devastating display to thrash Burkina Faso 7-0 in a friendly overshadowed by problems surrounding the visitors' trip to Buenos Aires.

The African team arrived in Argentina just five hours before kick-off after a private flight from Morocco was cancelled because of a "technical failure".

Match organisers said several of Burkina Faso's senior players then refused to travel, citing fatigue, which meant they fielded a young, inexperienced team at Estadio Monumental shortly after an 11-hour flight.

Lautaro Martinez, Gianluca Prestianni, Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez, Franco Mastantuono, and Giuliano Simeone were all on the scoresheet for the hosts, while Moumoune Diallo netted an own goal.

"What the Burkina Faso national team has done is truly commendable; it elevates football," Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni said.

"We try to respect them and are very grateful that they were able to come."

In a press release by match organisers, FIFA match agent Jairo Pachon said: "We would like to emphasise the commitment and dedication of the Burkina Faso federation and government.

"Faced with an extraordinary situation, they worked to provide a solution that would allow their country's representation to be maintained and give the footballers an important sporting opportunity."

'It will be an unforgettable day' - Argentina prepare for Messi farewell

Argentina's talisman Lionel Messi did not feature against Burkina Faso, as he prepares for Tuesday's friendly against Benin, which will mark the end of his 21-year international career.

Messi announced his retirement from Argentina duty in August, following his country's defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final and after saying he was considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge.

The 39-year-old, who captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances, making him the country's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.

"I imagine Tuesday's match will be very emotional for everyone, including Leo," Scaloni said.

"It will be an unforgettable day. It will be his day, and his teammates' day, who also gave him his greatest footballing joy. I'm grateful to be able to enjoy it."

"I imagine that if there were five Monumental stadiums, they would be packed."

Ghana News.title: NPP’s choice of Kojo Bamba, is a rejection of ‘suit and big English’ – Mustapha Gbande
Ghana News.content:
The election of Kwadwo Fosu Boadu, popularly known as Kojo Bamba, as First Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) reflects the grassroots’ rejection of what the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Deputy General Secretary in charge of Operations, Mustapha Gbande, describes as “suit and big English” politics.

Kojo Bamba was elected First Vice Chairman of the NPP after topping the party’s Vice Chairmanship contest with 3, 116 votes.

Mr Gbande said the outcome of the NPP’s recent national executive elections demonstrates the preference of the party’s grassroots for leaders with strong connections to the base.

Speaking on JoyNews' The Pulse, he described Bamba’s election as a reward for his grassroots activities, while arguing that the outcome also sends a message about the kind of leadership NPP delegates want.

“The NPP has chosen a Delta Force commander over all of this. For a grassroots NPP person, it’s a reward. It’s a message to their desire for security and their disapproval of all this suit and big English,” he said.

Mr Gbande further argued that the rejection of some former government appointees in the elections showed that NPP delegates were unwilling to accept attempts to blame party executives for the party’s electoral defeat.

He said the development should also serve as a lesson to the NDC, warning that individuals who preside over a party’s defeat should not return to seek leadership while shifting responsibility to party officials who had raised concerns.

Mr Gbande, however, raised concerns about Bamba’s election because of his reported association with the NPP’s Delta Force, arguing that the development could raise questions about the party’s position on political vigilantism.

“If we are talking about invisible forces, it’s no longer about party; it’s about Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, isn’t it? Because of the election of Bamba,” he said.

He added that if the issue was previously discussed in terms of groups or individuals associated with political vigilantism, Bamba’s election to a strategic party position could change the nature of the discussion.

Mr Gbande acknowledged that the election of individuals with histories of association with political groups does not automatically mean a political party is endorsing violence, citing the NDC’s own history of political actors associated with groups such as the Azorka Boys.

He nevertheless urged the NPP to consider the implications of the choices made in its latest national executive elections.

Ghana News.title: Innovators urged to build low-cost, locally maintainable health solutions
Ghana News.content:
A group picture of speakers and some participants

The Ghana Medical Innovation Expo 2026 has ended with a call for Ghanaian innovators to design low-cost medical equipment together with health workers, from the drawing board, so that devices meet local needs and can be maintained by local engineers.

The Director of the Institutional Care Division of the Ghana Health Service (GHS), Dr Lawrence Ofori Boadu, made the call at the Medical Innovation Expo 2026.

Organised by Academic City University in partnership with Northeastern University, USA and the 4GBI (For Ghana Biomedical Innovation), the three-day expo was themed "Beyond the No-Bed Syndrome". It brought together policymakers, health professionals, researchers, engineers and innovators.

Bed management system

In a speech read on behalf of the Director-General of the GHS, Dr Boadu said the Service was implementing an integrated bed management and referral coordination system to give ambulance crews real-time information on available beds and the capacity of health facilities to provide the required care.

He said Ghana had about one hospital bed per 1,000 people, against the World Health Organisation (WHO) recommendation of five, adding that increasing the number of beds alone would not solve the problem.

What was needed, he said, was a coordinated system that enabled patients to reach the right facility, with the appropriate equipment and skilled professionals, at the right time.

He cited the case of a 29-year-old engineer who was knocked down at the Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra on September 5 last year. Although an ambulance reached him within minutes, he was taken from one hospital to another and died without being admitted.

A committee set up to investigate the death found a "chain of delays", including inadequate stabilisation and poor coordination among health facilities.

Dr Boadu said the GHS had directed health facilities to stabilise emergency patients rather than turn them away, while thousands of health workers had been trained in basic life support.

Bed tracking software has also been piloted at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, Greater Accra Regional Hospital and Tema General Hospital, while bed management bureaus have been established in 10 regions.

He said these initiatives were being integrated into a system that would give ambulance crews a dispatch console, referral coordination and a live view of available beds across the country.

Local solutions

Dr Boadu said the Bed Management Bureau would provide real-time information on bed availability, particularly at regional and teaching hospitals, to help ambulance teams decide where to send patients.

He stressed that the challenge went beyond physical beds.

"It's not just a matter of beds, but again, with the skill, because when patients need care, it's not about the physical bed, but it's about the skill and then the equipment to manage that patient," he said.

Dr Boadu said the GHS was also working towards establishing a National Teleconsultation Centre to provide expert advice to lower-level facilities and reduce unnecessary referrals to major hospitals.

He added that some imported equipment was difficult to maintain because the technology was beyond the capabilities of local clinical engineers.

Innovation

The Senior Research and Development Director of External Innovation at Johnson & Johnson MedTech, Dr Ibrahim Badejo, said innovation should start with unmet clinical needs and aim to solve real healthcare problems rather than simply producing sophisticated technology.

According to him, the measure of innovation was its impact on patients and communities.

Dr Badejo said Ghana could become an innovation hub if it developed solutions to local challenges and scaled them globally, adding that innovations should improve clinical outcomes, affordability and access, since solutions that patients could not afford or reach would have limited impact.

He urged innovators to identify unmet needs, build multidisciplinary teams, validate their ideas early and work with hospitals, industry and government to scale successful solutions.

Expo history

The Vice-President of Academic Affairs at Academic City University, Dr Sena Agbodjah, said the BioInnovation Centre was established through a partnership involving Academic City, Northeastern University and Ghana BioInnovation, with a mandate to develop medical innovations to improve healthcare delivery.

She said the annual expo brought together academia, industry, regulators and innovators to share their work and identify gaps that could guide future innovation. The first edition, held in October 2025 on the theme "New Paradigms in Healthcare Technology", drew more than 200 participants.

Dr Agbodjah said this year's theme was chosen because the "no-bed syndrome" was a systemic challenge requiring solutions beyond simply increasing the number of hospital beds.

Ghana News.title: Frank Appiah Kusi, PhD: Governance Gaps, Transparency, and the Business of Football in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
Football in Ghana is more than sports; it is a cultural institution and a national asset that unites communities, drives national pride, offers economic opportunities, and has social power. Yet, despite its significance, the governance of football in Ghana remains fraught with challenges. The Ghana Football Association (GFA), often at the centre of reform debates, has faced criticism for poor accountability, weak financial transparency, and declining performance of the national teams. The recent crunch meeting between the Ministry of Sports and Recreation and the GFA was hailed as a turning point, but reforms targeted only coaching, leaving behind youth football development, women football, fan trust, infrastructure and governance. More so, the exclusion of the National Sports Authority (NSA)—the statutory body mandated to oversee all sport in Ghana—raises critical questions about transparency and the business of football. This editorial explores the governance gaps in Ghanaian football, examines how transparency affects sponsorship and commercialisation, and draws lessons from African and European best practices to propose a path forward.

The governance of football in Ghana is characterised by overlapping mandates, weak accountability structures, unilateral decision-makers, and orchestrated nuances. The NSA, empowered under the Sports Act, 2016 (Act 934), is mandated to supervise and coordinate all sporting disciplines (Sports Act, 2016). Its exclusion from the recent reform dialogue undermines its statutory role and creates opacity in football governance. Sponsors and investors thrive on accountability, yet the absence of the NSA weakens oversight and leaves the Ministry and GFA to operate in a bilateral arrangement that lacks independent checks (Akpalu, 2026). This governance gap is compounded by the GFA’s reliance on government bailouts while simultaneously claiming autonomy under FIFA statutes. Such contradictions create tension between national laws and international football regulations. The result is a fragmented governance system where accountability is diluted and transparency is compromised. Without clear oversight, sponsorship deals risk being negotiated in opaque corridors, leaving room for favouritism and mismanagement.

Transparency is the cornerstone of football business. Sponsors, whether local or international, demand clarity in financial management and accountability in the use of funds. In Ghana, however, sponsorship structures remain opaque. Betting companies dominate football sponsorship, while major corporate brands such as telecoms, banks, and consumer goods firms remain hesitant to commit due to weak financial disclosure and lack of independent audits (Quansah, 2026). This narrow sponsorship base erodes investor confidence and diminishes fan trust. Fans question whether sponsorship revenues are being used to strengthen grassroots football, build and maintain infrastructure, cushion women football or simply to sustain short-term fixes. The lack of transparency also stifles innovation in football commercialisation, limiting opportunities for broadcasting rights, merchandising, and stadium development. As Ghana seeks to rebuild its football ecosystem, transparency must be prioritised to attract diverse sponsors and restore credibility.

The exclusion of the NSA from football governance creates three major risks. First, it exposes sponsors to reputational damage, as they risk being associated with corruption or mismanagement. Second, it narrows the sponsorship base, leaving betting companies as the dominant funders while other industries avoid opaque structures. Third, it erodes fan trust, reducing merchandise sales, stadium attendance, and overall engagement with the sport. These risks are not merely theoretical; they have practical implications for the sustainability of football in Ghana. Without transparency, football cannot attract long-term investment, and without investment, the sport cannot develop the infrastructure and talent needed to compete internationally. Nigeria, even though presents with its own ups and downs, offers valuable lessons in football governance. The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has emphasised corporate governance codes and independent auditing of sponsorship revenues. By partnering with private auditors, the NFF has reassured sponsors and attracted diverse investments from telecoms, banks, and consumer brands (Ogunleye, 2025). This model demonstrates that transparency and accountability can unlock corporate confidence and expand the sponsorship base; however, corruption erodes this practice.

South Africa’s Premier Soccer League (PSL) is widely regarded as a model of commercialisation in Africa. The PSL operates with transparent broadcasting contracts, diversified sponsorships across industries, and strong fan engagement strategies. This has made the PSL one of the most profitable leagues on the continent (Ndlovu, 2024). Ghana can learn from South Africa’s emphasis on transparency in broadcasting and diversification of sponsors, which ensures financial sustainability and fan loyalty. The English Premier League thrives on independent governance structures and financial fair play regulations. Sponsorship deals are publicly disclosed, and clubs are subject to strict auditing. This transparency attracts global brands such as Emirates, Nike, and Barclays, making the Premier League one of the most commercially successful leagues in the world (UEFA, 2025). Ghana can adopt similar disclosure practices to reassure sponsors and attract international investment.

Furthermore, Germany’s Bundesliga emphasizes fan ownership through the 50+1 rule, which ensures community accountability. Clubs are required to maintain financial transparency, and sponsorships are diversified across industries. This model balances commercial success with fan trust, demonstrating that transparency and community engagement can coexist with profitability (Müller, 2025). Ghana can draw inspiration from Germany’s emphasis on fan engagement and accountability to rebuild trust in its football ecosystem. The experiences of Nigeria, South Africa, England, and Germany highlight the importance of transparency, accountability, and diversification in football governance. Nigeria’s independent audits build corporate confidence, South Africa’s transparent broadcasting expands revenue streams, England’s financial fair play ensures accountability, and Germany’s fan ownership restores public trust. Together, these best practices offer a roadmap for Ghana to reform its football governance and attract sustainable sponsorship.

To address governance gaps and restore transparency, Ghana must adopt a multi-pronged strategy. First, a tripartite governance model should be institutionalised, where the Ministry of Sports and Recreation, NSA, and GFA come together. The NSA should be allowed to institute a committee of experts in collaboration with GFA and other sectors of relevance in national coach assignment. The old mantra of the Ministry working directly with GFA should cease. NSA should be empowered with strong leadership at the Director General appointment with someone who understands the tenets of sport management and the changing dynamics of sport business. In doing so, the influence of the Ministry on NSA should also cease to enable the latter function by law serving as oversight responsibility of sport federations in Ghana. This mandate should have the backing and support of the Ministry of Sports and Recreation and Parliamentary Select Committee on Sport – as policy makers of sport in Ghana. This would restore accountability and ensure that no single entity or federation dominates decision-making. Second, independent audits must be mandated, with annual forensic audits conducted by credible and trusted firms to reassure sponsors. Third, a transparency rule should be established between the NSA, GFA and clubs to publish sponsorship agreements and financial reports online, allowing fans and investors to track the use of funds. Fourth, Ghana must diversify its sponsorship base, attracting telecoms, fintech, and consumer brands by guaranteeing accountability. Finally, fan engagement must be prioritised, adopting Bundesliga-style community accountability to rebuild trust and loyalty.

Football is more than a game; it is a national asset with economic, cultural, and social significance. To protect that asset, Ghana must harmonise its sports laws with FIFA statutes, empower the NSA to fulfil its mandate, and embed transparency into football business. By learning from Nigeria, South Africa, England, and Germany, Ghana can transform football into a sustainable industry that attracts sponsorship, strengthens grassroots development, and restores the Black Stars’ continental reputation. Governance gaps and transparency challenges must be addressed not as isolated issues but as integral components of football’s business ecosystem. Only then can Ghanaian football thrive in the modern era.

Reference

Akpalu, A. (2026, October 3). Reclaiming the soul of our game: A structural blueprint for a self-sustaining, accountable Ghana football ecosystem. Modern Ghana.

Quansah, M. (2026, October 3). Beyond Queiroz’s exit: Ghana football needs accountability, reform — not another quick fix. Graphic Online.

Sports Act, 2016 (Act 934). Accra: Government of Ghana.

Ogunleye, T. (2025). Corporate governance and football sponsorship in Nigeria. African Sports Business Journal, 12(3), 45–62.

Ndlovu, S. (2024). Commercialization of football in South Africa: Lessons from the PSL. Journal of African Sport Management, 8(2), 77–95.

UEFA. (2025). Financial fair play regulations and their impact on European football. UEFA Governance Report.

Müller, H. (2025). Fan ownership and transparency in German football. European Journal of Sport Governance, 15(1), 101–118.

Ghana News.title: Manhyia South MP charged with conspiracy, financial loss and money laundering
Ghana News.content:
The Office of the Attorney-General has filed three criminal charges against Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah over alleged financial misconduct in his handling of a legal case involving SIC Life Savings & Loans Company Limited.

The charges, filed at the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division in Accra on October 3, 2026, include conspiracy to commit a crime, intentionally causing financial loss to a public body and money laundering.

According to the charge sheet, the State alleges that Mr Awuah, while acting as a lawyer for SIC Life, conspired with the company’s then Managing Director in 2024 to intentionally dissipate GH¢9.85 million belonging to the company.

The second count alleges that he intentionally caused SIC Life to suffer a financial loss of GH¢9.85 million in the course of a business transaction.

The third count alleges that Mr Awuah transferred GH¢1 million to the then Managing Director of SIC Life, knowing that the money had been acquired through crime and with the purpose of assisting the recipient to evade the legal consequences of an offence.

How the case arose

The facts accompanying the charge sheet state that Mr Awuah is the Senior Partner of Sarkodie Baffour Awuah & Partners, which was engaged by SIC Life in May 2020 to recover a debt of GH¢6.3 million from Equity Savings and Loans Limited.

Under the terms of engagement, SIC Life was to pay the law firm 15% of the principal sum claimed as professional fees, together with 1% for expenses.

In July 2022, the High Court’s Commercial Division entered summary judgment in favour of SIC Life against Equity in the sum of GH¢10.86 million.

A 31.93-acre parcel of land belonging to Equity at Adamorobe, Oyibi, was subsequently attached in December 2023 in execution of the judgment.

The facts state that a revised judgment dated May 28, 2024, increased the judgment debt to GH¢14.85 million, including interest and costs. The land had a reserve price of GH¢25 million.

The State alleges that while the property was under attachment, Equity purportedly sold it to Eco Swiss Investment Limited on March 14, 2024, for GH¢21.76 million.

Investigators, according to the charge sheet, found that Eco Swiss had not been incorporated at the time it purportedly acquired the property.

The State further alleges that Mr Awuah was instrumental in arranging the transaction.

The settlement

By July 2024, Eco Swiss had paid only GH¢5 million of the purchase price and had filed a notice challenging the attachment, causing the auction to stall.

On July 18, 2024, SIC Life, Equity and Eco Swiss entered into Terms of Settlement under which SIC Life agreed to accept GH¢5 million from Eco Swiss in full and final settlement of the revised GH¢14.85 million judgment debt.

According to the prosecution's case, the settlement terms also provided for the payment of 15% of the original judgment debt to Mr Awuah and his law firm as legal fees, amounting to GH¢2.2 million.

Eco Swiss was also required to pay GH¢1 million in auctioneer’s fees.

The State alleges that the Managing Director of SIC Life signed the settlement terms in conspiracy with Mr Awuah and that investigators found no record of prior approval for the arrangement.

Alleged GH¢1m transfer

The charge sheet further states that after receiving the purported legal fees, Mr Awuah issued a cheque for GH¢1 million to the then Managing Director of SIC Life on November 11, 2024.

The prosecution alleges that the amount represented almost half of the purported legal fee paid to the lawyer.

According to the facts, Mr Awuah has not told investigators the purpose of the GH¢1 million transfer.

MP’s detention

Mr Awuah voluntarily surrendered to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) on October 1, 2026, following a High Court warrant issued on September 30.

He spent the night in custody and was expected to be arraigned before a weekend court.

The charge sheet was subsequently filed on October 3, with the MP expected to appear before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division.

Parliament has expressed concern over his continued detention, with Speaker Alban Bagbin calling for restraint and fairness in the exercise of coercive powers.

What next?

Mr Awuah is expected to be arraigned before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division in Accra, where the court will also consider any application for bail.

The allegations contained in the charge sheet are yet to be proven in court. Mr Awuah is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

Ghana News.title: Attorney-General charges Manhyia South MP over alleged GH¢9.85m financial loss
Ghana News.content:
The Office of the Attorney-General has filed three criminal charges against Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah over alleged financial misconduct in his handling of a legal case involving SIC Life Savings & Loans Company Limited.

The charges, filed at the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division in Accra on October 3, 2026, include conspiracy to commit a crime, intentionally causing financial loss to a public body and money laundering.

According to the charge sheet, the State alleges that Mr Awuah, while acting as a lawyer for SIC Life, conspired with the company’s then Managing Director in 2024 to intentionally dissipate GH¢9.85 million belonging to the company.

The second count alleges that he intentionally caused SIC Life to suffer a financial loss of GH¢9.85 million in the course of a business transaction.

The third count alleges that Mr Awuah transferred GH¢1 million to the then Managing Director of SIC Life, knowing that the money had been acquired through crime and with the purpose of assisting the recipient to evade the legal consequences of an offence.

The facts accompanying the charge sheet state that Mr Awuah is the Senior Partner of Sarkodie Baffour Awuah & Partners, which was engaged by SIC Life in May 2020 to recover a debt of GH¢6.3 million from Equity Savings and Loans Limited.

Under the terms of engagement, SIC Life was to pay the law firm 15% of the principal sum claimed as professional fees, together with 1% for expenses.

In July 2022, the High Court’s Commercial Division entered summary judgment in favour of SIC Life against Equity in the sum of GH¢10.86 million.

A 31.93-acre parcel of land belonging to Equity at Adamorobe, Oyibi, was subsequently attached in December 2023 in execution of the judgment.

The facts state that a revised judgment dated May 28, 2024, increased the judgment debt to GH¢14.85 million, including interest and costs. The land had a reserve price of GH¢25 million.

The State alleges that while the property was under attachment, Equity purportedly sold it to Eco Swiss Investment Limited on March 14, 2024, for GH¢21.76 million.

Investigators, according to the charge sheet, found that Eco Swiss had not been incorporated at the time it purportedly acquired the property.

The State further alleges that Mr Awuah was instrumental in arranging the transaction.

By July 2024, Eco Swiss had paid only GH¢5 million of the purchase price and had filed a notice challenging the attachment, causing the auction to stall.

On July 18, 2024, SIC Life, Equity and Eco Swiss entered into Terms of Settlement under which SIC Life agreed to accept GH¢5 million from Eco Swiss in full and final settlement of the revised GH¢14.85 million judgment debt.

According to the prosecution's case, the settlement terms also provided for the payment of 15% of the original judgment debt to Mr Awuah and his law firm as legal fees, amounting to GH¢2.2 million.

Eco Swiss was also required to pay GH¢1 million in auctioneer’s fees.

The State alleges that the Managing Director of SIC Life signed the settlement terms in conspiracy with Mr Awuah and that investigators found no record of prior approval for the arrangement.

Alleged GH¢1m transfer

The charge sheet further states that after receiving the purported legal fees, Mr Awuah issued a cheque for GH¢1 million to the then Managing Director of SIC Life on November 11, 2024.

The prosecution alleges that the amount represented almost half of the purported legal fee paid to the lawyer.

According to the facts, Mr Awuah has not told investigators the purpose of the GH¢1 million transfer.

MP’s detention

Mr Awuah voluntarily surrendered to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) on October 1, 2026, following a High Court warrant issued on September 30.

He spent the night in custody and was expected to be arraigned before a weekend court.

The charge sheet was subsequently filed on October 3, with the MP expected to appear before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division.

Parliament has expressed concern over his continued detention, with Speaker Alban Bagbin calling for restraint and fairness in the exercise of coercive powers.

Mr Awuah is expected to be arraigned before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division in Accra, where the court will also consider any application for bail.

The allegations contained in the charge sheet are yet to be proven in court. Mr Awuah is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

Ghana News.title: Food Security: Buffer Stock CEO calls for more investment in Agri-Tech
Ghana News.content:
The CEO of the National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO), George Abradu-Otoo, has called for increased investment in technology to strengthen food security interventions across Africa.

According to him, greater deployment of technology in agriculture is critical to achieving the continent’s food sufficiency goals.

Mr Abradu-Otoo made the call at a forum on biotechnology, ecosystems and food security during the 2026 International Forum on Industry and Technologies for Humans in Gelendzhik, Russia.

The two-day event, known as BIOPROM 2026, brought together scientists, policymakers, government officials and trade experts to examine the impact of biotechnology on health, science and food security.

Mr Abradu-Otoo identified Artificial Intelligence, drones, climate sensors, and advanced irrigation systems as technologies that could help improve agricultural productivity and strengthen food self-sufficiency.

He also commended the Ghanaian government for strengthening public policy on agriculture through initiatives aimed at stimulating and increasing production, including the Agriculture for Economic Transformation programme.

The forum was opened by Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister, Denis Manturov, who reiterated the government’s commitment to addressing challenges contributing to food insecurity in the region.

Mr Abradu-Otoo subsequently held discussions with Mr Manturov and other Russian government officials on issues related to agriculture, technology and food security.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
