World.title: ICPC, AGF defend blocking family members from visiting detained El-Rufai, seek N1bn rights suit’s dismissal
World.content:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) has urged the Federal High Court in Abuja to dismiss the N1 billion rights enforcement suit filed by detained former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai.

The Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF), also in a separate counter-affidavit, urged the court to dismiss the suit, which has been assigned to Judge Chigozie Onah, arguing that the ICPC is empowered to establish protocols within its facilities to prevent security breaches.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the detained ex-governor instituted the suit against the ICPC, its Chairman, Musa Aliyu, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), and the AGF.

Mr El-Rufai, through his suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1852/2026 and filed by Ubong Akpan on 13 August, sought N1 billion in damages for being prevented from having access to his wife, Aichatou Asabe, and son, Abba El-Rufai, in July this year.

Mr El-Rufai is also pursuing a separate N1 billion fundamental rights suit at the Federal High Court in Abuja over an alleged unlawful invasion of his house by ICPC operatives in Abuja in February.

Mr El-Rufai has been detained by the ICPC for more than seven months since February based on a court order issued in an ongoing corruption proceeding instituted by the ICPC against him in Kaduna.

The former governor, who alleged that his wife and son were denied access to him prayed the court to declare that his fundamental human rights guaranteed under Part IV of the Nigerian constitution remain inviolable and in force notwithstanding his detention by the commission and should be honoured. The suit presents nine prayers in total.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The ICPC, responding in a joint counter-affidavit sworn by John Uche, a chief anti-corruption assistant in its Internal Security Support Unit, described several claims in the affidavit filed in support of Mr El-Rufai’s suit as false.

Mr Uche maintained that Mr El-Rufai was in the lawful custody of the commission by order of the Federal High Court in Kaduna. He said the order was issued in a criminal case marked FHC/KD/73C/2025.

Why family members were denied access to El-Rufai – ICPC

He said on 7 July, in compliance with the court order permitting access to Mr El-Rufai’s physician, the commission facilitated a medical visit to his personal physician accompanied by their officers and his wife, Asabe.

He said shortly after the hospital visit by the doctor and Mr El-Rufai’s wife, the ICPC received reports that the medical visit had turned into a political meeting, breaching its security protocol and demonstrating that the existing access control environment was vulnerable.

Against this development, the commission said it adopted a temporary-access control measure, restricting non-essential access to the ex-governor because unrestricted access presented a continuing risk until the vulnerability was understood and adequately mitigated.

The commission said that as this occurred on 7 July, Mr El-Rufai’s son, Abba, approached Mr Uche at his desk to request a visit to his father.

Mr Uche wrote that he contacted his superior, Henry Hwande, who instructed him to find out the purpose of Abba’s visit.

He said he made the enquiry and was told that it was a regular visit and the information was relayed to his superior who instructed that Abba should wait in the commission’s waiting area.

He said while Abba was waiting, Asabe, Mr El-Rufai’s wife, met him and after conversing with him began raising her voice and demanding that Abba be granted access to his father.

“That my colleague, Miss Titilayo Remi, tried to speak and reason with her to de-escalate the situation but she was uncooperative,” Mr Uche wrote.

Mr Uche said several minutes later, Abba attempted to proceed into the commission’s building, but he quickly stood in his way to prevent both him and Asabe from gaining access.

“That while being focused on preventing him from gaining access, I fell into a ditch where my leg trapped and I called out for help at which point the applicant’s son and Aichatou Asabe continued to make their way towards the building’s entrance, as captured by the CCTV footage.

“That my cry for help attracted the security personnel who then swung into action to prevent the unauthorised entry of the applicant’s son while Aichatou Asabe gained access into the building and headed for the detention area.

“That after he was prevented from gaining entry into the building, the applicant’s son lay in the gutter and repeatedly rubbed his leg against the edge of the gutter.

“That the 1st respondent has Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras installed at various strategic locations within and around its office premises for security and monitoring purposes, which cameras record activities and events occurring with their respective fields of view.”

He added that the contents of the storage system, including the CCTV recordings, remained accurate and were not altered or tampered with during the material period.

Mr Uche said that following a second security breach on 7 July, the ICPC determined that its existing access arrangements were no longer adequate warranting an urgent review.

The officer said during the course of the review, the commission uncovered another security breach involving Asabe.

He said Asabe was allegedly smuggled into the ICPC’s premises on Saturday, 4 July at about 7:35 p.m. after official visiting hours with the connivance of some officers of the commission, who are currently facing disciplinary action.”

He said that based on Asabe’s repeated disregard for access control protocols, the commission determined that her continued access posed a specific security risk.

“As such, her visiting access to the applicant was temporarily suspended pending completion of the security review and implementation of appropriate mitigation measures.”

He said he was informed by Henry Hwande, the head of the Internal Security Support Unit, on 26 August, that:

“On 8 July, Asia Ahmed El-Rufai one of the applicant’s wives wrote requesting audience with the Director of Operations following the incident of 7 Jul 2026.

“Further to the letter, the Director of Operations alongside Mr Henry Hwande met with Asia Ahmed El-Rufai and a counsel by name, Mr Aremu, at the Director Operations office on 9 July.

“One of the issues discussed at the meeting was the denial of access to Aichatou Asabe to which the Director Operations responded that there was an ongoing investigation and Aichatou Asabe was temporarily suspended from accessing the 1st respondent’s premises until same was completed.

“The 1st respondent, having earlier responded to the issue of Aichatou Asabe’s temporary denial of access, did not see the need to respond to the letter of 16 July 2026 as nothing new had come up,” he said.

He said contrary to Mr El-Rufai’s claim, other members of his family, including his son who was refused entry on 7 July, had severally been granted access to visit him bringing meals, medication and other necessary supplies after the 7 July incident.

Mr Uche, who attached a copy of the commission’s visitors log as Exhibit ICPC D to his counter-affidavit, said dismissing the detained ex-governor’s claims would be in the interest of justice.

AGF also counters El-Rufai’s suit

The AGF, in a counter-affidavit sworn on 11 September by Oni Michael, an administrative officer in the civil litigation and public law department of the Federal Ministry of Justice, also denied several of Mr El-Rufai claims.

Mr Michael stated that the AGF had no responsibility to arrest and/or detain any person suspected of committing any crime, including Mr El-Rufai. He added that the AGF does not maintain a detention facility.

“That the alleged infringement of the applicant’s right was not done by the 3rd respondent in any way whatsoever as he is not responsible for the maintenance and control of the 1st and 2nd respondents’ detention facility.”

The officer further stated that the AGF was not part of the alleged events of 7 July and at no time did he deny Mr El-Rufai’s family members access to him.

According to Michael, the order of Judge R.M. Aikawa of the Federal High Court in Kaduna solely directed the ICPC and its chairman to allow the applicant access to his counsel and personal physician.

“That the attached order did not include access to Aichatou Asabe or any other person.

“That the 1st and 2nd respondents are empowered to put in place protocols within their facilities to prevent breach of security,” he said.

The officer submitted that maintenance of serious security protocols at the ICPC’s detention facility is a matter of national security.

Mr Michael stated that Mosunmola Yetunde, ICPC’s lawyer, informed him that the commission, complying with the court order allowed Mr El-Rufai access to his personal physician accompanied by ICPC officers and his wife, Asabe.

“That the medical meeting turned into a political meeting.

“That the 1st respondent adopted a temporary access control measure which resulted in temporarily restricting non-essential access to the applicant due to vulnerability risk.

“That the restriction put in place was to ensure serious security protocol, necessary for the maintenance and control of the 1st respondent’s detention facility.

“That it became necessary flowing from the events of 7 July to review the CCTV Security footage of the 1st respondent’s facility, Mr Michael wrote.

He added that during the course of the review, it was discovered that there had been an earlier security breach involving Asabe.

He said this happened in connivance with an ex-officer of the commission, wherein Asabe was smuggled into the commission’s facilities after official visiting hours.

“That the act of Aichatou Asabe and the ex-officer of the 1st respondent breached the 1st respondent’s security access protocol.

“That the officer found liable in smuggling Aichatou Asabe into the 1st respondent’s detention facility has been dismissed from the service of the 1st and 2nd respondents.

Besides this suit, Mr El-Rufai has a separate N1 billion legal action against the ICPC, the Inspector-General of Police and the AGF over the ICPC-led search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on 19 February.

On 21 September, Judge Joyce Abdulmalik adjourned the case until 27 October for a definite hearing.

Mr El-Rufai faces two separate corruption cases: one before the Federal High Court and the other before the Kaduna State High Court. One of the courts denied him bail and ordered his remand his custody in the ICPC custody pending the conclusion of the trial.

World.title: NNPC revenue plunges by N10.6trn in 2025
World.content:
NNPC Limited recorded a 23.4 per cent decline in group revenue to N34.52 trillion in 2025, from N45.08 trillion recorded in 2024, according to the company’s 2025 audited financial report.

The N10.56 trillion decline was largely driven by a sharp fall in revenue from petroleum products, which dropped by 77.6 per cent, from N9.68 trillion in 2024 to N2.17 trillion in 2025.

This was disclosed in the company’s 2025 audited report published on Wednesday last week. The financial report, which provided a breakdown of NNPC’s revenue by commodity and geographical market, shows that crude oil remained the company’s largest source of revenue, and that earnings from the commodity also declined.

According to the breakdown of the report, NNPC’s revenue from crude oil fell by 13.1 per cent from N29.21 trillion posted in 2024 to N25.39 trillion in 2025.

The decline in crude oil and petroleum products revenue more than offset increased earnings from natural gas and power during the year.

The company’s revenue from natural gas rose by 18.3 per cent, from N5.20 trillion in 2024 to N6.15 trillion in 2025, while power revenue increased by 25.4 per cent, from N9.42 billion to N11.81 billion.

The report said revenue from services declined from N980.46 billion in 2024 to N792.33 billion in 2025, which implies about 19.2 per cent decline.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria remains dominant market

The report also showed that Nigeria accounted for the bulk of NNPC’s group revenue in 2025.

Revenue generated from Nigeria stood at N23.84 trillion, representing about 69 per cent of the group’s total revenue.

Other significant geographical markets included the United Arab Emirates, which contributed about N2.81 trillion; Douglas, Isle of Man, with about N2.26 trillion; Switzerland, with N1.95 trillion; and the British Virgin Islands, with about N711.3 billion.

The geographical breakdown also shows that NNPC generated revenue across several international markets, including Singapore, Spain, Germany, Mauritius, the United Kingdom, the Bahamas, the United States, Ghana, Vietnam and Togo.

Despite the significant decline at group level, the revenue of NNPC Limited as a standalone company remained relatively stable.

The company’s revenue fell by just 1.7 per cent, from N19.66 trillion in 2024 to N19.32 trillion in 2025.

The divergence between the group and company figures reflects the broader contribution of NNPC’s subsidiaries and other group entities to the consolidated results.

The report’s figures show that crude oil remained the backbone of NNPC’s earnings, accounting for about 74 per cent of group revenue in 2025. Natural gas contributed another 17.8 per cent, while petroleum products accounted for about 6.3 per cent.

The figures highlight the continued exposure of NNPC’s revenue base to developments in the crude oil market, while also showing the growing contribution of natural gas to the company’s earnings.

In January, NNPC unveiled its Gas Master Plan (GMP) 2026, aimed at driving industrialisation and strengthening the nation’s energy security.

The company also unveiled the 20 million Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) cylinder supply initiative targeted for delivery by 2030, alongside the NNPC LPG and cylinder supply expansion initiative.

The Gas Master Plan 2026 is an offshoot of the Nigerian Gas Master Plan 2008, a strategic framework designed to maximise economic benefits from Nigeria’s abundant gas resources.

A key feature of the GMP 2026 is its full alignment with the Nigerian Decade of Gas Programme.

It is expected to serve as the definitive framework for coordinated gas sector development, execution discipline and value creation over the next decade.

World.title: 32 people on board crashed Nigerian military aircraft – Aviation Minister
World.content:
There were 32 people on board a military aircraft that crashed in Ondo State on Monday, the Minister of Aviation, Festus Keyamo, said in a post on X.

PREMIUM TIMES reported the crash on Monday morning, with the Nigerian Air Force saying the aircraft was travelling on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos.

In his first official statement on the crash, Mr Keyamo said, “Preliminary information suggests that there were 25 passengers and 7 crew members on board.”

Search and rescue operations are still ongoing, and the casualty figure from the crash has yet to be determined.

Read the minister’s full statement below.

“I regret to inform the general public that Air Traffic Controllers have informed me of the disappearance of a military aircraft with tail number NGR 931, enroute Lagos from Benin at 0913 hours earlier today. All efforts to raise the aircraft on radio proved abortive.

“Subsequently information however confirmed that the military aircraft has crashed close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The wreckage has been located and search and rescue operations are ongoing.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Preliminary information suggests that there were 25 passengers and 7 crew members on board.

Whilst the control and regulation of military aircraft are completely outside the authority of the Ministry of Aviation, and Civil Aviation Authority, I have just spoken to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke and pledged our total cooperation and assistance in the search and rescue efforts ongoing.

Further information on this unfortunate incident will be made available subsequently.

World.title: At Oct 7 memorial, Netanyahu says will be no Hamas rule in Gaza
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks during the state memorial ceremony for the third anniversary of October 7 attack, at Mount Herzl military cemetery in Jerusalem on October 5, 2026. Netanyahu on October 5 vowed there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza as he attended a memorial event marking three years since the militant group’s October 7, 2023 attack. (Photo by DEBBIE HILL / POOL / AFP)





Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday vowed there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza as he attended a memorial event marking three years since the militant group’s October 7, 2023 attack.

Monday is a national day of remembrance for the deadliest day in Israel’s history, with flags lowered to half-mast on public buildings from 6:29 am, the time the attack began.

Speaking during a state ceremony at the Mount Herzl military cemetery in Jerusalem, Netanyahu said “we have achieved enormous accomplishments, but there are still missions ahead of us, and we intend to complete them”.

“There will be no Hamas rule in Gaza,” he added, vowing to continue targeting anyone who was involved in the attack or who held hostages.

In a separate speech later on Monday, Netanyahu said he stood with victims’ families and the nation shared their grief.

“There is no forgiveness for the murderers, the torturers, the arsonists. There is no forgiveness for the destroyers, the looters, the kidnappers,” he said.

Later in the speech, a heckler shouted: “You didn’t protect my son and 1,200 others killed on October 7 — shame!” leading Netanyahu to briefly pause the address.

The Hamas-led attack resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures. Militants also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive that has killed more than 74,200 people in Gaza, according to the territory’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

Since a ceasefire was declared last October, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,440 people in Gaza, according to the ministry.

Plans for Gaza’s post-war governance have begun to take shape, but the issue remains largely unresolved in practice.

Since Hamas’s October 2023 attack, Israel has fought wars on several fronts, including against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon.

During his speech on Monday, Netanyahu also vowed to keep striking Hezbollah to “create an opportunity for peace with a country whose people, for the most part, want peace with us”.

Netanyahu also hit out at the clerical leadership in Iran, where Israel and the United States launched a joint attack on February 28, triggering the Middle East war.

“We will not allow the ayatollah regime in Tehran to threaten our existence,” Netanyahu said, adding the Iranian leadership was “weaker than it has been since its establishment”.

World.title: Ondo crash: Aiyedatiwa mobilises rescue support
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

AKURE — Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has expressed sympathy to the Chief of the Air Staff, the Nigerian Air Force and families of personnel and passengers aboard the aircraft that crashed in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of the state.

The governor also directed the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Ministry of Health and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise logistical and human support for the ongoing search-and-rescue operation.

The Nigerian Air Force confirmed that an ATR-42 aircraft on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos crashed in the Igbokoda area on Monday, October 5. Search-and-rescue operations are ongoing.

In a statement issued by his Chief Press Secretary, Ebenezer Adeniyan, Aiyedatiwa said, “Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time.”

According to the statement, the governor has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Ilaje Local Government Chairman, Hon. Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies on the ground.

The statement read:

“The Governor of Ondo State, His Excellency, Hon. Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa, has received with deep sadness the news of the crash of a Nigerian Air Force aircraft in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, in the early hours of today, Monday, October 5, 2026.

“According to preliminary reports confirmed by the Nigerian Air Force Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the aircraft, an ATR-42 with tail number NGR 931, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed in a swampy area opposite the Naval Base in Igbokoda.

“The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, has confirmed that 25 passengers and seven crew members were on board.

“On behalf of the Government and good people of Ondo State, Governor Aiyedatiwa expresses his heartfelt sympathy to the Chief of Air Staff, the entire Nigerian Air Force family, and the families of all personnel and passengers on board the ill-fated aircraft. Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time.

“The Governor has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Ilaje Local Government Chairman, Hon. Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies on ground.

“To aid ongoing efforts, Governor Aiyedatiwa has directed the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), the Ministry of Health, and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise and offer full logistical and human support to the Nigerian Air Force and other emergency response agencies in the search and rescue operations currently ongoing at the crash site.

“The Governor has also directed that the area be cordoned off and secured to allow for smooth and unhindered rescue operations, while urging residents of Igbokoda and adjoining communities to remain calm, cooperate with emergency responders, and refrain from spreading unverified information.

“The Ondo State Government will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as more information becomes available from the Nigerian Air Force.

“We pray for the safety of our gallant officers and for the success of the rescue efforts.”

As of the latest official reports, authorities had not confirmed the condition of those aboard the aircraft.

World.title: Disgraced former US House Speaker dies at 84
World.content:
Dennis Hastert

Dennis Hastert, the longest-serving Republican speaker of the US House of Representatives whose career ended in disgrace after he admitted sexually abusing teenage boys he had coached, has died aged 84, officials said Monday.

The Kendall County Coroner’s Office in Illinois said Hastert died at his home Saturday night while under hospice care.

Hastert was one of Washington’s most powerful politicians during eight years as House speaker from 1999 to 2007, a position that placed him second in the line of succession to the presidency.

But his reputation collapsed years after he left Congress when a federal investigation into suspicious bank withdrawals exposed payments intended to conceal sexual abuse dating back to his years as a high school wrestling coach.

Hastert pleaded guilty in 2015 to illegally structuring cash withdrawals to avoid bank reporting requirements as part of a $3.5 million agreement with one of his victims.

At his sentencing the following year, Hastert admitted for the first time that he had sexually abused boys while teaching and coaching wrestling at Yorkville High School in Illinois from the 1960s to the early 1980s.

“They looked to me and I took advantage of them,” Hastert said in court.

Prosecutors detailed abuse involving at least five boys, some as young as 14.

He could not be prosecuted for the sexual offenses because the statutes of limitations had expired, and was instead sentenced to 15 months in federal prison for violating banking laws.

US District Judge Thomas Durkin described Hastert at sentencing as a “serial child molester.”

Hastert served in the House from 1987 until 2007 and became speaker after the turbulent departure of fellow Republican Newt Gingrich and the withdrawal of Gingrich’s intended successor, Bob Livingston.

He remained speaker until Democrats regained control of the House in the 2006 midterm elections.

Hastert was released from federal prison in 2017 after serving most of his sentence.

World.title: Aircraft crash: We can only investigate if invited by military – NSIB
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Following the crash of an ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State, the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has offered to provide flight data and cockpit voice recovery and readout support to the Nigerian Air Force.

NSIB, which said investigation of the accident rests with the military authority because it involved a military aircraft, added that its Flight Safety Laboratory could be deployed to assist with the recovery and analysis of flight data and cockpit voice recordings should the Nigerian Air Force formally request its assistance.

A statement signed by NSIB Director General / Chief Executive Officer, Captain Alex Badeh Jr, reads: “NSIB has received reports of an accident involving a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State on 5 October 2026. The Nigerian Air Force has confirmed that the aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred and that search and rescue operations have been activated and are ongoing, in coordination with relevant authorities and emergency response agencies.

“The Bureau extends its sincere condolences to the Nigerian Air Force and to the families and colleagues of all those on board. Our thoughts are with them and with the search and rescue teams working at the site.

“This occurrence involves a military aircraft. In line with the NSIB Establishment Act, 2022, and with established international practice, the investigation of military aviation accidents rests with the military authority. The NSIB does not investigate military accidents unless formally invited to do so by that authority.

“Should the Nigerian Air Force so request, the Bureau stands ready to assist. That assistance can include the deployment of investigators and the use of the Bureau’s Flight Safety Laboratory for flight data and cockpit voice recovery and readout, as well as related technical support. The NSIB commends the swift activation of search and rescue operations and the efforts of first responders at Igbokoda. The public is urged to rely exclusively on official updates from the Nigerian Air Force on the rescue operation and on any investigation.”

World.title: APC women begin 2027 grassroots mobilisation
World.content:
Tinubu pledges support for female candidates

By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja

Women leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) have pledged to mobilise women across the country for the 2027 general elections, urging members to translate the Federal Government’s reform agenda into grassroots action.

The women made the commitment at the one-day Women’s Stakeholders’ Mobilisation and Empowerment Pre-Inaugural Summit 2026, where they also called for stronger networks, greater participation of women in governance and increased access to empowerment opportunities.

The summit brought together APC women leaders from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, members of the National Assembly, ministers, women’s groups and other party supporters.

Speaking at the event, the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, thanked the women for their support for President Bola Tinubu and urged them to return to their respective states to mobilise voters for the party.

She said the campaign would be anchored on the administration’s “Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0: From Reform to Prosperity”, arguing that the government’s economic reforms were beginning to yield results.

“The theme of this year’s rally, the Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0, From Reform to Prosperity, is not just a slogan, it is our reality,” she said.

She listed economic stabilisation, declining inflation, growing foreign reserves, increased investment, support for farmers and access to student loans among the administration’s achievements.

According to her, the APC women’s campaign would not be restricted to the presidential election but would extend to candidates contesting legislative and state-level elections.

“What you see on the ballot box is APC. We are here to promote APC, nothing less, from presidency to partnership, to National Assembly, and also to the state assembly,” she said.

She urged the women to speak with one voice and translate their support into votes during the 2027 elections.

“Let us share the hope that when Nigerian women have spoken, we speak with one voice, and we vote,” she added.

Tinubu also expressed support for female candidates contesting elective positions, saying various women support groups within the party had been brought together to strengthen the campaign structure and improve mobilisation across the country.

She said women leaders would play a key role in coordinating campaigns and representing the national campaign structure at the state level.

“We are going to also have a state campaign, but all these women here will be representing you when you have state parties. We are going to work on that; they will represent you, and then they will speak,” she said.

Also speaking, the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul-Aziz Yari, said women would play a critical role in the 2027 elections, describing them as an important voting bloc.

Yari urged the women to remain united behind the APC, saying the party was working to provide them with the necessary support for effective grassroots mobilisation.

“What we need is one voice, one movement, one choice, and one man. That’s what we need for 2027,” he said.

He expressed confidence in the ability of APC women leaders to mobilise voters across the states, adding that their participation would be crucial to the party’s electoral strategy.

Also speaking, the APC National Women Leader said the summit was an opportunity to strengthen women’s participation in politics and development, stressing that empowered women would contribute significantly to stronger families and communities.

She said women leaders had a responsibility to take government programmes and opportunities to the grassroots, listen to citizens’ concerns and provide feedback to government.

According to her, “our action plan is clear. First, we must build stronger women-to-women networks across our wards, local governments and communities.”

She added that APC women had been mandated to identify people in need of support, connect them with available empowerment opportunities and ensure beneficiaries became agents of development in their communities.

The APC women leader also called for a shift from mobilisation to measurable action, with clear responsibilities, grassroots structures, regular engagement and accountability.

“My dear sisters, the time to organise is now, the time to act is now, and the time to turn the new road into prosperity is now,” she said.

She further pledged the support of APC women for President Bola Tinubu’s administration and his re-election bid in 2027.

The event also highlighted government empowerment initiatives targeting women, elderly citizens, persons with disabilities and young people.

The speakers urged the women to take ownership of such programmes and use them to deepen engagement with communities ahead of the 2027 elections.

The gathering was attended by APC women leaders, First Ladies, political stakeholders and representatives of support groups from different parts of the country.

The women, through chants and solidarity messages at the event, declared their readiness to commence grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Reactions trail continued captivity of NYSC members
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Chidi Nkwopara

OWERRI — Reactions have continued to trail the prolonged captivity of prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) who were kidnapped in Imo State while travelling to orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states.

Chief Raymond Onuekwusi expressed concern over the continued captivity of the young people, saying their families were being subjected to severe emotional distress while the victims themselves could be facing serious difficulties in the hands of their abductors.

He said: “While the families of the abducted youngsters are passing through serious and unimaginable pain, only God knows what the kidnap victims themselves are experiencing in the hands of their abductors.

“Nobody can carelessly rule out psychological trauma, possible abuse and health challenges, as the victims remain in captivity.

“Let us not forget that the only sin of the victims, which we can readily point at, is their willingness to serve their fatherland! I don’t know when this has become a crime.

“However, this ugly incident has brought Imo State again into bad light. It is equally sad that the state government, to the best of my knowledge, is yet to issue any statement on the matter.

“While there is nothing on ground in Imo State to show that such a catastrophic incident took place in the state on our Independence Day, it is most disturbing that our nation’s highways are unsafe.

“Why can’t our governments protect human lives and property in this day and age? Is this not part of the oath our leaders took before going into office?”

When reminded of a recent statement attributed to the state Commissioner of Police, Mr Audu Garba Bosso, that security agencies had identified the location where the abducted corps members were being held, Onuekwusi said the development would only be meaningful if it led to their safe rescue.

“It may be a pleasing development but nothing will be better for us all than rescuing them alive,” he said.

He, however, expressed concern that the disclosure about the location of the victims could compromise security operations.

“My serious fear is that the Imo police boss goofed, by giving out more information than was necessary. From what he gave out, will the criminals not take commensurate action against a possible counter attack?” he asked.

Responding to criticisms levelled against him by Imo journalists, the Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, Mr Henry Okoye, said he took public feedback seriously.

“I take all public feedback seriously. Sometimes, silence simply means I am listening, reflecting, and considering the best way to respond. Please do not mistake my silence for disregard,” Okoye said.

Meanwhile, the State Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Onwuasoanya FCC Jones, said the party and government were committed to securing the release of the abducted prospective corps members.

He said: “The APC administration places great value on the life of every Nigerian and we will not allow non-state actors to threaten the lives of our citizens without serious and immediate response from the government.

“The Commander-in-Chief, in collaboration with the Governor, has released every necessary resource and personnel to ensure that these citizens are safely rescued and the criminals made to face the full wrath of the law for attempting to harass ordinary Nigerians.

“We urge Imolites of all political persuasions to join the APC in prayers for the successful rescue of these innocent citizens, while we also encourage citizens who reside around the communities where these criminals are hiding to be free to provide the security agents with information and communal support required to root out the bad eggs from their hideout and make our communities safe for law-abiding citizens and residents.”

Reacting to the statement, a citizen, Chidi Okoroafor, criticised the APC’s response, describing it as “shoddy” and saying it failed to address what he considered a wider public reaction to the abduction.

He said: “Beyond the shoddy writing, your statement also failed to address a more serious moral failure.

“While fellow Nigerian citizens, including young corps members, were still being held captive by criminals, many people went ahead with Independence Day celebrations as if nothing was wrong.

“Instead of a national mood of disappointment, concern and collective anxiety, we witnessed noise, dancing and festivity. That is not resilience; it is callous indifference.”

World.title: Rivers seals 21 health facilities, arrests three
World.content:
Facilities linked to alleged baby trafficking, racketeering

By Davies Iheamnachor

PORT HARCOURT — The Rivers State Government has sealed 21 health facilities over alleged involvement in baby trafficking and other regulatory violations, with three persons arrested for prosecution.

The crackdown, conducted across four local government areas by the Rivers State Ministry of Health in the third quarter of 2026, included a joint operation with the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) at Manda Clinic and Maternity, Elelenwo.

According to the ministry, a Liberian national reportedly disclosed during the operation that three children had been procured from the facility within one month.

The Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Health, Dr Vincent Wachukwu, disclosed this on Monday during the ministry’s third-quarter press briefing in Port Harcourt.

Wachukwu said the enforcement followed surveillance reports indicating that more than 150 health facilities were operating without registration and regulatory supervision.

He said the 21 facilities sealed comprised eight hospitals, five maternity homes and eight diagnostic centres across Port Harcourt, Obio/Akpor, Ikwerre and Etche Local Government Areas.

According to him, 19 of the facilities were found operating without registration and below the minimum standards set by the ministry, while another registered facility was found operating without a licensed doctor or nurse.

He said: “The Rivers State Ministry of Health is fully committed to its regulatory function and is committed to eradicating quackery from Rivers State as part of our mandate on health security.

“This exercise is a continuation of our anti-quackery mandate to stamp out all unregistered facilities and facilities operated without the minimum standards.”

Wachukwu said Manda Clinic and Maternity, Elelenwo, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area, was operating without registration and had no licensed medical practitioners.

He added that its operators were arrested by NAPTIP following the joint operation, after which the facility was sealed by the ministry.

Other facilities shut include Vasty Clinic, Omoku; Danny Clinic and Daba Clinic in Old Port Harcourt Town; Kambel Hospital, Abara-Etche; Havilla Hospital, Igwuruta; Golden Era Hospital, Igwuruta; and Ola-Oluwa Hospital, Igwuruta.

Wachukwu said Havilla Hospital was an unregistered facility operated by a man identified as Mr Isaac, who claimed to have undergone medical training in Ukraine in 2013 but had no licence from the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN).

He added that Kambel Hospital, Abara-Etche, and Golden Era Hospital, Igwuruta, were shut after inspectors found that neither a licensed doctor nor nurse was operating the facilities.

On Sarah Maternity, Belema Polo, Enugu Waterside, the Permanent Secretary said the facility, operated by a popular social media traditional birth attendant, had a patient load of more than 1,000 women and daily traffic of over 200 women.

He said the ministry used the inspection to establish practice guidelines, supervision and  standards, while the operator was issued an official warning and designated as a contact point for other traditional birth attendants and maternity operators on the need for supervision and training.

Wachukwu said the remaining 16 facilities sealed during the exercise were found to be unregistered and operating below the minimum standards stipulated under the Rivers State Facility Registration Act No. 2 of 2019.

He warned that the ministry would sustain the enforcement campaign and urged residents to patronise only health facilities that meet the state’s regulatory requirements.

He said: “We mandate all registered facilities to display their Certificate of Standards at the reception of their facilities.

“We also mandate individuals and corporate organisations to only access care in facilities with verified Certificates of Standards, as this serves as the quality assurance check for health security.”

World.title: Ondo Plane Crash: Aiyedatiwa Orders Full Support for Rescue Operations, Mourns Victims
World.content:
Fidelis David in Akure

Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has directed the immediate mobilisation of state emergency and health agencies to support the ongoing search and rescue operation following the crash of a Nigerian Air Force aircraft in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of the state.

The aircraft, an ATR-42 with tail number NGR 931, crashed in a swampy area opposite the Naval Base in Igbokoda in the early hours of Monday while on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos, according to preliminary information confirmed by the Nigerian Air Force.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed that 25 passengers and seven crew members were on board the ill-fated aircraft, bringing the total number of persons aboard to 32.

The Nigerian Air Force Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, also confirmed the incident, while search and rescue operations continued at the crash site as of the time of filing this report.

Reacting to the development, Aiyedatiwa expressed deep sadness over the incident, extending his condolences to the Chief of Air Staff, officers and personnel of the Nigerian Air Force, as well as the families of those aboard the aircraft.

The governor said the state stood in solidarity with the affected families at the difficult moment, noting that his thoughts and prayers were with them.

Aiyedatiwa, according to a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Prince Ebenezer Adeniyan, has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Chairman of Ilaje Local Government Area, Hon. Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies deployed to the scene.

To strengthen the emergency response, the governor directed the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Ministry of Health and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise and provide full logistical and human support to the Nigerian Air Force and other agencies involved in the search and rescue operation.

He also ordered that the crash site and its immediate surroundings be cordoned off and adequately secured to ensure that rescue personnel could carry out their operations without hindrance.

The governor urged residents of Igbokoda and neighbouring communities to remain calm, cooperate with emergency responders and avoid spreading unverified information about the incident.

The statement added that the Ondo State Government would continue to monitor developments and provide further updates as more information becomes available from the Nigerian Air Force.

Aiyedatiwa also prayed for the safety of the officers involved in the operation and expressed hope for the success of the ongoing rescue efforts.

World.title: Updated: Military Aircraft Crashes in Ondo, NAF Begins ‘Search and Rescue’ Operation
World.content:
Fidelis David in Akure

A military aircraft has crashed in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State.

The tragic accident occurred on Monday morning in a swampy terrain opposite the Naval Base in Igbokoda, throwing residents of the coastal community into panic.

Although the identity of the plane and the number of personnel on board had yet to be officially confirmed, military gear was reportedly recovered from the crash site.

The Chairman of Ilaje Local Government Area, Mr Maurice Oripelaye, who confirmed the incident in a telephone conversation with journalists, said the aircraft was burnt in the accident.

Oripelaye said, “We have confirmed that a helicopter crashed in the area, but we cannot ascertain the number of people that were on board yet. Military gear was found at the scene, but the helicopter had burnt to rubble.”

However, the Ondo State Police Command through the Police Public Relations Officer, Jimoh Abayomi, later confirmed the incident, urging members of the public, particularly residents of Igbokoda and adjoining communities, to remain calm and refrain from circulating unverified information, assuring that the public would be duly informed as soon as further credible information become available.

Meanwhile, the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) confirmed the incident, saying it had activated an immediate search-and-rescue operation.

In a statement by the Director of Public Relations and Information, NAF Headquarters, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the Air Force said the aircraft involved was an ATR-42 which was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred.

The NAF said, “Search and Rescue operations, in coordination with relevant authorities and emergency response agencies, are currently ongoing,” adding that it remained committed to ensuring the success of the ongoing rescue efforts.

Sources said the crash occurred in a swampy area opposite the Naval Base, while efforts were ongoing to secure the scene and ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Residents and witnesses were said to have gathered around the area as relevant authorities commenced assessment of the crash site.

As of press time, the number of personnel on board and their condition remained unclear, while further details on the cause of the accident and the circumstances surrounding the crash were expected from the authorities.

World.title: Kila Rejects ‘Fake Professor’ Label, Threatens Legal Action
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Prof. Anthony Kila has rejected a Premium Times report describing him as a ‘fake professor’, describing the characterisation as inaccurate, misleading and damaging to his reputation and professional standing.

Kila, who is the Pro-Chancellor of Michael and Cecilia Ibru University, Delta State, and Director of the Commonwealth Institute of Advanced and Professional Studies (CIAPS), made his position known in a statement responding to the publication of October 3, 2026.

“For the avoidance of doubt, I am a professor, and I stand by the title and the professional and academic credentials on which it is based,” he stated.

He argued that the report reflected what he described as an incomplete understanding of the nature, origin and institutional basis of his professorship, insisting that the matter should be assessed on the basis of relevant facts and documentation.

Kila said he would make available the relevant facts and documents concerning his professorial status, stressing that: “The facts and documentation will speak for themselves.”

He took particular exception to the description ‘fake professor’, arguing that it was presented as a factual conclusion requiring evidence and had serious implications for his reputation.

While acknowledging the role of journalism in scrutinising the credentials of individuals occupying positions of responsibility, Kila said such scrutiny should be conducted with fairness and proper understanding of the facts.

He also expressed concern over what he described as the level of attention directed at him, noting that he holds no political office, is not seeking one and is not a government official.

The academic thanked colleagues, friends, students and members of the public who had contacted him following the publication to express confidence in his academic and professional credentials.

Kila further disclosed that he had instructed his lawyers to review the publication and any subsequent dissemination of the allegations and advise on appropriate legal steps to protect his reputation and professional standing.

“The facts and documentation will speak for themselves,” he stated.

World.title: Court Orders INEC to Upload Olawepo-Hashim’s Name as Accord Party’s Presidential Candidate
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

Justice Mohammed Umar of a Federal High Court on Monday ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to upload the name of Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim as the candidate of the Accord Party in the 2027 presidential election.

Justice Umar gave the order shortly after declaring that Olawepo-Hashim was lawfully nominated as presidential candidate of the party.

Olawepo-Hashim had approached the Federal High Court, Abuja, for an order compelling the Accord Party to recognize him as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election.

The plaintiff also sought another order directing the party to also forward his name to INEC as its standard-bearer in the forthcoming general election.

Delivering judgment in the suit on Monday, Justice Umar agreed with the plaintiff that the primary election that produced him was lawfully conducted, adding that the purported cancellation of the primary having not been communicated was of no moment.

The court subsequently held that the plaintiff lawfully emerged as the candidate of the Accord Party and his name should be immediately uploaded by the electoral umpire.

Details later…

World.title: Ogun PDP Deputy Guber Candidate, Sowunmi-Kolapo, Fetes Retired Traffic Warden
World.content:
*Says Adebutu’s govt’ll prioritise workers’ welfare

The Deputy Governorship Candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia ‘Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has held a grand retirement reception in honour of a retired Deputy Superintendent of Traffic, DST Anifat Abiodun Bello, describing her “infectious commitment to duty,” as rare and worthy of emulation.

At the dinner, held in Obantoko, Abeokuta, Sowunmi-Kolapo commended the retired traffic warden, popularly known as Aunty Anifat, for her professionalism, discipline, resilience and dedication to traffic management during her years of service with the Ogun State Police Command.

The PDP deputy governorship candidate said the honour was the beginning of greater things to happen in the retired officer’s life, urging other security agents and indeed, all workers, to emulate Bello’s outstanding service to the Nigeria Police Force.

“You are a role model for younger Nigerians. I want to commend you for your professionalism. Gold or silver, I do not have. But please accept this as a token of appreciation for your infectious commitment to duty. It is the beginning of greater things to come for you,” she told the retired traffic officer while presenting a cheque of N500,000 to her.

She assured workers in Ogun State of rewarding welfare packages once the government of Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, the PDP governorship candidate, comes on board next year, declaring that “hardwork will pay.”

“I want to assure our people in Ogun State that hardwork will pay and our civil servants will always smile home. When we come on board, the suffering they have put us through in Ogun for the past eight years will be a thing of the past,” the Deputy Governorship Candidate promised.

Other dignitaries at the reception ceremony, including the wife of the Ogun governorship candidate, Yeye Adenike Adebutu; Ogun PDP Chairman, Dr Abayomi Tella; leaders of the party at various levels, and religious leaders in Egbaland, among others, paid glowing tributes in appreciation of Mrs Bello’s diligent service.

Adebutu’s wife, while showering more encomiums on the retired officer, announced another N500,000 cash support for her, saying she would be part of the Adebutu administration once he is voted into power in 2027.

“I want to congratulate you, I see you all the time while performing your traffic duty, ever smiling. One day, I was passing and I asked myself, how does this woman manage to smile always. You will be part of Adebutu’s government.

“I want to thank our deputy governor (Sowunmi-Kolapo) for putting this reception ceremony together. Many people know you and they see what you do. God will continue to honour you. I thank you for your selfless service to Ogun,” Mrs Adebutu said.

Also speaking, Ogun PDP Chairman, Abayomi Tella, said Mrs Bello’s selflessness and passion for other people were commendable and should be emulated by all.

“Mama Bello has proven to all of us that there is nothing you do that won’t be appreciated. You are now in the news positively because of your good work,” he stated, thanking Sowunmi-Kolapo for celebrating the retired officer.

“I want to thank our deputy governor (Kolapo) because this is extraordinary. Because of who you are, you have decided to honour this woman. God’s blessings will never cease in your home,” Tella prayed.

For Alhaji Semiu Sodipo, Ogun PDP Secretary, aside from Mrs Bello’s ever-smiling posture and diligence, she never indulged in bribe-taking, an attribute that he said other public servants should take a cue from.

“What is very unique about her is that she is always happy, saluting and greeting people; not frowning or transferring aggression to road users. Madam, you are very fantastic. Madam Anifat won’t take bribe from anyone. People like you are very rare.

Mrs Bello and her family members who graced the occasion could not hide their joy as they appreciated Sowunmi-Kolapo’s thoughtfulness and generosity.

They equally commended Mrs Adenike Adebutu for her kind gesture and thanked others for celebrating and supporting hardwork, dedication and service.

While praising the retired officer’s life of passionate service, her younger brother, Nunasu Jacob, said, “Aunty Anifat is accommodating and caring. She is generous to a fault, very nice and jovial.”

In her vote of thanks on behalf of the family, Dorcas Olusegun, one of Mrs Bello’s daughters, commended Hajia Sowunmi-Kolapo for organising the reception ceremony, thanking her and others who supported and honoured her mother.

Turning to Adebutu’s running mate, she said, “We really thank you, ma, for giving us a wonderful occasion to celebrate our mother. Your thoughtfulness and generosity made this possible. Your gesture means so much to our family and it will be indelible.”

Apparently overjoyed, Mrs Bello danced in appreciation to the honour and support accorded her by the PDP leaders in Ogun State.

“I am really happy and I want to thank our mummy, Hajia Sowunmi-Kolapo, Mrs Adebutu and others who have celebrated me. I ask God to bless them and grant them their good heart desires,” she prayed.

Mrs Bello seized the opportunity to advocate for diligence among all categories of workers, saying, “everyone should do their job well. Our youths, especially, must know that hard work pays.”

Recall that a video clip had shown Mrs Bello on her last day in uniform being celebrated by Abeokuta residents.

Members of the public who attested to her discipline, humility and no-bribes principle, refused to let her go quietly, showering her with cash gifts.

World.title: When Supreme Court Speaks, Politics Must Follow The Law
World.content:
*A legal perspective on the Supreme Court’s judgment on the Electoral Act 2026

By Olukayode Ajulo

The Supreme Court has spoken. We must now allow the law to speak through our conduct.

On 24 September 2026, the Supreme Court allowed INEC’s appeal in the dispute concerning Sections 77(5), 77(6), 77(7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. It set aside the judgment of the Court of Appeal and restored the judgment of the Federal High Court.

The immediate consequence is clear, but it is worth stating it correctly. The Supreme Court did not make these provisions law. They were enacted by the National Assembly. What the Supreme Court has now authoritatively determined is that the provisions challenged before it are not unconstitutional on the grounds upon which they were challenged. That distinction matters.

The provisions remain part of the law governing our electoral process, and they must be treated accordingly. The reports of the judgment indicate that the seven-member panel, led by Justice Adamu Jauro, specifically upheld Sections 77(5), (6) and (7), as well as Section 84(2), and held that they were not inconsistent with the 1999 Constitution.

There is another point which deserves emphasis because it goes to the heart of the constitutional argument. Section 228(a) of the Constitution expressly empowers the National Assembly to make laws providing guidelines and rules to ensure internal democracy within political parties, including laws regulating the conduct of party primaries, congresses and conventions.

Indeed, in President, Federal Republic of Nigeria & Anor v National Assembly & Ors (2022), the Supreme Court considered the scope of this constitutional power and recognised that the legislative authority of the National Assembly extends to making laws concerning internal party affairs within the constitutional limits prescribed by Section 228(a). That is significant.

The autonomy of political parties is real. But it is not an autonomy exercised in a constitutional vacuum. Party autonomy operates within the Constitution and within legislation validly enacted pursuant to the Constitution. The Supreme Court’s present judgment must therefore be understood against that constitutional architecture.

There has been understandable public interest in the fact that the Court of Appeal had earlier reached a different conclusion. There is nothing unusual about that in the life of litigation. Courts sometimes disagree, and that is precisely why our judicial system has appellate courts. The important point is that the Supreme Court is the apex court.

Section 287(1) of the Constitution is unequivocal: “The decisions of the Supreme Court shall be enforced in any part of the Federation by all authorities and persons, and by courts with subordinate jurisdiction to that of the Supreme Court.” That constitutional command is not ornamental.

The Supreme Court has now set aside the contrary decision of the Court of Appeal. The latter therefore cannot continue to be treated as the prevailing judicial position on the constitutional questions determined by the apex court. As the Supreme Court itself has repeatedly emphasised, its decisions bind the lower courts and must be given effect. The controversy has therefore moved from interpretation to compliance.

Sections 77(5), 77(6) and 77(7) concern the membership register of political parties and its use in congresses, conventions and primaries. Following the Supreme Court’s decision, these provisions should no longer be approached as though their constitutional validity remains an open question. They are operative provisions of the Electoral Act.

A political party that is required by law to submit a membership register to INEC cannot reasonably treat that register as a document that may be disregarded whenever it becomes inconvenient. The Supreme Court’s decision does not, of course, prevent whatever lawful administrative corrections or updates the Electoral Act or valid regulations permit. But the governing principle is straightforward. A statutory requirement cannot be reduced to a matter of political convenience.

The jurisprudence of the Supreme Court has long recognised that not every disagreement within a political party is justiciable. In Onuoha v Okafor (1983) 2 SCNLR 244, the Court established the traditional principle concerning the internal affairs of political parties. That principle has subsequently been considered in cases including Shinkafi v Yari (2016) and APGA v Anyanwu. But there is an important qualification. Where the legislature has expressly regulated an aspect of the electoral process, compliance with that statutory regime is a matter of law.

Indeed, in PDP v Lawal (2023), the Supreme Court recognised that an allegation of non-compliance with statutory requirements governing the nomination process could properly engage the jurisdiction of the courts. So, the proposition that political parties have internal autonomy cannot be stretched into a proposition that statutory electoral requirements are optional. Autonomy is not immunity from the law.

This is why Section 84(2) deserves equal attention. The same reasoning applies to Section 84(2), which provides for direct primaries or consensus as methods of nominating candidates.

The Supreme Court has now upheld the constitutional validity of that statutory framework in the case before it. The Court has not invented a new method of party nomination. Rather, it has determined that the statutory framework enacted by the National Assembly is not unconstitutional on the grounds presented in the litigation.

Political parties therefore need to examine their nomination procedures carefully and ensure that their internal processes conform to the Electoral Act. The principle is neither complicated nor controversial: Political parties are free to conduct their affairs within the law; they are not free to conduct their affairs outside it.

Therefore my word to political parties and aspirants will be to urge them to take this judgment seriously, and to do so without partisan colour. This is not a judgment that should be viewed simply as a victory for INEC or a setback for a particular political party. It is a judgment of the Supreme Court.

Every political party should therefore review its membership register, congress and convention arrangements, primary procedures, nomination guidelines and relevant electoral timetable against the Electoral Act as it now stands.

Aspirants should also do the same. No serious aspirant should leave the legality of the process to chance and hope to resolve it in court after the political contest is over. We have seen enough of that. A candidate should emerge from a lawful process, not become lawful merely because he or she has emerged. That distinction is worth remembering.

INEC should now give clear and practical effect to the judgment. Its guidelines and communications to political parties should reflect the law as it has been authoritatively interpreted by the Supreme Court, and it should make the relevant requirements clear, communicate applicable timelines properly and apply the law consistently to all political parties.

However, there is an equally important caution. INEC must administer the law; it must not make the law. The Commission cannot use its regulatory powers to add requirements that Parliament has not imposed, just as it cannot disregard requirements that Parliament has imposed and the courts have upheld. Its strength lies not in making electoral law, but in administering it fairly, faithfully and within the limits of its constitutional and statutory mandate.

And as patriots, we must learn to accept judicial decisions. This is a broader issue which, in my view, deserves attention. We must develop a stronger culture of accepting judicial decisions, particularly decisions of the apex court.

It is perfectly legitimate to disagree with a judgment. It is equally legitimate, where the law permits, to seek an appropriate judicial remedy. What is not acceptable in a constitutional democracy is for institutions or political actors to select the parts of a judgment that suit them and disregard the rest.

Section 287(1) does not say that Supreme Court decisions shall be obeyed when convenient. It says they shall be enforced. The rule of law cannot operate on a pick-and-choose basis. So we should let 2027 elections begin with compliance.

The 2027 elections are still ahead of us. There is therefore time for political parties and aspirants to look carefully at their processes, identify areas of possible non-compliance and correct them lawfully before they become disputes. That would be far better than conducting questionable processes today and asking the courts to rescue them tomorrow.

The lesson of this judgment, to my mind, is simple. The Supreme Court has settled the constitutional controversy before it. The Court of Appeal’s contrary decision has been set aside. The statutory provisions upheld by the Supreme Court remain operative.

The duty of political parties is to comply. The duty of aspirants is to understand the law before entering the contest. The duty of INEC is to administer the law fairly, consistently and within the limits of its statutory powers. And the duty of all of us is to remember that elections are not conducted in a legal vacuum.

Politics may be about competition. But the rules of that competition are determined by law. The Supreme Court has spoken. Let us now allow the law to do its work.

World.title: Anosike Promises Abians Monthly ‘Meet-Your-Governor’ Forum to Tackle  Problems
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Abia State, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, has promised to institute a monthly public forum as governor to get first-hand information on the welfare and problems of the Abia people with a view to addressing them directly.

Anosike pledged his campaign office in Umuahia when members of one of his leading support groups, the Kelechi Anosike G’eme Karia Movement, paid him an interactive visit to brief him on their activities.

The PDP flag bearer said his administration would be anchored on accessibility and people-centred governance.

Anosike said: “I can’t be the governor Abians cannot access. I will be very accessible. Many appoint Special Assistants who would receive mails, read them, and decide who should see the governor or not. That is very wrong. Nobody reads my mails for me. You read your mail yourself.”

He said the disconnect between the government and the governed often arises when those who worked for victory are abandoned after the election.

“Part of the problem is when you appoint people who were not part of your campaign trail and critical stakeholders who worked with you. If you don’t use those involved in the system, they won’t know the people, and there will be a disconnect. I will be accessible both to the pro-groups and the entire people of Abia State.”

On his proposed public interface, he said: “We will hold the Meet-Your-Governor Forum at least once a month. There are people who are crying daily because of injustice, nobody to address their matter. There are people looking up to God over the continuous injustice. Oppression and intimidation are going on daily; if any governor gets to hear it, he will solve it on the spot. But how will he hear it? Some don’t get to know until they leave office. Those things will stop.

“If it’s once a month, we will create that forum. We will go to Michael Okpara Auditorium or any big hall: the governor, his deputy, the Police, DSS Director, and all who will help to solve the problems will be at the high table to hear the people’s complaints. If you don’t attend to and solve the people’s problems, then what are you doing in government? Government is about the people.”

Anosike restated his welfarist ideology, insisting that it is not a political rhetoric.

“When I tell people I am a welfarist, that is not politics, that’s my makeup, that’s my nature. When we said we are going to build a Micro-finance Bank at Aba to give interest-free loans, we were not just making a promise because I am not going to do it with my personal money; it is the state money because the government is for the people.

“There is no form of economic empowerment for the people; it’s terrible. So, any government that cannot provide for the people should leave governance alone. The nature of government we want to bring will get to every ward,” he said.

Earlier, the Director-General of the Kelechi G’eme Karia Movement, Kelechi Nwosu, said the group has established functional structures in all 17 LGAs, 184 wards and 4,006 polling units in the state.

“We are working to deliver over 80,000 votes, planning a one-million-man march across all 17 LGAs, starting from Umuahia North. We will work hard for the emergence of Anosike as the state governor,” Nwosu announced.

He requested a branded campaign vehicle, office accommodation, and inclusion in the State Campaign Council.

In their separate remarks, the Coordinator for Ugwunagbo LGA, Azubuike Moses, appealed for mobilisation support, while the Movement’s Woman Leader, Mrs. Juliet Kalu, urged Anosike not to be afraid or intimidated but to pursue his governorship ambition with courage and faith in God, pledging to recruit more women into the Movement.

Responding, Anosike commended the group for its sacrifices and commitment.

He said: “I thank you for your work, commitment, sacrifices, conviction, and your belief system for this project. I’m a believer in destiny and divine organization of things. There is a reason for everything. In law, we say equity, like nature, does nothing in vain. There is a reason for this project. Of all the pro-groups working for this project, this group stands out as the best. You have done so well.

You have done such serious and marvelous work.”

The PDP candidate expressed confidence in victory, declaring: “You see this game we are playing; come February 6, we will be in the Government House. We are determined to take our state back and do the right thing. We have been in power; we now know what it is to be outside power; it is a terrible thing. We want to take back power and do the right thing. We are doing everything intentionally.”

He promised to donate a branded Sienna van and office accommodation to the Movement, and urged members to ensure their presence is felt in every ward.

World.title: Orlando Pirates to unleash Mohau Nkota against Sundowns?
World.content:
Orlando Pirates winger Mohau Nkota could make his first appearance of the season against Mamelodi Sundowns this weekend.

The Buccaneers and The Brazilians meet in the final of the MTN8 at the Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban on Saturday evening.

Both teams have been on form this season and will meet for the first time this campaign.



Ahead of the final, Nkota was seen training with the team for the first time which indicates he could be available for selection against Downs.

Nkota returned to Pirates on a season-long loan from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq on 4 September but due to the injury he sustained last season, he is yet to make an appearance for the Sea Robbers.

The 21-year-old was part of the Bucs academy before he was promoted in 2024. He only played a season before moving to Saudi.

What ex-Pirates winger said about Nkota

Former Sundowns and Pirates winger Lebohang Mokoena feels Nkota returning to Mayfair will help him as well as the club.

“I think he’s got a big role to play, especially with the experience he has gained over the last season or so. Also remember, he was a big part of that Bafana team, as much as he didn’t make the World Cup squad,” Cheeseboy told Soccerbeat.

Mokoena then added that Nkota could be returning to Pirates with one goal in mind: winning the league title.



“Maybe at the back of his mind, he’s thinking, ‘I left without winning the league. Time for me to collect a league medal because this side, it looks like oil prices have increased in Saudi,’” Mokoena joked.

The former winger also believes Nkota’s ability to play on the left could prove particularly valuable for Pirates.

“Looking at the position he is playing, and being a left-footer, I think Pirates are scarce in that department. They only have Moremi starting,” he added.

World.title: RIP: Affies Grade 12 learner dies one day after 18th birthday
World.content:
A grade 12 learner named Kéan Botha has tragically lost his battle with cancer just one day after his 18th birthday.

AFFIES MOURNS KEAN BOTHA

Afrikaanse Hoër Seunskool, known as Affies, announced the death of their grade 12 learner Kéan Botha , who died just one day after his 18th birthday. Botha passed away after losing his battle with cancer on Sunday. He was a hocked player and named the most promising player in 2025.

“It is with grief that we learned that Kéan Botha (grade 12) lost his battle against cancer last Sunday, a day after his 18th birthday. Kéan was a avid hockey player. He was named the most promising player in 2025 and played for the school’s first team,” read the statement.



“We pray for the Lord’s comfort of the Botha family in this extremely difficult time. Affies expresses his deepest sympathy to Kéan’s family and his friends,” read the statement.

In September, Grade 9 day scholar Nico Caine passed away. Nico was a Grade 9 day scholar at Paul Roos Gymnasium, one of Stellenbosch – and South Africa’s – best-known schools.

TRIBUTES POUR IN FOR THE LEARNER

“Our deepest condolences to Affies and the Botha family following the passing of Kéan Botha. A talented hockey player and proud Affie, Kéan’s life and sporting spirit will be remembered with great respect. May the Lord surround his family, friends and the entire Affies community with comfort and strength during this difficult time. From the Maritzburg College family, our thoughts and prayers are with you 🔴⚫⚪,” wrote @maritzburg_college.

“This is absolutely heartbreaking to read, may his family be comforted in this difficult time 😢🕊️,” wrote @mrs_gale_.

“Someone who always put others above himself even though he went through a bad time. Someone of true character and a real man to look up to even if he was only 18 years old. ❤️💛💚,” wrote @gustav_b10.

“Rest in eternal peace Kéan. May your family and friends be comforted by warm memories of a beautiful life! ❤️,” wrote @erniefaller.

World.title: MTN8 final: Orlando Pirates predicted XI to beat Sundowns
World.content:
Orlando Pirates face Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final this Saturday, with the Buccaneers aiming to lift the trophy for a fifth consecutive time.

Pirates head into the final as slight favourites after beating Sundowns in their previous two MTN8 finals. However, they will know that another tough battle awaits against their biggest domestic rivals.

With Thalente Mbatha unavailable, the midfield is likely to be the biggest area of concern for the Buccaneers. Nevertheless, Pirates have enough quality across the squad to challenge Sundowns and defend their title.



Here is how Orlando Pirates could line up:

Goalkeeper: Sipho Chaine

Sipho Chaine should retain his place between the posts. The goalkeeper has established himself as a key figure for the Buccaneers and will be expected to play an important role against Sundowns.



Orlando Pirates defence to be key in MTN8 final

Defence: Kamogelo Sebelebele, Lebone Seema, Nkosinathi Sibisi, Deon Hotto

Kamogelo Sebelebele should continue at right-back, while Lebone Seema and Nkosinathi Sibisi are expected to form the central defensive partnership.

Deon Hotto should slot in at left-back, providing experience and attacking threat from the flank.



Midfield: Mthetheli Mthiyane, Thapelo Mokodi, Camren Dansin

The midfield could be the most difficult area for Pirates to get right, particularly with Mbatha missing.

Mthetheli Mthiyane and Thapelo Mokodi could operate in the middle alongside Camren Dansin. They will have a huge task against a Sundowns midfield that is likely to dominate possession.



Attack: Oswin Appollis, Yanela Mbuthuma, Gamphani Lungu

Oswin Appollis could start on the left wing, with Gamphani Lungu operating from the right. Pirates reaching the MTN8 final was due to their attack and will need to get the best out of their wingers.

Yanela Mbuthuma is expected to lead the line and will need to make the most of his opportunities against a strong Sundowns defence.



Pirates favourites in the MTN8 final?

On paper, this is a strong Orlando Pirates side capable of beating Sundowns. The Buccaneers have already shown their ability to perform in this competition, and their experience in recent MTN8 finals could give them an advantage.

If Pirates play to their full potential, they should have enough quality to overcome Sundowns and lift the MTN8 trophy for a fifth consecutive year.

World.title: October 2026 fuel price: Inland petrol tops R30 a litre for the first time
World.content:
The October fuel price is official, and it’s worse than the forecasts predicted. From Wednesday, South Africans will pay more at the pumps than ever before.

The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources has confirmed the new prices, which take effect on Wednesday, 7 October.

Petrol 95 rises by R3.33 a litre .

. Petrol 93 rises by R3.12 .

. Diesel climbs by between R2.84 and R3.24 a litre, depending on the grade.

WHAT THE OCTOBER 2026 FUEL PRICE MEANS AT THE PUMP

In September, 95 petrol cost R26.92 a litre inland and R26.05 at the coast.



Add the October 2026 increase, and inland 95 climbs to about R30.25 a litre. That pushes petrol past R30 for the first time in South Africa’s history.

At the coast, including Cape Town and Durban, 95 rises to about R29.38. Inland 93 climbs to about R29.88.

The previous record for 95 petrol was set in June 2026, at R28.06 a litre inland and R27.19 at the coast.



Diesel is breaking records too.The wholesale price of 500ppm diesel rises from R29.11 to about R31.95 a litre inland.

That’s above its peak of R31.18 in May 2026.

Here’s what that looks like in your wallet

Filling a 50-litre tank with inland 95 will cost about R166.50 more than in September 2026.



That’s roughly R1512 a tank, up from R1346.

A year ago, things looked very different.

In September 2025, 95 petrol cost R21.55 a litre inland.



WHY THE OCTOBER FUEL PRICE IS SO HIGH

According to the department, the average Brent crude oil price rose from $87.89 (R1,425) to $101 (R1,637) a barrel during the review period.

The department blamed continued US-Iran tensions, uncertainty over oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, higher shipping costs and shrinking inventories.

The rand offered almost no help. It strengthened ever so slightly, from R16.213 to R16.212 to the dollar, and that shaved less than a cent off each litre. The final hike also overshot the forecasts.



PARAFFIN AND GAS GO UP TOO

It’s not only motorists who will feel the pain.

The wholesale price of illuminating paraffin rises by R3.58 a litre, with its maximum retail price climbing by R4.77 a litre.

LPGas goes up by 42 cents a kilogram, and by 48 cents in the Western Cape.



Many households rely on paraffin and gas for cooking and heating, so these increases reach well beyond the forecourt.

The DMPR will publish the full price schedule for each zone on Tuesday, 6 October, so check your area’s exact pump price before you fill up.
