World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 5, 2026
World.content:
press review

Tigray Rebels Withdraw From Mekelle as Fighting Intensifies

Rebel forces in Ethiopia’s northern Tigray region have temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital, Mekelle, as fighting with government forces moves closer to the city. The Tigray People's Liberation Front said it relocated its fighters to reduce risks to civilians. The residents said that pro-government forces now control Mekelle and mobile phone services have resumed in parts of the city. The renewed fighting has spread across Tigray, Afar and Amhara, raising fears of a wider conflict in the Horn of Africa. The TPLF recently joined six other armed groups in an alliance seeking to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government. The development comes amid worsening relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea, as well as tensions with Egypt and Sudan, with Ethiopia accusing its neighbours of supporting the rebels. The United Nations has warned that the deteriorating security situation is disrupting humanitarian operations. The latest violence threatens the fragile 2022 peace agreement that ended a devastating two-year civil war in Tigray, which an African Union mediator estimated killed about 600,000 people.

France Steps Up Support for Ebola Fight in DR Congo



France said that it will increase support for efforts to contain a major Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 4,000 people have died. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced the additional support during a visit to Bunia in Ituri province, one of the areas hardest hit by the outbreak. According to the DR Congo Health Ministry, 4,042 people have died among 8,376 recorded cases since the outbreak was declared on 15 May. France has already allocated €13.4 million towards the response. Barrot said he would seek additional humanitarian funding during discussions on France’s budget. Although the number of new cases has declined in some areas, health officials warn the outbreak remains severe, with insecurity and difficulties accessing communities complicating the response. Doctors Without Borders says the situation has worsened in North Kivu, which has accounted for 40% of new confirmed cases since late August. DR Congo Health Minister Roger Kamba said that the epidemic has peaked. France is urging continued vigilance to prevent further spread.

Rwanda Genocide Justice Campaigner Dafroza Gauthier Dies

Dafroza Gauthier, a Rwandan genocide survivor who spent decades helping track down people accused of participating in the 1994 genocide and living in France, has died of cancer at the age of 72. Alongside her French husband, Alain Gauthier, she founded the Collective of Civil Plaintiffs for Rwanda, which filed civil cases against dozens of genocide suspects in France. Their efforts helped bring several suspects to trial under universal jurisdiction, with seven ultimately receiving final convictions and prison sentences ranging from 14 years to life. Gauthier, who was born into a Tutsi family in southern Rwanda, witnessed ethnic violence from a young age and lost much of her family during the genocide, including her mother, who was killed in a church in Kigali. After attending a genocide trial in Belgium in 2001, the couple began systematically investigating suspects living in France. Their work contributed to the 2014 conviction of former Rwandan intelligence chief Pascal Simbikangwa, who received a 25-year sentence for genocide and crimes against humanity. Gauthier maintained that her goal was justice rather than revenge and continued the work until her death.

Somaliland Rejects Somalia Claims Over Israel and Berbera

Somaliland has rejected comments by Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud about its relationship with Israel and the strategic port of Berbera, saying Somalia has no authority over Somaliland’s foreign relations. Somaliland's Foreign Ministry described the president's remarks as misleading and reaffirmed its claim to sovereignty, saying its diplomatic ties with Israel are sovereign decisions intended to promote cooperation, development and regional stability. It also rejected claims that Berbera could be used as a platform for aggression against other countries. Somaliland defended its support for negotiated arrangements allowing landlocked Ethiopia access to the sea and criticised Somalia’s opposition to the 2024 Ethiopia-Somaliland memorandum of understanding. Somaliland and Israel established diplomatic relations after Israel formally recognised Somaliland in December 2025. The Somaliland government accused Somalia of interference and threats of force and called for restraint. It said that it would continue pursuing peaceful diplomacy and partnerships across the Horn of Africa and Red Sea region.

Close 

Chivayo and Wife to Be Buried Despite Missing Remains

The bodies of Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife, Lucy Muteke, will be buried at Glen Forest Cemetery in Harare on Thursday, despite some remains, including their heads, still missing after their helicopter crash. The couple died when their Bell 430 helicopter crashed at Kudenga Farm in Marondera while they were travelling from their rural home in Gandami, Chikomba East. Three other people also died in the crash, which left the bodies severely fragmented and some remains destroyed by fire. A family spokesperson dismissed social media claims that several skulls had been recovered, saying the last identifiable personal items found were Chivayo's wristwatch and his wife’s watch. Because the remains are incomplete, there will be no body viewing before the burial. The couple will be buried side-by-side in separate graves. The family has also rejected claims that the funeral will be private, saying anyone wishing to mourn Chivayo is welcome to attend. Chivayo was declared a provincial hero.

World.title: South Africa: Fochville Crash Accused Due in Court - South African News Briefs - October 5, 2026
World.content:
press review

Fochville Crash Accused Due in Court

The man accused of causing the deaths of 11 learners and their scholar transport driver in Fochville is expected back in court, reports EWN. Gert van Emmenis faces 12 counts of culpable homicide and a charge of reckless and negligent driving over the July 2024 crash, in which a Ford Ranger collided with a taxi carrying the children. The taxi overturned and caught fire, killing the 11 children, all under 14, and their driver. The case has been postponed several times for further investigations. The court is expected to consider representations before the matter can move forward. Van Emmenis was granted R20,000 bail after the State did not oppose his application.

Thembisa Women Demand Safer Community



Women living in the Vusimuzi informal settlement in Thembisa, Ekurhuleni have said that they fear for their safety and want the area declared a danger zone following the discovery of 12 women's bodies across Ekurhuleni in the past two months, reports SABC News. Residents said that criminals operate with little police visibility, with women reporting robberies, attacks and incidents of criminals entering homes at night. Their concerns come after 23-year-old Boitumelo Mashita was shot and killed in Thembisa on 28 September, allegedly by her estranged husband. Mashita was laid to rest.

AKA and Tibz Murder Trial Begins

The long-awaited murder trial of rapper Kiernan "AKA" Forbes and celebrity chef Tebello "Tibz" Motsoane is set to begin at the Durban High Court, nearly three years after the pair were gunned down outside a restaurant on Florida Road, reports EWN. Seven men are expected to stand trial for the two murders. The case has faced delays, including the extradition of brothers Siyabonga and Malusi Ndimande from Eswatini after they allegedly fled there following the February 2023 killings. They were returned to South Africa last year and charged with the murders. The trial is expected to run until 6 November, with a break on 4 November for the elections.

World.title: Nigeria: Breaking - 32 People On Board Crashed Nigerian Military Aircraft - Aviation Minister

PREMIUM TIMES reported the crash on Monday morning, with the Nigerian Air Force saying the aircraft was travelling on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos.

There were 32 people on board a military aircraft that crashed in Ondo State on Monday, the Minister of Aviation, Festus Keyamo, said in a post on X.

PREMIUM TIMES reported the crash on Monday morning, with the Nigerian Air Force saying the aircraft was travelling on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In his first official statement on the crash, Mr Keyamo said, "Preliminary information suggests that there were 25 passengers and 7 crew members on board."

Search and rescue operations are still ongoing, and the casualty figure from the crash has yet to be determined.

Read the minister's full statement below.

"I regret to inform the general public that Air Traffic Controllers have informed me of the disappearance of a military aircraft with tail number NGR 931, enroute Lagos from Benin at 0913 hours earlier today. All efforts to raise the aircraft on radio proved abortive.

"Subsequently information however confirmed that the military aircraft has crashed close to the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The wreckage has been located and search and rescue operations are ongoing.

Preliminary information suggests that there were 25 passengers and 7 crew members on board.

Whilst the control and regulation of military aircraft are completely outside the authority of the Ministry of Aviation, and Civil Aviation Authority, I have just spoken to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke and pledged our total cooperation and assistance in the search and rescue efforts ongoing.

Further information on this unfortunate incident will be made available subsequently.

World.title: Nigeria: Helicopter Crashes in Ondo
World.content:
The identity of the helicopter and the people on board have yet to be ascertained as of the time of this report.

A helicopter has reportedly crashed in Igbokoda, the headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State. The exact number of people in the helicopter and their fate could not be determined at the time of this report.

The incident occurred on Monday, throwing residents of the coastal community into panic as emergency responders and other relevant authorities moved to ascertain what happened.

PREMIUM TIMES will provide more details in subsequent reports.

World.title: Mozambique: Mozambique's Army Is Losing a Crucial Counter-Insurgency Battle
World.content:
analysis

Foreign training has strengthened the army, but abuses against civilians undermine the community support needed to defeat insurgents.

When terrorists attacked Cabo Delgado nine years ago on 5 October 2017, the Mozambique Defence Armed Forces (FADM) was taken by surprise, despite its three decades of experience fighting armed conflicts inside the country.

Until then, Mozambique had been largely spared the terrorist threats experienced by other African countries and beyond. The FADM had scant control over Cabo Delgado province and was unprepared for a rural guerrilla war imposed by local jihadists with external support. It lacked combat capability, logistics, modern military equipment, air combat assets and military intelligence.



The FADM has since benefitted from substantial external training and efforts to improve logistics and equipment. But this has yet to translate into results on the ground, where communities still suffer inadequate security and human rights violations at the hands of state forces. And it is in these communities that the FADM should be gaining the upper hand against insurgents.

Insurgents' seizure of district capitals and TotalEnergies subsequent suspension of its US$20 billion gas extraction project in 2021 forced the government to request external support, some of which benefitted the FADM.

The Southern African Development Community Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) helped the FADM dismantle terrorist bases and neutralise leaders, restore state authority, strengthen maritime security and protect access routes within the province. The Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) helped recover territories key to the gas industry's logistics and trained the FADM in counter-terrorism, as did the European Union (EU), Algeria, United States (US) and other allies.

Of all these programmes, the EU's has had the greatest impact, channelling roughly €89 million into training and the acquisition of non-lethal equipment. The EU Training Mission in Mozambique trained over 1 600 military personnel, divided into 11 FADM Quick Reaction Force companies. The courses covered command and control, communication, civil-military cooperation, human rights and international humanitarian law.

Mozambique reactivated its military cooperation with Algeria, focusing on operational training, counter-terrorism and technical capacity building for army personnel. Specialised training of an FADM battalion currently underway in Algeria is expected to include tactical instruction, among other elements.

Through the US' Joint Combined Exchange Training programme, the FADM receives instruction in small-unit tactics, operational planning, combat medical care and civil protection.

These initiatives are gradually transforming the FADM's capabilities and increasing the survival rates of military personnel. However, inadequate logistics and equipment remain a major operational weakness, with much of FADM's gear originating from Russia and China. Military personnel report obsolete and non-functional weaponry, which has led to deaths on the battlefield, and insufficient transport for troops and for evacuating the injured.

In response, the Ministry of National Defence has built partnerships to secure logistics, supplies and equipment for the FADM. In March, an agreement was signed with India to supply defence equipment and transfer technology for the assembly and repair of aircraft, land vehicles and patrol vessels.

In 2024, a defence cooperation agreement with Turkey was ratified by Mozambique's Council of Ministers to develop an industry focused on military aviation and weapons, combat vehicles and the manufacture of naval assets.

The US is providing US$1.5 million for a new programme to strengthen Mozambique's capacity to manage and secure weapons and ammunition, and to reduce the risk of conventional weapons being diverted to criminal and terrorist groups.

However, the impact of these partnerships has yet to be felt on the ground. Since SAMIM's withdrawal in mid-2024, the FADM has independently led offensives, patrols along major roads, and established defensive positions to contain terrorists' advance. But weaknesses are showing.

Terrorist groups that had been confined to remote bases regained momentum and began attacks on major roads to steal food, abduct drivers and passengers, and demand ransoms. Joint police and FADM escorts were introduced, but the insurgents staged deadly ambushes, killing police officers, soldiers and civilians.

Human rights violations are another problem. Mozambican troops have repeatedly been accused of sexually exploiting displaced women, killing civilians suspected of collaborating with terrorist groups and committing war crimes against captured terror suspects. While the EU's training emphasises human rights, reports of civilians being killed by the FADM continue.

With training provided to the FADM by various countries, the problem of multiple military doctrines hinders a coherent approach to human rights. And Mozambique's political leadership has not clarified the matter. In his September speech marking the FADM's 62nd anniversary, none of President Daniel Chapo's recommendations addressed the need to respect human rights in counter-terrorism operations.

This is where Mozambique is losing the war against terrorism. As long as the FADM fails to gain the support of local communities in Cabo Delgado, the insurgents will keep thriving. They do not need to be militarily superior to government troops, as they are characterised by small, lightly armed bands practising guerrilla warfare.

Close 

To survive, they need to hide from government forces, which is made possible by the rough terrain, poor road access and distance from the centres of state power. And they benefit from local communities who agree not to report insurgents to government agents.

Effective counter-insurgency requires government forces to distinguish between active rebels and non-combatant community members. Rather than being targeted or killed by security forces, these community members should be encouraged to cooperate by reporting the insurgents' presence.

The recent establishment of a counter-terrorism centre offers hope that Mozambique can benefit from interagency coordination to better plan and conduct its counter-insurgency operations. But for this to happen, the FADM must reverse its culture of human rights abuses against communities affected by the insurgency and foster effective civil-military cooperation.

Borges Nhamirre, Researcher, Transnational Threats and Organised Crime, ISS

World.title: Nigeria: 28 Killed Despite Curfew in Plateau
World.content:
At least 28 people have been killed in a renewed wave of attacks across three local government areas of Plateau State despite a dusk-to-dawn curfew imposed by the state government on September 21 to restore peace and prevent further loss of life.

The affected areas, including Mangu, Bokkos and Barkin Ladi, have witnessed repeated attacks in recent weeks, leaving thousands of residents living in fear, disrupting farming and cattle grazing and forcing many people to abandon their livelihoods.

Daily Trust reports that the latest incident occurred yesterday where two people were killed and six others injured following an attack on Sunday evening on Fulani herders in a pick up vehicle around Total filling station in Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The latest attack occurred less than two weeks after gunmen attacked herders around Kassa community of Barkin Ladi, killing five and injuring one.

The state chairman of Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria (MACBAN), Ibrahim Yusuf Babayo, who confirmed the incident in Jos yesterday said the gunmen attacked the vehicle around 5:30 while they were returning from the Cattle market to Bassa LGA of the state.

The chairman condemned the incident and called on the security agencies to track down those responsible and bring them to justice. He described the attack unprovoked and disturbing.

He said the insured victims have been rushed to the hospital, adding that one person was missing.

The spokespersons of Operation Enduring Peace and State Police command, Captained Polycarp Oteh and SP Alabo Alfred, didn't respond to inquiries from our correspondent as of press time.

Plateau had continued to witness attacks and killings despite the curfew imposed by the government.

In September alone, many people, including men, women and children, were reportedly killed, while houses and farmlands were destroyed and hundreds of cattle shot dead. The attacks have displaced families and disrupted economic activities across several communities.

Worried by the deteriorating security situation, the Plateau State government, through the Commissioner for Information and Communication, Joyce Ramnap, imposed an immediate dusk-to-dawn curfew on Barkin Ladi, Bokkos and Mangu on September 21.

The restriction of movement, which took effect that day, runs from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. The government said the measure was intended to enable security agencies to stabilise the affected areas, protect lives and prevent a breakdown of law and order.

Security operatives were also directed to enforce the curfew and a ban on motorcycles in the affected areas.

However, the measure has failed to halt the killings, with several attacks recorded after its imposition.

The development has raised fresh concerns about the effectiveness of the security measures and the ability of security agencies to protect residents in the volatile communities.

More killings after curfew

Meanwhile, the attacks have continued despite the curfew and the visit of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to the state on September 16 following killings in Mangu and other parts of Plateau.

During his visit, Disu said the police were committed to restoring peace and strengthening security operations in the state.

He assured residents that the police would continue to work with stakeholders to find lasting solutions to the crisis, stressing that sustainable peace required synergy and collaboration between security agencies and communities.

But fresh attacks were recorded in the affected communities.

On September 20, five Fulani herders were killed in Kassa community, Barkin Ladi, while transporting cattle from Bokkos to Jos South.

The following day, the state government announced the curfew.

On September 22, gunmen reportedly ambushed security operatives attached to Operation Rainbow along Gagshi Road, killing a police officer. Three Berom farmers were also reportedly killed at Rakok community in Barkin Ladi on the same day.

In Mangu, three vigilantes of Mwaghavul extraction were ambushed and killed at the Kyikyau-Gyambwas boundary.

Two Berom miners were killed at Gangare community, Barkin Ladi, on September 23 while carrying out mining operations.

The following day, a 27-year-old Fulani herder was killed, and 30 cattle reportedly rustled around Banka village in Mangu.

On September 25, three vigilantes, including a youth leader, were killed in Kassa community, Barkin Ladi. The attackers reportedly stormed the community around 1am and opened fire on the victims, who were said to be on duty protecting the area.

The killings prompted protests, with residents reportedly calling on soldiers stationed in the area to leave, expressing frustration over repeated attacks despite the presence of security personnel.

On September 26, five miners were killed and two others injured when gunmen ambushed them at Marit community in Barkin Ladi.

The violence spread further on September 27 when gunmen attacked a herding community in Lamor, Pushit District of Mangu. More than 20 cattle were reportedly killed, while several others were injured and more than 70 remained missing.

A Fulani herder was also killed around Rakung village in Barkin Ladi on the same day.

On September 28, three women working at a mining site in Rakum community, Barkin Ladi, were killed and another person injured after gunmen opened fire at the site.

A 14-year-old Fulani herder, Aliyu Ismail, was reportedly killed around Wereng community in Riyom Local Government Area on October 1.

The latest reported attack occurred on October 3 when two Berom men from Heipang District, Barkin Ladi, were shot dead at a mining site around Kuru Jenta, near the boundary between Jos South and Barkin Ladi.

Livelihoods paralysed

Beyond the deaths, the prolonged violence has severely affected economic activities, with farmers and herders suspending operations in parts of Mangu, Riyom and Barkin Ladi because of fear of attacks.

Residents said they were no longer able to freely access farms or grazing areas located far from their communities.

A resident of Dorowa Babuje in Barkin Ladi, Paul David, described the situation as chaotic.

"We cannot go to the farm freely like before because you don't know who is hunting for your life. We are no longer going to the farm as we used to. Farms that are far from the community cannot be accessed," he said.

A herder in Lugere, Barkin Ladi, Habibu Ibrahim, said grazing had also become difficult because herders risked being attacked or having their cattle rustled.

"We don't graze our cattle the way we used to because you can easily be attacked and killed. It is very difficult to move around because your life is at risk. We are being hunted by gunmen," he said.

Another farmer from Bokkos, Christopher Rafan, said the crisis had forced farmers to change their farming practices.

He said his cousin was killed while returning from the farm, adding that residents no longer planted tall crops such as maize and guinea corn close to communities because the crops could obstruct their view of approaching attackers.

He urged the government to intensify security in the villages, noting that some of the volatile rural communities were not covered by the curfew.

A herder in Riyom, Musa Abdullahi, also said grazing had become restricted because herders could no longer safely move long distances with their cattle.

A crisis with deep roots

The latest violence has further deepened longstanding tensions between Berom and Fulani communities, with leaders of the two groups trading accusations over responsibility for attacks on their members.

The rivalry, often complicated by farmer-herder disputes, land ownership and the longstanding indigene-settler divide, has claimed hundreds of lives and destroyed communities over the years.

The crisis also has an ethno-religious dimension dating back to the violent conflict that erupted in Jos in September 2001. The initial dispute later escalated into wider religious violence, leaving hundreds dead and many more displaced.

Since then, mistrust between Christian and Muslim communities has persisted, with accusations and counter-accusations often following fresh attacks.

The violence later spread into rural communities, particularly through farmer-herder conflicts, resulting in killings, destruction of property and displacement.

A committee set up by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and chaired by General Nicholas Rogers (retd.) to investigate the root causes of the crisis reportedly disclosed that about 11,000 people had been killed in Plateau over two decades.

Successive federal and state governments have established committees and introduced various initiatives aimed at ending the violence, but the attacks have continued.

Non-governmental organisations have also been working to complement government efforts through dialogue, mediation and community resilience programmes.

Close 

Organisations including the Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue, Youth Initiative Against Violence and Human Rights Abuse, CLEEN Foundation and Justice, Development and Peace Commission have facilitated inter-community dialogue, mapped conflict drivers and supported local peace structures.

The efforts have produced peace accords in some flashpoint areas, including Riyom and Barkin Ladi, where communities agreed on responsible grazing, early reporting of incidents and measures to curb criminality and drug abuse.

However, the latest attacks have shown the fragility of the peace efforts.

The Executive Director of YIAVHA, Pwakim Jacob Choji, said the government needed to invest more in social cohesion and community dialogue.

Choji said growing grievances against government were undermining public confidence and contributing to the security challenges.

The Director of the Civil Liberties Organisation, Steve Aluko, said the crisis could be resolved if the government addressed what he described as wrong profiling of criminal elements, weak enforcement of justice and inadequate security presence in difficult terrains.

He also advocated state policing and a regional security architecture that would combine intelligence gathering, analysis and appropriate deployment of security personnel.

The Vice Chancellor of Plateau State University, Bokkos, Professor Shedrack Best, identified inadequate youth participation in peacebuilding as one of the factors sustaining the crisis.

Best, a professor of International Relations and Peace Building, said many peace initiatives were targeted at traditional, religious and community leaders, while youths at the grassroots, who often bear the brunt of the violence, were left out.

He urged stakeholders to organise peacebuilding programmes in villages and directly involve young people from the affected communities.

He commended the Plateau State Peace Building Agency for taking peace initiatives to villages and local government areas.

With 28 people killed despite the curfew and security assurances, residents are now calling for stronger protection of vulnerable communities, while stakeholders continue to seek a lasting solution to the cycle of violence.

World.title: Israeli medical workers who treated Oct 7 wounded relive day terror hit home
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

As Israel marks three years since the Oct. 7, 2023 terrorist attacks, stories of bravery and self-sacrifice continue to emerge from within a nation grappling with recovery and rehabilitation.

For Nil Kirsht-Levi, the three years since the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, massacre have been defined by devastating personal loss, an agonizing wait for her sister who was taken hostage and brought to Gaza and an unwavering commitment to caring for fellow survivors of the cross-border terror attack.

Kirsht-Levi, a nurse with Israel's largest healthcare provider, Clalit Southern District, who lives in Kibbutz Magen, spent the morning of Oct. 7 treating patients remotely from her safe room while trying to protect her three children as terrorists invaded the community and went from house to house. At the same time, she desperately texted her sister, Rimon Buchshtab-Kirsht, who lived with her husband in nearby Kibbutz Nirim.

FREED HOSTAGE ROM BRASLAVSKI DETAILS ABUSE, STARVATION DURING 738 DAYS IN GAZA CAPTIVITY

"I lost more than 30 patients that day, more than 200 people I knew, and around 100 people I knew were kidnapped," Kirsht-Levi told Fox News Digital. "I’m lucky to have a job that saves me, healthy children, a healthy husband. We work every day to recover and rehabilitate ourselves. Every day, we fall and get back up, but we are here — for ourselves, for others and we have won," she continued.

"We should never forget, but we must move forward, live every moment and keep going. It’s a privilege to be alive," she added.

On Oct. 7, Kirsht-Levi’s sister sent a message saying she could hear Arabic and that terrorists had entered her home. Weeks of agonizing uncertainty followed before Kirsht-Levi saw her sister alive in a Hamas video. She had campaigned for her release and ultimately welcomed her home 53 days later, emaciated and covered in scars, as part of a ceasefire deal in November 2023.

Her sister's husband, her brother-in-law, Yagev Buchshtab however, had been murdered by the terrorists.

During the 2023 Palestinian terror assault, launched on the Jewish holiday of Simchat Torah, Michaela Koretsky, a midwife with Clalit’s Southern District, improvised lifesaving treatments for wounded members of Kibbutz Alumim.

Like so many others, Koretsky was jolted awake by air raid sirens at 6:29 a.m. that fateful day, as Hamas launched thousands of rockets at Israel, providing cover for terrorists as they crossed the border in the ensuing invasion. She rushed with her husband and children to the shelter, where she received a message from Eran, a member of the kibbutz’s civil defense squad, asking if she was home. Eran then began bringing wounded kibbutz members to her for first aid.

ISRAELI OCTOBER 7 SURVIVORS CONQUER TRAUMA ALONGSIDE LEGENDARY ROCK ICONS IN POWERFUL NEW DOCUMENTARY

"When they entered the house carrying Amichai, he was covered in blood… I switched into nurse mode," she said.

Koretsky had Amichai placed on the floor as they continued to hear gunfire outside the kitchen window. She improvised bandages and prepared an IV while staying in contact with an emergency room doctor from Soroka Medical Center who was also in the kibbutz. He confirmed that Amichai was stable.

Then Eyal was brought in. He had been shot, with one of the bullets lodged in his lung. After Koretsky placed him on an IV and administered additional oxygen, it became clear that he needed to be evacuated.

"We needed to save lives, so I switched my brain into action mode and did what needed to be done. The whole time I dit not think that the terrorists would enter my house. I knew one of my children was afraid they would figure out where the wounded were being taken and come after us, but I told myself, ‘I am protected. It will not happen,’" she told Fox News Digital.

Her husband, Tzviki, accompanied by members of the kibbutz’s civil defense squad, reached his car and alone he evacuated the wounded under fire to Netivot, where they were transferred to waiting ambulances. From there, both Amichai and Eyal were taken to Soroka Medical Center for further treatment.

Prof. Shlomi Codish, director of the hospital in Beersheba, said he made three lifesaving decisions early on Oct. 7 that shaped the response throughout the day.

HAMAS USED SEXUAL VIOLENCE 'DELIBERATELY AND SYSTEMATICALLY' ON OCT 7, COMMISSION REPORT FINDS

First, he and his team decided not to send the night shift home, allowing the hospital to begin the day with twice its normal staffing level. At 7:45 a.m., they declared a mass-casualty incident, despite not yet knowing how many wounded would arrive and alerted all available staff to report to the hospital. Finally, they ordered additional blood supplies in anticipation of the surge of casualties.

"We usually start the shift with 50 units of blood in our blood bank. By the end of the day, we had given 250 units. If we hadn’t ordered additional blood early that morning, we might have run out and people may have died," Codish told Fox News Digital.

Codish said the hospital faced several overwhelming challenges throughout the day, beginning with the sheer number of wounded being brought to the hospital.

"In the first 24 hours, we received 674 wounded people. At the peak, we received more than 80 in a single hour, with an average of just 40 seconds between wounded people arriving," he said.

"This was one of the largest mass-casualty events resulting from terror in human history. The hospital itself was also under fire, with dozens of incoming missile warnings from the Gaza Strip, while attacks were taking place simultaneously at a very large number of sites," he added.



The second challenge was the immediate impact of the invasion on hospital staff themselves. "Everyone who came in left a family at home that was potentially under attack. They got into their cars and drove through air-raid sirens in areas that weren’t protected, at significant personal risk, to come in and save lives," he said.

Another major challenge was maintaining care inside the hospital as the number of casualties surged. The hospital began the day at full capacity, forcing staff to quickly free up intensive care beds and operating rooms for incoming patients. With roads around the hospital unsafe, transferring patients to other facilities was not an option in the first hours of the attack, while sending ambulances into the field risked exposing them to Hamas ambushes.

"When you see babies or children with direct injuries, that is not something you typically see on a battlefield. We saw elderly people with severe wounds inflicted directly, with no protection," Codish said, reflecting on the brutality he witnessed that day.

"As a medical professional, what we saw was beyond words. Two babies suffering from dehydration after their parents were killed, simply waiting to be rescued — I defy anyone to find a word other than ‘evil’ to describe it," he added.

World.title: Tom Kim plays his way to a military exemption, Austin Smotherman achieves a dream, and Brooks Koepka has life
World.content:
Tom Kim is used to playing golf for millions of dollars and job security, and is pretty comfortable in that setting as a four-time PGA Tour winner, but none of it compares to the pressures he faced while competing in this past weekend's Asian Games in Japan.

To leave America and golf behind and return to South Korea to serve in the military for over a year, or not — those were the stakes for the 24-year-old. Golf is already difficult enough, but adding the pressure of a legitimately life-altering situation seems downright crippling; Kim thrived under the wildly unique circumstances, and a text message from Tiger Woods may have played a tiny role in it all.

In Utah, the FedEx Cup Fall got back underway on the PGA Tour. It was already a milestone week for Austin Smotherman, but it turned into a career-altering one when it was all said and done on Sunday. Meanwhile, the DP World Tour played host to the always awesome Alfred Dunhill Links, and the consistently strong field featured Brooks Koepka, who may just have needed a few walks around some of the best courses on Earth to get his confidence back.

Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com .

Tom Kim plays his way out of military service

Under South Korean law, most able-bodied men must serve 18 to 21 months of military service. Special exemptions, however, are granted for both athletes and classical artists who excel in international competitions. Athletes can receive exemptions by earning any medal at the Olympics or a gold medal at the Asian Games.

Kim, born in Seoul, South Korea, would likely have had an opportunity in the 2028 Olympics to earn a medal and receive his military exemption, but why wait four years when an opportunity presented itself?

Kim entered the Asian Games in great form, fresh off being the leading points earner for his International side in the Presidents Cup, and he was able to ride the momentum into grabbing a one-shot lead heading into the final round in Japan. A one-shot cushion certainly eases things, but the pressures of a military exemption on the line, having to go out and perform across 18 holes, makes that cushion feel minuscule.

Prior to teeing it up in what will, in all likelihood, be the most important round of golf he ever plays in, Kim received a text message from none other than Tiger Woods.

"Just be you. Nothing more, nothing less," the message from Woods said, according to Korea’s Yonhap News Agency. It's safe to say that the short and sweet message from the big cat made an impact.

Kim went out and carded four birdies in his opening eight holes in the final round before making an eagle on the 13th to really grab hold of the moment. He ultimately carded a final-round 64 to earn a three-shot victory and the gold medal, and you could practically see the relief leave his body after he finished his final hole.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Given the wildly unique circumstances, it's impossible to even begin to imagine the pressure Kim must have felt throughout the week. He may have been the favorite to win gold to begin the games, but anything can happen when you're playing for a piece of your life's future in the most literal sense imaginable.

The year 2026 will be one that Kim never, ever forgets. While earning a military exemption undoubtedly tops his list of accomplishments for the year, he also won the Scottish Open for his first win on Tour in nearly three years and has climbed more than 70 spots in the world rankings after beginning the year outside the Top 100.

The 100th time's the charm for Austin Smotherman

Austin Smotherman is what we like to call a young journeyman.

The Bank of Utah Championship marked the former SMU Mustang's 100th career start on the PGA Tour, but the 32-year-old has played a lot of professional golf after turning pro back in 2016.

Mini tour reps, more than 30 starts on PGA Tour Latin America, another 102 starts on the Korn Ferry Tour, and now 100 on the biggest stage, he's paid his dues, and they paid off with a maiden victory in The Beehive State on Sunday.

Finding the winner's circle always helps to find perspective, but after his two-shot victory on Sunday, Smotherman was genuinely just happy to be in the position he's in as a competitor on the PGA Tour.

"One hundred starts out here is an incredible number, just to be blessed to have 100 starts, but even more so, to play professional golf now for 10 years, travel the world, have the support I've had, it's pretty unreal to lift a trophy at the highest level," the California native explained. "It's something we've dreamed about since I was a kid, and here we are."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Smotherman began Sunday's final round with a one-shot advantage over Doug Ghim, and while neither of the two had their A+ game across the final 18 holes, it was Smotherman who answered the call best when adversity came calling.

After making a double bogey on the Par 4 13th hole, he immediately answered with the tee shot of a lifetime on the drivable 14th to set up a routine birdie before playing his final three holes at 1-under to secure win No. 1.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

With the win, Smotherman earned a spot in the first two signature events of the 2027 PGA Tour season and a payday of $1.08 million.

Brooks Koepka finally finds something across the pond

Outside of Top 15 finishes at The Players and the Masters, Brooks Koepka's first season back on the PGA Tour after making his return from LIV Golf wasn't necessarily one to remember. Statistically, the five-time major champion was one of the best iron players in the game in 2026, but things never felt in sync, which led him to miss the FedEx Cup Playoffs altogether.

After putting together a season nowhere close to his standard, Koepka took a month-long hiatus from competitive golf before electing to try and retool with some reps on the DP World Tour.



While the journey got off to a bad start with a T-55 at the Irish Open in September and a missed cut at the BMW PGA Championship, this past weekend's Alfred Dunhill Links Championship may have been the springboard the American was looking for.

Tournament rounds spread across Kingsbarns, Carnoustie, and the Old Course at St. Andrews will grab the attention of anyone with a pulse, and Koepka's T-6 proved that.

The Alfred Dunhill may be the last time we see Koepka tee it up for quite some time, but those reps and that result in difficult conditions across the weekend could be something we look back on if he makes some immediate noise in 2027.

World.title: Washington family requests SCOTUS injunction after daughter was allegedly sexually assaulted by trans athlete
World.content:
EXCLUSIVE: A Washington family has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to step in after lower courts refused to let a teenage wrestler compete this season without being matched against a male athlete.

Alliance Defending Freedom (ADF) filed an emergency application with Justice Elena Kagan on behalf of K.M.K. and her mother, Stephanie Lynne Brown. The filing asks for an injunction pending appeal in K.M.K. v. Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA). The plaintiff is listed only as K.M.K. She is Kallie Keeler, the Puyallup-area wrestler who has spoken publicly about here experience in being allegedly sexually assaulted by a trans athlete during a match.

Keeler has been on the mat since she was 4. Wrestling was the season she waited for all year. She has not competed in a WIAA event since leaving the team in January, and she has said she is unsure she will return if she can be paired against a male again without notice.

FAMILY FILES LAWSUIT ALLEGING DAUGHTER WAS SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE DURING GIRLS' COMPETITION

The application says Keeler was 15 when she wrestled for third place at the Lady Jag Kickoff on Dec. 6, 2025, a girls’ tournament at Emerald Ridge High School. She and her mother say they were not told her opponent was male. During the match, they allege, the opponent penetrated her. Another team’s coach told her afterward that the opponent was male, the family says.

When Brown asked for a guarantee that her daughter would not have to face a male without penalty, and for notice so she could opt out, the district refused. It offered forfeiture if Keeler already knew the opponent was male. It said gender-identity information would be kept confidential.

"No girl should have to choose between playing the sports she loves and her safety," the application says. It asks the Court to bar officials from forcing Keeler to wrestle a male while the appeal goes forward, or at least to require notice and a no-penalty opt-out.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

INSIDE THE SUPREME COURT BATTLE TO 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS'

The defendants are the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association, the Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction, Superintendent Chris Reykdal, and the Puyallup School District. The athlete and the athlete’s family are not parties.

A federal judge in Tacoma denied a preliminary injunction on Aug. 23. The Ninth Circuit denied an emergency injunction on Sept. 25, calling the request a mandatory injunction and finding no likelihood of success strong enough to justify relief before the season. Wrestling in Washington opens in mid-November. ADF says that without an order now, Keeler loses the season Title IX is supposed to protect.

The filing leans on the Supreme Court’s June 30 decision in West Virginia v. B.P.J., which held that states may limit girls’ teams to biological females, and on Mirabelli v. Bonta, a March parental-rights order.

The U.S. Department of Education opened a Title IX investigation into the district in February. Two Rogers High School administrators were later charged with failing to make a mandatory report. Prosecutors did not charge the opponent.

The district has previously declined to comment, citing student privacy and litigation. OutKick sought comment from the WIAA, the Puyallup School District and the Washington Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction on the Supreme Court application.

Former Republican Rep. Dennis Hastert, who was the longest-serving GOP House Speaker, died on Monday at the age of 84.

Hastert died peacefully of natural causes at his home, according to Kendall County Coroner Jacquie Purcell. The longtime politician represented Illinois' 14th Congressional district for 20 years and served as Speaker of the House for eight years before retiring in 2007.

His career was later tarnished by a bank fraud conviction linked to his efforts to quash the story of a former student who accused him of sexual abuse during his time as a high school wrestling coach. He was sentenced to 15 months in prison in 2016.

Hastert also underwent sex offender treatment, two years of supervised release after his time behind bars and paid a $250,000 fine to a crime victims fund.

Hastert pleaded guilty in the case to attempting to pay $3.5 million to an unnamed individual to keep the alleged sexual abuse a secret.

Before he sentenced Hastert, Judge Thomas M. Durkin described the then-74-year-old Illinois Republican as a "serial child molester," and that "accusing Individual A of extorting you was unconscionable."

Multiple alleged victims and their family members read victim impact statements prior to Hastert's sentencing.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Steven Block called Hastert's conduct "horrendous." But because of the statute of limitations, Hastert could only be charged with a financial crime related to the payments he was making to one of at least four victims of sexual abuse.

World.title: Highest-ranking US official to ever serve jail time, former House Speaker Dennis Hastert dead at 84
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Former House Speaker Dennis Hastert, R-Ill., "passed away at his home due to natural causes," according to Kendall County, Illinois, Coroner Jacquie Purcell.

The brief statement was posted on the coroner’s website early Monday morning.

Hastert was 84 and one of the most ignominious figures to serve in American politics.

He was the longest-serving Republican speaker in history, wielding the gavel from 1999 to 2007. But Hastert’s career featured one of the most disgraceful falls from grace, becoming the highest-ranking U.S. official to ever do jail time.

MONICA LEWINSKY RECALLS 'VERY DARK MOMENTS' AFTER SCANDAL, SURVIVING JUDGMENT BY 'BILLIONS OF STRANGERS'

The scandal involving Hastert emerged years after he left Congress — but dates back to the 1960s and 1970s when he served as high school history teacher and wrestling coach in Illinois. Hastert admitted in 2015 that he sexually abused teenage students and athletes as young as 14 — long before he entered Congress in the mid-1980s.

Hastert was an accidental speaker.

He served as chief deputy whip in the Republican hierarchy in late 1998 when House Speaker Newt Gingrich, R-Ga., decided to step aside. Gingrich was controversial. Some GOP members had knives out for him and believed Gingrich overplayed his hand pushing for impeachment of President Clinton. This, coupled with Republicans nearly losing control of the House in the 1998 midterms, set the table for Gingrich to step aside.

Republicans tapped then-Rep. Bob Livingston, R-La., Chairman of the Appropriations Committee, to become Speaker in 1999.

But in late 1998, as the House voted to impeach Clinton, it came to light that Livingston had an inappropriate relationship with a lobbyist. Hours before the House voted to approve two articles of impeachment for Clinton linked to his relationship with Monica Lewinsky, Livingston stepped aside and said he would not stand for speaker in the new year.

By nightfall, Republicans picked Hastert, a backbencher, to serve as speaker in 1999.

Hastert was criticized in late 2006 for not moving more aggressively to protect teenage House pages after it was discovered that then-Rep. Mark Foley, R-Fla., sent inappropriate text messages to the pages. The scandal led to the end of the House page program, which dates back to the beginning of the republic.

Hastert lost the speakership when Democrats seized control of the House in the 2006 midterms. Hastert did not serve in the GOP leadership in early 2007 and resigned from office later that year.

FMR DEM REP BARNEY FRANK, SHARP-TONGUED LIBERAL TRAILBLAZER AND DODD-FRANK CO-AUTHOR, DIES

Hastert was often quiet and shunned interviews and the press.

Known as "Coach" to fellow lawmakers because of his wrestling background, Hastert often proclaimed that he was more of a "listener" than a "speaker."

But Hastert’s career took a dark turn in 2015.

US OLYMPIC HERO NANCY HOGSHEAD WINS LEGAL BATTLE AFTER VOLLEYBALL COACH'S $250M DEFAMATION SUIT IS DISMISSED

Federal banking regulators flagged Hastert’s curious withdrawals of staggering amounts of cash at peculiar intervals. Banking regulators suspected the transactions signaled that someone may be blackmailing the former Speaker.

But that’s how it came to light that Hastert was actually paying millions of dollars in hush money to the family of a student he abused in the 1970s.

Hastert admitted to sexually abusing students decades before at his trial for illegal bank transactions, saying he "mistreated athletes" and "took advantage of him." The judge in the case called the former speaker "a serial child molester."

Hastert served 13 of 15 months of his federal sentence for banking crimes at a facility in Rochester, Minn. However, Hastert never faced legal ramifications for sexual conduct.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Hastert is also known for the "Hastert Rule." When Hastert served as speaker, he would not bring a piece of legislation to the floor unless it had the support of a majority of House Republicans. House GOPers continued to use that standard for bills for many years after Hastert left office.

But that terminology fell out of favor after Hastert was convicted and information about his past became public.

World.title: Human vs humanoid robot cage fight goes viral
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

We've watched humanoid robots play soccer, run races and even fight other robots. Now, content creator Frankie LaPenna has taken things in a much wilder direction by stepping into a cage to fight them himself.

The event was staged by REK, a robotics entertainment company that puts remotely controlled humanoids into live combat events. In San Francisco, LaPenna faced three robots in a series of bouts, including two full-size EngineAI T800s, as part of what REK billed as the first human-versus-humanoid robot cage fight.

The viral footage getting most of the attention comes from one of those T800 fights. LaPenna moves toward the robot and throws several punches. The machine fires back with punches and kicks before one shot sends him flying across the cage. And if the robot looks like it walked straight out of "The Terminator," that was clearly the point. But the bigger story here is what these machines can actually do, who was controlling them and how much of the fighting was really driven by AI.

HUMANOID ROBOTS PERFORM LIVE SURGERY IN WORLD FIRST

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare with AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you prepare for appointments, remember important details, understand complicated medical information, research prescription questions and organize your next steps. No technical experience is needed.

Plus, recordings of all our past classes are available, including How to Stop Spam, Phone Security and Financial Protection, each with a free downloadable checklist.

Watch the free replays and get your checklists at CyberGuyLive.com

The bigger robots were modified EngineAI T800s

After facing a smaller Unitree G1, LaPenna went up against two modified EngineAI T800s, built by Chinese robotics company EngineAI. EngineAI lists the standard T800 at about 5 feet 8 inches tall and roughly 165 to 187 pounds, depending on the version. REK describes the modified machines used in its fights as about 6 feet tall. For the event, REK also gave the T800 a much more intimidating look. The mechanical head and glowing red eyes lean heavily into "The Terminator" theme. Put a machine that size inside a fighting cage and you can see why the video grabbed so much attention.

There was a person controlling the robot

Here's the big thing to know about this fight: there was a human behind the controls. REK's technology partner Reflex Arc says pilots operate the humanoids in real time using VR gear or a gamepad. AI helps with balance and trained movement, while the human pilot directs the action. So when you see a T800 throw a punch or launch a kick, the robot is carrying out the pilot's commands. It is not independently deciding how to fight LaPenna. That still leaves plenty to be impressed by because the machine has to stay upright, recover from contact and turn those commands into real physical movement inside the cage.

HUMANOID ROBOT VIDEOS SHOW MACHINES LASHING OUT

Frankie LaPenna actually fought three robots

The viral clip getting most of the attention only shows part of what happened that night. According to REK CEO Cix Liv, LaPenna faced three robots during the event. He reportedly started against a smaller Unitree G1 before moving on to two modified EngineAI T800 humanoids. REK says its modified T800 machines can kick with up to 850 pounds of force, which helps explain why the footage looks so intense.

LaPenna was knocked down during one of the T800 bouts, but Liv said he recovered, knocked the robot off balance and ultimately ended the fight with the robot's head coming off. REK has continued teasing more footage, and the short clips circulating online still do not show the full sequence of all three bouts. So what most people are seeing online is only one part of the event.

The fight took a physical toll on LaPenna

The physical side of the fight became pretty clear once LaPenna started trading punches with the robots. Liv said LaPenna originally wanted to fight without protective equipment, but REK insisted that he wear it. He ultimately entered the cage in motorcycle-style protective gear and gloves. According to Liv, LaPenna injured his hand while punching one of the robots but otherwise avoided a serious injury. Even with a human controlling the machine remotely, LaPenna was still trading blows with a heavy metal robot capable of putting real force behind its movements.

REK is betting on robot fighting as entertainment

REK has been building toward this kind of event for a while. The company stages live fights where people remotely control humanoid robots against other humanoid robots. It also has a simulator that lets players learn the controls before some get the chance to pilot the real machines. Reflex Arc says REK's first simulator championship generated 3,670 matches, with the winners flown to San Francisco to pilot real robots at REK2 in August. The simulator uses the same basic controls and trained balance system as the physical robots. That helps explain where REK is going with all of this. The idea is to take something that feels like a video game and put it into a real fighting cage with actual humanoid robots. Then LaPenna stepped inside and raised the stakes by putting a person on the other side.

LET'S LOOK BACK ON THE BEST MOMENTS (READ: CRASHES) FROM THE WORLD HUMANOID ROBOT GAMES

We've seen robot fighting before

Robot combat itself is nothing new, and we've been following that evolution closely. In 2025, four Unitree G1 humanoids fought in a boxing-style tournament in China. Those machines were also controlled by human operators, and the matches included punches, kicks and knockdowns. We have also watched humanoid robots play soccer without human control, rally on a tennis court and kick soccer balls hard enough to leave visible dents in a wall . REK's event takes that progression in a different direction. This time, the person sharing the cage with the machine can actually feel what happens when that robotic strength comes back at them.

What this human vs humanoid robot fight really shows

Strip away the Terminator head and the social media theatrics, and there is a pretty remarkable robotics demonstration underneath it. The larger T800s weigh as much as about 187 pounds, yet they can stay balanced in a confined fighting area, absorb contact and execute punches and kicks under human control.

The hardware is clearly becoming more capable. Compare today's humanoids with the awkward walking robots we were watching only a few years ago, and the change is dramatic. And something tells me Frankie LaPenna will not be the last person crazy enough to climb into the cage with one.

Kurt's key takeaways

I've watched humanoid robots do some pretty wild things, but seeing one kick a person across a cage definitely got my attention. The big thing to remember is that there was still a human pilot behind the controls. These robots were not independently deciding how to fight LaPenna. AI helped with balance and trained movement while a person directed the action in real time. What stands out to me is how quickly the physical side of this technology is advancing. These machines can stay upright through contact, recover and put some serious force behind their movements. REK even required LaPenna to wear protective gear before sending him into the cage. It makes for a viral video, but there is a more serious side to this, too. As humanoid robots become stronger and more capable, we are going to have to think carefully about who is controlling them, what safeguards are in place and where this kind of power should be used.

World.title: Plea agreement hearing set for ex-CIA officer found with gold bars
World.content:
WASHINGTON — A plea agreement hearing in federal court has been set for Tuesday in the case of an ex-CIA officer found with 303 gold bars worth $40 million at his home, according to court records.

David Rush, who has been accused of faking his lengthy professional record, has only formally been charged with one count of theft of public funds, accused of falsifying pay records. But two people familiar with the investigation have told NBC News that Rush is also accused of making up a false CIA program. Investigators believe there is likely more money or other items missing beyond what was seized by federal officials at his home, four people familiar with the investigation told NBC News.

Rush was placed on leave sometime before his arrest and eventually fired from the CIA. Court records show that the hearing Tuesday afternoon has been set before U.S. District Judge Michael Nachmanoff in Alexandria, Virginia.

A plea agreement would allow the government to avoid a lengthy trial which could bring further attention toward any mistakes the CIA made in the process and prevent the disclosure of additional information on the agency’s operations.

Rush has not yet entered a plea and has been held since his arrest. His attorney had no comment Monday. The prosecution and defense together had earlier requested additional time to work out a plea deal.

Rush’s case has also cast an unwelcome spotlight on the No. 2 at the Pentagon, Steve Feinberg, who had a close professional relationship with the former officer, sources told NBC News. Feinberg, through a Pentagon spokesperson, has denied the two had a close relationship.

Rush had worked on secret maritime programs at the Pentagon, NBC News reported in June. Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg was interviewed by the FBI as part of the investigation into Rush, but Feinberg has not been accused of wrongdoing and the bureau said in a statement he was not under investigation. There’s no indication Feinberg knew about Rush’s alleged fabrications. Several senior CIA officials were placed on leave over the management of Rush’s requests for money, NBC News reported in June.

The U.S. intelligence community’s inspector general is also investigating the circumstances that led to Rush’s arrest, which has raised questions among intelligence officials and U.S. lawmakers about how the CIA could have missed basic alleged falsehoods in Rush’s application, including about his academic and military records, NBC News reported last month.

World.title: Russia pounds Kyiv during German chancellor’s visit in a new escalation
World.content:
Germany’s leader faced a grim new reality as his train pulled into Kyiv: air raid sirens and the boom of Russian strikes on the Ukrainian capital.

During previous visits by international dignitaries of Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s stature, the Kremlin paused or dramatically reduced attacks on the city. On Sunday, the sounds of war rang out repeatedly as the German delegation made its way around Kyiv, in what looks to be a new level of escalation by Moscow.

On Monday, Germany’s foreign intelligence chief warned his country was at risk of becoming embroiled in a “violent conflict with Russia,” as Moscow steps up its “shadow war” against European democracies.

Germany has been one of the most ardent supporters of Ukraine since the early days of the Russian invasion, supplying both military and financial aid. The country has also taken in more than a million Ukrainian refugees fleeing the war.

Merz’s visit came as Russia has ramped up its around-the-clock strikes on Kyiv in recent weeks. The attacks and the air raid alerts that accompany them have severely disrupted life in the city, forcing millions to constantly seek shelter and paralyzing the capital’s businesses and transport networks.

Over the last four days, including on the day Merz was visiting, Russia has hit several of Kyiv’s key bridges, with some strikes coming in broad daylight and as traffic was flowing through them — in what appears to be a new tactic to disrupt links between the capital’s two sides separated by the Dnipro River to further disable movement around Ukraine’s largest city.

An air raid alert went off as Merz and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the site of a drone attack on the National Academy of Sciences last week. The dramatic daytime strike on the national landmark saw people clinging to windows to escape flames and thick smoke billowing out of the structure.
