World.title: Dubrovnik Nominated for the Title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination
World.content:
October the 5th, 2026 – Dubrovnik, once known as the unfortunate poster child of mass tourism, has now been nominated for the title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination.

After being named the world’s best sustainable destination back in 2025, Dubrovnik has once again been nominated this year for the prestigious title of “World’s Leading Sustainable Destination 2026” as part of the World Sustainable Travel & Hospitality Awards. Morski reports that voting is open until the 21st of October, and Dubrovnik is competing for the title against four other world destinations.

The new nomination represents a continuation of the international recognition of the City of Dubrovnik’s long-standing activities aimed at responsible and sustainable tourism management, the preservation of cultural and historical heritage, the protection of the natural environment, and the quality of life of the local population.

In 2025, Dubrovnik won the title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination, with particular emphasis in the justification on the Respect the City initiative, launched back in 2017 as a strategic and multidisciplinary model of destination management.

Among the measures recognised at the time were the application of new technologies in visitor management, an artificial intelligence-based system for predicting visitor numbers, the Dubrovnik Pass, coordination of cruise ship arrivals and a reservation system for tourist buses, as well as other projects that align tourism development with the needs of the local community and the protection of valuable heritage. The results of this approach are also visible through the assessment according to the criteria of the Global Sustainable Tourism Council (GSTC), according to which Dubrovnik increased its score from 70 percent in 2019 to 86.04 percent in 2023.

Competing with Dubrovnik for the title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination 2026 are Diriyah – The City of Earth, Dubai, the Maldives, and Serengeti National Park. Voting has been open from the 25th of September and will remain open until the 21st of October 2026. Representatives of the tourism and hospitality sector, the media, and the general public can participate. Votes from verified professionals in the tourism and hospitality industry carry double the value of public votes.

You can support Dubrovnik here.

The World Sustainable Travel & Hospitality Awards (WSTHA) is otherwise a global awards programme launched at COP28 in Dubai with the aim of recognising and showcasing individuals, organisations, destinations and initiatives that make a significant contribution to the sustainable development of tourism and hospitality. WSTHA is a sister programme of the World Travel Awards, an international tourism awards programme established in 1993, and 2026 marks its third annual edition.

The categories and criteria of the programme are guided by an international Advisory Board composed of experts, representatives of the academic community and leading institutions in the field of sustainable tourism. The programme is based on the principles of the UN Sustainable Development Goals and an approach that encompasses people, planet, place, prosperity and partnerships, with the aim of recognising concrete solutions, innovations and measurable progress towards more sustainable tourism.

World.title: Croatia Has a New Football Stadium That is Unique in the World
World.content:
October the 5th, 2026 – Croatia now has a brand new football stadium that is entirely unique in the world and boasts a million dollar view.

While spears are currently being broken over the issues with the new stadium at Maksimir, plans are being forged for the new so-called Poljud beauty and Kranjčevićeva is almost finished. Zvonimir Varga reports for Poslovni that Croatia is however home to a non-controversial new football stadium getting much less attention. It has sprung up on the sunny Kvarner coastline and will certainly attract plenty of attention with its appearance, particularly with its impressive view.

On Friday evening, along the main road that runs through Rijeka and Opatija, the new stadium of NK Opatija was officially opened with a match against the first-division side from Rujevica. Built on the site of the old one, it has become a modern complex constructed according to the infrastructural criteria of the Croatian Football Federation (HNS) for the second Croatian football league in which NK Opatija competes.

The new stadium has 802 seated places, separate stands for home and away fans, auxiliary facilities and a completely new artificial surface with the highest FIFA certificate. In addition to the main pitch there is also a smaller auxiliary pitch and a warm-up area. The main building houses new changing rooms, rooms for coaches and referees, a first-aid and doping-control room, an indoor training hall, storage rooms, a VIP area, catering facilities and a fan shop.

But what captures attention at first glance is the location of the stadium — more precisely the view that opens from the central stand onto the open sea, with the city of Rijeka on the left. Although this is a smaller stadium, there are not many stadiums in Europe, or even in the world, that offer such a view of the sea.

In Croatia the only comparable ones are Poljud, from which the sea is only partially visible, and Kantrida, where professional matches have not been played for a long time. In Europe there is the legendary Estadio Riazor of Spanish Deportivo, Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo in Venice, Stade Louis II in Monaco, and Henningsvær Idrettslag Stadion in Norway (without stands but surrounded by sea and mountains). Around the world, there are similar stadiums in Japan, Australia and South Africa. There are certainly more, but we are not sure whether any can match the ‘million-dollar view’ from the new Opatija stadium.

It should be emphasised that works on the renovation of the Opatija stadium began at the end of 2024, after the contract was signed with the contractor GP Krk. The total value of the project stands at a whopping 6.5 million euros. The project was realised through the city company Opatija 21, and financing was secured with credit funds from HBOR and Zagrebačka banka, with financial support from the Ministry of Tourism and Sport.

We all well remember the bronze medal from Russia and the silver from Qatar 2022, when it was said that the time was right for building new stadiums. We also remember the photo opportunities of the then football officials back in 2014 at Zagreb’s Svetice with shovels that were never put into the ground. Fortunately for all sports lovers, Croatian football today has some new people and initiatives, so we can be proud of Opus Arena in Osijek, the upcoming stadiums at Kranjčevićeva and Maksimir, the announced renovation of Poljud, and now also this small but distinctive new stadium in Opatija.

World.title: Zagreb Tram Payment and Ticket Inspection to Change in 2027
World.content:
October the 5th, 2026 – Zagreb tram payment methods and ticket inspection is set to change in 2027, making it all contactless and (finally) modernised.

Zagreb Electric Tram (ZET) is finally modernising its ticket payment system, and from 2027 onwards, passengers should be able to buy tickets by simply tapping a contactless bank card, mobile phone or smartwatch on a validator. Poslovni reports that the new system will support cards that use the Visa and Mastercard payment systems, as well as digital wallets such as Apple Pay and Google Pay, according to the portal Financije.hr.

“The public procurement procedure for new validators and central control units is currently underway, while full implementation on all trams and buses is expected during the summer of 2027. The modernisation covers more than 700 vehicles, as well as the necessary adjustments to the sales system platforms, which is why the introduction is being carried out gradually and requires a series of technical and operational activities,” ZET revealed recently.

Under the model that ZET is developing, a passenger will be able to buy a ticket by tapping a contactless payment method on the validator. After a successful transaction, a notification will appear on the screen, accompanied by an audio signal, confirming whether the purchase was successful. In the first phase, the system will allow the purchase of only one single ticket per transaction. ZET states that the possibility of buying several tickets at the same time, i.e. in a single transaction, will be considered and developed later in the project.

The new system should also simplify ticket inspection. Passengers will no longer need to show a paper ticket, a transaction confirmation or data from mobile banking. “During inspection it is enough to tap the same payment method that was used for validation – a contactless bank card, smartphone or smartwatch – on the inspector’s device. The device will then check the validity of the travel right linked to the payment method used,” they explained.

The goal of the modernisation is to give passengers a simpler way to buy tickets, as well as more efficient validation and inspection of travel rights. The new system could also make it easier for tourists to buy tickets, especially those who are not familiar with the existing purchase method. As a reminder, ZET has recently been in the spotlight because of a workers’ strike that began on the 28th of September. Zagreb’s tram and bus services were then fully restored after the County Court ruled in the first instance that the strike was unlawful.

World.title: Munjara – The Croatian Hydro Power Plant That Looks Like a Castle
World.content:
October the 4th, 2026 – Munjara in Ozalj is a Croatian hydro power plant that looks just like a castle. It has been in function since 1908 and still produces electricity.

When you think of industrial facilities, it’s more than likely that your first associations are “grey, unattractive, boring and a bit ugly”. That’s true in most cases, but not in all. Putni kofer writes that a pleasant surprise awaits you in Ozalj, a beautiful town built on a cliff above the magical River Kupa, located just 17 kilometres from Karlovac. Right there stands the most beautiful example of industrial architecture – the magnificent hydroelectric power plant “Munjara”, which is also the oldest hydroelectric power plant in the whole of continental Croatia. And to make things even better, it still produces electricity to this very day.

construction took just 15 months

This beauty looks like a real castle, proudly standing in the middle of the river – more precisely on its natural waterfall – and from it there is also a magnificent view of the stone structure of the Old Town of Ozalj. The legendary “Munjara” was put into operation way back in 1908 in order to supply neighbouring Karlovac with lighting. Its construction lasted only 15 months, which is an impressive fact even for today’s times. It was built according to the designs of civil engineer Valerijan Rieszner, and its impressive historicist appearance is the work of the famous Austrian architect Hermann Bollé, who participated in the urban design of Zagreb and who, among other things, restored and built the Mirogoj cemetery complex and the building of the Museum of Arts and Crafts in the capital.

it was the brainchild of the one and only nikola tesla

The Ozalj hydroelectric plant truly looks spectacular, just like a stone neoclassical palace with crown-like battlements and harmonious arcades, surrounded by tall spruces… And did you know that our greatest inventor and engineer Nikola Tesla lobbied as early as 1892 for the construction of a hydroelectric power plant on the Korana or the Kupa? His vision was realised in 1908, when Karlovac finally got public electric lighting. As a reminder, Šibenik was the first to receive it in 1895, while Zagreb was electrified in the autumn of 1907. In the years that followed, the “Munjara” hydroelectric power plant significantly contributed to the industrial development of Ozalj, Karlovac and Duga Resa. This facility of great historical significance is a protected cultural asset under the supervision of the Directorate for the Protection of Cultural Heritage and the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Croatia, and after 118 years of existence and with more than 5,000 hours of operation per year, it continues to produce electricity today.

time moved on, but munjara remains

Initially, “Munjara”, with its two Francis turbines, served only for the public lighting of the city of Karlovac, and consumption was free! But when the development of the entire Ozalj region began to be encouraged after the Second World War, demand for electricity also increased, so in 1948 construction of a second hydroelectric power plant began on the left bank of the Kupa. However, the beautiful “Munjara”, you will likely agree, is impossible to surpass. This striking building can be visited with a guided tour by the plant’s expert staff, and all details about registration and visiting can be found here.

World.title: Copernicus Marine Analysis Finds Concerning Changes to Croatian Waters
World.content:
October the 4th, 2026 – The ten-year Copernicus Marine analysis has found some very concerning changes to Croatian waters, some of which are now deemed irreversible.

The tenth edition of the Copernicus Ocean State Report (OSR10), published on the 30th of September 2026, summarises a decade of systematic monitoring of the oceans and European seas (Grégoire et al., 2026). Morski reports that among the exceptional events of 2024, the report also highlights the Adriatic Sea. This analysis presents what the report says about the Adriatic, how these findings fit into changes across the entire Mediterranean, and what they mean for sea monitoring and management. It is based on the report summary (Mercator Ocean International, 2026) and on chapters published in the State of the Planet series.

croatian waters and the wider mediterranean context

The Mediterranean Sea is warming significantly faster than the global average: its surface temperature rose by 0.32 ± 0.01 °C per decade in the period 1982–2024, while the global sea surface temperature is rising by 0.12 °C per decade (EU Space Programme, 2026; Mercator Ocean International, 2026). In 2024 the Mediterranean recorded the highest number of marine heatwave days in the last two decades, regardless of the detection method, and average temperatures were 1.23 °C above the baseline (Fernández-Álvarez et al., 2026). The most extreme conditions were recorded in the eastern Mediterranean. Sea level is not rising uniformly: decade-long trends differ between the western and eastern basins (Borile et al., 2026), and among the cities for which the summary shows changes over the last decade are Venice and Trieste in the northern Adriatic.

The Adriatic is the northernmost and shallowest part of the Mediterranean and is therefore highly sensitive to influences from the land. Limited water exchange, strong land–sea connectivity and high anthropogenic pressure make it vulnerable to disturbances (Coll et al., 2010, according to Krauzig et al., 2026). Along the north-western coast the Po and numerous smaller rivers flow into the sea, bringing freshwater rich in nutrients. This water is mainly transported southwards along the Italian coast by the Western Adriatic Current (Cozzi and Giani, 2011).

five episodes of surface freshening

Krauzig et al. (2026) analysed high-frequency measurements from two autonomous meteo-marine stations – the Fortunae buoy near Fano and the Meda station near Senigallia – as well as data on precipitation and river discharges, satellite images and Copernicus Marine Service products. In the period from May 2023 to November 2024 they identified five separate freshening episodes lasting from 12 to 53 days, with salinity drops of 6.7 to 20.1 g kg⁻¹.

Table 1. Surface freshening episodes in the northern Adriatic, 2023–2024 (according to Krauzig et al., 2026)

The first episode is particularly illustrative because salinity fell from 36.19 to 23.42 g kg⁻¹ in just 13 days. The most extreme was the fifth, in which salinity decreased from 35.09 to 14.97 g kg⁻¹ in 10 days – the most intense freshening in the entire series. The authors distinguish episodes driven by prolonged, abundant inflow (the first) from those with a faster and sharper drop (the second and fourth). This points to the dual sensitivity of the basin: to sustained meteorological pressure and to sudden, short-lived hydrological extremes.

Figure 1. Salinity drop during the fastest freshening by episode (according to Krauzig et al., 2026)

a mix of causes…

The first freshening was linked to a series of five rainy episodes in the Emilia-Romagna region from 1 to 24 May 2023, which culminated in catastrophic floods. Storm Minerva (from the 16th to the 18th of May) brought more than 300 mm of precipitation near Forlì – more than five times the monthly climatological average. Interestingly, the Po remained well below its average discharge during that period, at around 2,000 m³ s⁻¹, because the most intense rainfall did not affect its main catchment, while smaller rivers such as the Lamone, Savio and Reno exceeded historical flood levels. The second episode was probably caused by local convective storms in the Marche region, and the third by prolonged rainfall in November and early December 2023, when up to 383 mm of rain fell in the Parma Apennines. The fourth was triggered by an unusual spring storm in April 2024, with 70 to 80 mm of lighter but persistent precipitation.

Autumn 2024 brought a new series of extremes. Storm Boris (17–20 September) dumped around 300 mm of precipitation in eastern Emilia-Romagna, and on the 18th and 19th of October a new storm caused record discharges of all major rivers; the Po’s discharge reached 7,880 m³ s⁻¹. The authors interpret this as a sign of a pronounced hydrological recovery after a prolonged drought, and the transition from drought to water abundance is precisely the key difference between 2023 and 2024. Statistically significant links between accumulated precipitation and river discharges (p < 0.05) show time lags of 6 to 120 hours: small rivers with short catchments, such as the Rubicon, respond almost immediately (r = 0.74; lag 6 h), while larger catchments, such as the Adige, respond with a delay (r = 0.71; lag 36 h). Such findings fit the concept of “precipitation whiplash” – sudden transitions between dry and wet extremes (Tan et al., 2023).

the ecological consequences

Every freshening triggered a pronounced biogeochemical response. After the first episode turbidity averaged around 70 NTU for more than a month, with chlorophyll-a above 10 µg L⁻¹, reflecting the simultaneous inflow of sediment and nutrients. Back in June and July 2023 turbidity exceeded 200 NTU and chlorophyll-a 30 µg L⁻¹, and mucilaginous macroaggregates – gelatinous accumulations associated with warm, stratified and nutrient-rich conditions – were observed (Arrighi and Domeneghetti, 2024). Such phenomena impair seawater quality and threaten mariculture and tourism. The second episode shows that even smaller convective systems can stimulate biological productivity without a large sediment input: turbidity remained low, while chlorophyll-a and oxygen saturation, which reached around 150 %, rose almost simultaneously (r = 0.77). The strongest response was recorded after the fifth episode, when chlorophyll-a exceeded 60 µg L⁻¹ with unusually low turbidity. The authors interpret this as the sediments from the Po having probably settled or dispersed before reaching the stations, while nutrients continued to be transported, and favourable light conditions enabled increased primary production. In the summers of 2023 and 2024 the sea surface temperature exceeded 30 °C, accompanied by extensive accumulations of mucilaginous aggregates (Krauzig et al., 2026). An independent chapter by Di Biagio et al. (2026) confirms this picture with a model and satellite approach: in spring and autumn 2024 the northern Adriatic was marked by anomalous eutrophication, and chlorophyll concentrations in early spring 2024 were more than twice the usual average (Mercator Ocean International, 2026).

significance for croatian waters

Three limitations should be taken into account when interpreting the findings. First, the measurements come from two points along the western (Italian) coast and cannot be mechanically transferred to the entire basin. Second, the estimate of freshwater inflow of around 42.5 m³ h⁻¹ per metre of coastline for the first freshening is based on a simplified salt mass balance and is more suitable for comparing orders of magnitude than as an estimate of total discharge. Third, this is a period of only two years, so long-term trends cannot be derived from it: the events are an indicator of the basin’s vulnerability, not proof of permanent change (Krauzig et al., 2026).

For the Croatian coast, where tourism, mariculture and fisheries are of great economic importance, the key question is the extent to which such events are reflected on the eastern Adriatic. The report does not answer this directly: the observations are limited to the Italian coast, and the current cited by the authors transports freshwater southwards along the western coast. Effects in Croatian waters therefore cannot be assumed, but must be verified by continuous observations and domestic research of our own.

this reports conclusion for croatian waters

The central message of the report is that knowledge about the ocean needs to be turned into action through three levels: monitoring, forecasting and planning (Mercator Ocean International, 2026). The Adriatic example illustrates all three. Relatively inexpensive autonomous stations with high sampling frequency recorded sudden changes that satellite and reanalysis fields would have captured only partially, so the authors recommend including such observations in Copernicus and other databases. Coastal forecasting models are important for monitoring land–sea dynamics (Di Biagio et al., 2026); this is also confirmed by the Baltic example, in which a forecasting system accurately predicted a record drop in sea level three to four days in advance (Tuomi et al., 2026). For planning it is important that, according to the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, heavy precipitation and river flooding will become more frequent and intense when the global temperature exceeds 1.5 °C, and small catchments such as those along the north-western Adriatic are considered particularly vulnerable by the authors (IPCC, 2023, according to Krauzig et al., 2026).

The Adriatic, primarily its shallow northern part, shows how complex events – from sudden alternations of drought and floods through freshening and stratification to phytoplankton blooms and mucilaginous aggregates – form a cause-and-effect chain with direct consequences for seawater quality, mariculture and tourism. At the same time, the limitations of the available data remind us that systematic and openly accessible observations from both sides of the basin are needed for a reliable assessment of the state of the entire Adriatic, including the Croatian coast.

World.title: How Will Croatian Road Tolls Function Without the ENC?
World.content:
October the 4th, 2026 – Croatian road tolls are about to alter forever, but how exactly will they function without the famed ENC after March 2027?

Croatian Motorways state that the new system will apply to the entire motorway network in Croatia, including sections managed by HAC, Bina-Istra and Autocesta Zagreb-Macelj. Poslovni reports that as of the 1st of March 2027, it should be possible to travel on Croatian motorways without toll booths and without stopping. This option is particularly important for occasional and foreign motorway users, but before the system is introduced they still need to check how the vehicle will be included in the charging system and how the bill will be settled.

Croatian Motorways state that the new system will apply to the entire motorway network in Croatia, including sections managed by HAC, Bina-Istra and Autocesta Zagreb-Macelj. The toll will continue to be calculated according to the distance travelled and the vehicle category, but passage will be recorded electronically, without stopping at a barrier.

According to the Toll Collection Act, light vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes will be able to use an ENC device or be registered in a system that automatically reads registration plates. Heavy goods vehicles will have to use an on-board device. The system will thus combine ENC technology with cameras for automatic licence plate recognition.

HAC emphasises that reading registration plates is intended for light vehicles without ENC, i.e. for occasional and foreign users. This could simplify passage for tourists who travel through Croatia by car and do not use ENC throughout the year. However, the official information published so far does not provide all the details about vehicle registration, linking payment methods or charging for users who only come to the country occasionally. Therefore, drivers without ENC should not yet be advised to take steps that the competent authorities have not yet officially described. Before the system starts operating, it will be important to follow the instructions of Croatian Motorways and the official Crolibertas website. The basic rules are known – light vehicles can choose between ENC and licence plate reading, and motorways will no longer be passed through toll booths – but the exact procedure for occasional and foreign users will need to be confirmed once all implementing instructions are published.

World.title: Croatia Suffer Heaviest Defeat in History in 7-0 Loss to England
World.content:
Croatia hosted England at Rujevica in Rijeka in the third round of Nations League A, Group 3. Both sides went into the match with three points, each having beaten the Czech Republic and lost to Spain. After a win against the Czechs in Prague and a defeat to Spain in Seville, Croatia welcomed England for a 6 pm kickoff, but the evening turned into the darkest in the national team’s history.

Due to a UEFA sanction, no tickets were sold for the match, but the stands were far from empty, as around 6,000 children from primary schools and football academies across Croatia, accompanied by their coaches, turned out to support the Vatreni.

Lineups:

CROATIA: Livaković, Stanišić (Šutalo 76′), Vušković, Gvardiol, Perišić, Modrić (Jakić 56′), Kovačić (yellow card), Baturina (Vlašić 46′), P. Sučić (Mario Pašalić 46′), Ivanović, Musa (Matanović 46′)

ENGLAND: Pickford, Quansah, Konsa, Guehi, Hall (Gibbs-White 80′), Anderson (Lewis-Skelly 80′), Scott (Garner 69′), Saka, Gordon (Eze 69′), Bellingham, Kane (Rogers 69′)



Match report

German referee Sven Jablonski got the match underway, and England threatened from the start, with Livaković ready for Gordon’s third-minute effort. The visitors took the lead in the eighth minute after Joško Gvardiol played a loose pass into the middle. England pounced, and Jude Bellingham slipped in an unmarked Kane. The England captain had time to compose himself and lifted the ball over Livaković from around ten meters to make it 1-0.

By the 20th minute, England were in total control, with Croatia unable to get out of their own half. A minute later, England struck again, this time through Bellingham. Livaković denied Gordon a sitter in the 25th minute, and at the half-hour mark Croatia were still searching for their first attempt on the England goal. In the 35th minute, Perišić delivered a good cross into the box, but Pickford punched clear.

England crowned their dominance with a third goal in the 39th minute, as Gordon finally beat his club teammate Livaković at the third attempt. Croatia registered their first shot on target in the 41st minute from a Stanišić cross, though it posed no danger to England. Moments later came Croatia’s first real chance, but after weaving through the English defence, Kovačić’s finish lacked accuracy.

England added a fourth right on the stroke of half-time. In the 45th minute, Bellingham crossed from the left to find Bukayo Saka completely alone five meters out, and the Arsenal forward had no trouble making it 4-0. Just one minute of stoppage time was added, and Croatia went into the break completely powerless after England’s show of strength at Rujevica.

Croatia made three changes at half-time, with Musa, Baturina and Petar Sučić staying in the dressing room and Matanović, Vlašić and Mario Pašalić coming on. Matanović nearly made an immediate impact in the 48th minute with a powerful strike from distance that flew just wide of the post. But the nightmare continued in the 53rd minute, when Kane grabbed his second of the night to make it 5-0.

Bellingham was off target with another England chance in the 56th minute, and Croatia captain Luka Modrić then made way for Kristijan Jakić. Croatia won their first corner of the match in the 62nd minute, but Pickford claimed Perišić’s delivery. In the 68th minute, Saka netted his second to put England 6-0 up, and Kovačić was shown a yellow card shortly after.

England manager Thomas Tuchel made a triple change in the 69th minute, bringing off Kane, Scott and Gordon for Rogers, Garner and Eze. Croatia brought on Šutalo for Stanišić in the 76th minute, while England replaced Hall and Anderson with Gibbs-White and Lewis-Skelly in the 80th.

Croatia’s heaviest ever defeat had been the 6-0 loss to Spain in the 2018 Nations League, and that record came under threat in the 72nd minute when Saka nearly added a seventh. Croatia brought on Šutalo for Stanišić in the 76th minute, while England replaced Hall and Anderson with Gibbs-White and Lewis-Skelly in the 80th.

Croatia’s players were left fuming in the 83rd minute when Franjo Ivanović went down in the box after a challenge from Konsa, but referee Jablonski waved away their penalty appeals. Four minutes later, the record was gone. In the 87th minute, Morgan Rogers collected a long ball from Bellingham in the Croatian half, raced clear on the counter, sent Livaković the wrong way and slotted home to make it 7-0, the heaviest defeat in Croatia’s history.

Croatia meets Spain next on Tuesday at Poljud.

World.title: airBaltic planning up to 700 layoffs across Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius
World.content:
Latvian airline airBaltic is planning layoffs that could affect 500–700 jobs across the Baltics, including in Tallinn, as it restructures its business.

airBaltic, which employs nearly 3,000 people across the Baltics, announced Monday it is taking steps to adapt its operations to a new business model, including changes to its workforce.

While the exact number of layoffs is still subject to change, the Latvian flag carrier currently estimates that planned changes could affect approximately 500–700 positions across its bases in Riga, Vilnius and Tallinn.

The airline has already notified the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund (EUIF) of the planned collective layoffs but declined to give estimates by base or employee group, saying more details will be shared with staff this month.

"No final decisions have been made regarding individual employees, and we will engage directly with our colleagues as the next steps are determined," CEO Erno Hildén said, pledging transparency and care throughout the sensitive process.

Long-haul overhaul

The measures aim to improve financial stability, streamline airBaltic's network and boost efficiency. The airline has previously announced plans to reduce its Airbus A220-300 fleet and expand year-round ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance and insurance) partnerships.

The planned changes will not affect airBaltic's flight schedule, the airline said Monday, with all scheduled flights currently operating as planned.

In mid-September, airBaltic announced it would restructure its financial obligations under U.S. law while continuing to operate normally. The company also secured a new €350 million loan at an interest rate of around 12 percent.

In August, Latvia's Saeima approved a bailout plan for the airline under which the state will provide airBaltic with up to another €30 million in funding and amend the terms of its existing obligations.

airBaltic reported a €44.34 million loss last year, several times smaller than in 2024, while revenue rose 4.2 percent to €779.34.

World.title: Riigikogu election campaigning gets going 5 months before polling day
World.content:
Many political parties have already activated their Riigikogu election campaigns with five months still to go.

This relatively early start is deliberate, with factors such as campaign costs, voter fatigue and what the other parties are doing all being weighed up.

Another new development is that social media campaigning is now banned, "Aktuaalne kaamera" reported.

The Riigikogu elections take place in early March, but campaigning season is already underway just as the days get shorter and the weather grayer. To counter this, parties were seen to set up colorful tents, with flags and other decorations.

If anything, campaign season has started a little early, something which the opposition Social Democrats (SDE) party's campaign manager, Karmo Kuri, put down to election-fatigue setting in with the public when polling day gets nearer.

"What we have noticed is that at the height of the campaign, when people are already starting to get fed up with it, they say, 'Why do you only come out here just before the elections?' That has also been our starting point," Kuri told "Aktuaalne kaamera."

Parties can end up spending millions of euros on their campaigning, and members, leading and grass roots alike, are often expected to chip in too.

Isamaa MP Riina Solman said she was stumping up thousands of euros of her own money.

"My budget right now is €10,000, which I can set aside from my salary. But on top of that there is also the party's campaign. Senior politicians are also included in the party's campaign and on its posters," Solman, whose party is also in opposition nationwide, though in office with Center in Tallinn, noted.

As for the Center Party, its members will have to dig deepest into their own pockets, as the party's financial situation has not been good for a long time, and as a result it is focusing mainly on direct contact with voters.

"If you also want posters, they actually cost quite a lot. Take the last local elections, for example. Right here on Pirita Road, a large poster for two weeks cost three and a half thousand euros," explained Pirita district elder and Center Party member Kaido Saarniit.

So what are the parties talking to the voters about? The economy and cost of living featured highly.

"The closer we get to winter, the more home heating, as well as our party's general approach to family policy and such issues, have come into focus," Kuri said.

"What we are asking people about today is how they feel about the excise duty increases that have now been imposed on fuel. And that grates on people. We are also collecting signatures against the fuel excise duty increase," Solman added.

Things will really get going in the new year, when strests, roadsides, advertising hoardings, shopping malls and other locations will start to fill with ' posters of politicians and their parties; TV and radio spots will accompany this.

"The tent campaign taking place across Estonia right now is still modest. These elections are going to be very active," Saarniit said.

One party which has not kicked off its campaign just yet is the coalition Reform Party. This is set to start in the second half of this month, by which time it should be clear what their current coalition partner Eesti 200's plans are – possibly including a merger with the Greens.

Similarly, the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) has still to unveil its campaign.

Campaigning will continue right up to polling day, March 7, 2027.

World.title: Gallery: Pre-war statesman reburied in Kuressaare over a century after death
World.content:
Estonian statesman Otto Pukk has been laid to rest on his home island of Saaremaa, 126 years after his birth there and 75 years after his death.

Pukk (1900–1951) was the last chair of Estonia's Riigivolikogu, the lower chamber of the legislature between the two world wars.

His remains, together with those of his wife, Agnes, were reburied at Kudjape cemetery in Kuressaare, the capital of Saaremaa, where he was born.

Pukk took part in the Estonian War of Independence (1918–1920) before fleeing to Sweden ahead of the Soviet occupation in 1944. He worked as a journalist, lawyer and politician. He served in two Riigikogu compositions and was the last chairman of the Estonian Riigivolikogu before the Soviet occupation. He was also a member of the Otto Tief government, briefly in office in September 1944 in the vacuum left by the Nazi occupiers' withdrawal and before the return of the Soviet occupiers later that same month.

The Kuressaare reburial was organized by family members including his grandchildren.

"It is a joyous event that my grandfather and grandmother are home again. That wish has always been there. In the early 1990s, when many statesmen were reburied, he had the opportunity too, but then my grandmother was still alive — over 100 years old — and he didn't quite want to. We finally took it on. This is a family initiative, and in that sense a circle is complete and their wish has been fulfilled," said Pukk's grandson, also named Otto.

Riigikogu Speaker Lauri Hussar was among those who addressed the ceremony.

World.title: QR codes for online drug sales popping up near Estonian schools
World.content:
QR code stickers appearing near schools in Estonia are directing users to a website selling drugs online, police say, raising concerns about access by minors.

The stickers have appeared in larger cities and lead to a site designed like an online store, with drugs, prices, payment options and even customer reviews included.

Police have received numerous reports about the stickers, many of which have been placed along children's routes to school.

At the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), Rain Vosman, head of the South Prefecture's Criminal Bureau, said the website was created in late 2025, but identifying those behind it is difficult.

He said police have a dedicated team working to take down drug-selling sites, but the process can take time. Vosman urged people to report such websites and remove QR stickers when they encounter them.

Generated image from a website selling drugs online. Source: screenshot

"We can see that the QR codes are changing, so there are probably several people printing or distributing them," he explained.

A single person could also be behind the operation, he continued, with those involved in printing and distributing the stickers recruited and paid to do so but unaware of where the codes actually lead.

Police believe the stickers are being deliberately placed near schools because minors are among the intended audience. Vosman said youths' curiosity and growing familiarity with cannabis may make some more willing to experiment without fully understanding what they are consuming.

Drug trade slides into DMs

Much of the drug trade has moved to messaging apps, Vosman said, with Telegram groups among the most common channels.

Feedback left on online drug sales. Source: screenshot

QR codes can be used to direct people to such groups, where drugs are offered and payments can be made by bank transfer or in cryptocurrency.

Police also say QR codes are used to recruit people as runners who hide drug packages and send their GPS coordinates to sellers in exchange for money.

While minors who take on such jobs may not realize they are participating in drug trafficking, those caught can face criminal liability for illegally handling narcotics.

"These are very serious offenses that can even land you behind bars," Vosman emphasized, adding that police will also confiscate any money earned from the activity.

World.title: Peeter Kaldre: A dangerous moment
World.content:
As the United States scales back its military role in Europe, the continent faces a dangerous test: strengthening its own defenses while Russia intensifies its threats and war against Ukraine.

It is appalling that 500 million people (Europe) have to ask 300 million people (the United States) for protection against 140 million people (Russia). That is what NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said recently when the subject of reducing the U.S. military presence in Europe came up. Rutte is certainly not the first to put it this way, but it illustrates the situation European security now finds itself in.

How to shoot yourself in the foot

The U.S. plan to reduce its military contribution to NATO and delegate more responsibility to European countries is nothing new; nearly every U.S. administration has talked about it. Why should the United States have to defend wealthy Europe when Europeans themselves barely lift a finger for their own defense? The difference is that the Donald Trump administration has now begun to act and the first cuts are already taking place.

All this is happening at a time when Russia is waging a full-scale war in Europe against Ukraine and is increasingly threatening European countries that support Ukraine.

The September 15 issue of Foreign Affairs featured an article by three security experts — Franklin C. Miller, Eric Edelman and Walter B. Slocombe — pointing to the risks posed by such a U.S. plan. The authors refer to a new security strategy completed last year that calls for shifting the focus from Europe to Asia and the Middle East.

The article lists military capabilities that the Americans want to cut in Europe but that Europe will not be able to replace anytime soon. Its conclusion is that such a policy threatens America itself — in other words, the United States would be hurting itself.

The U.S. military presence in Europe prevents potential adversaries from growing stronger and becoming a threat to the United States. One example cited is that, for the first time in many years, the United States did not take part in a NATO exercise in the North Atlantic that practiced countering Russian submarines. Those same nuclear-armed submarines are designed to approach the U.S. coast...

The story of the Dead Hand

Now the United States is pulling back, but Europe is simply not ready to replace the Americans. One way forward is through so-called coalitions of the willing, one example being the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF), led by the United Kingdom and comprising the Baltic and Nordic countries.

The JEF does not have to wait for NATO's Article 5 to be formally invoked; it can act immediately. Jamie Murray, commander of the British contingent stationed in Estonia, put it well: We are ready to go into battle immediately. There are currently 900 British troops in Estonia, with another 300 to be added next year.

We should also bear in mind that the United Kingdom has nuclear weapons, as does France. Although their combined arsenal cannot be compared with Russia's, the Kremlin still has to take it into account. In theory, NATO's collective defense provides for the possibility of using nuclear weapons, including in Estonia's defense. Finland's recent decision to allow nuclear weapons into or through the country in the event of a threat was a powerful statement.

Incidentally, Finland and Sweden seem to have been transformed since joining NATO. Sweden recently announced that if Russia attacks, Sweden will strike targets deep inside Russia.

As for nuclear weapons, Russia has recently begun threatening their use again. Some time ago, Vladimir Putin warned Europe at the Valdai forum that if European countries were planning to take action against Kaliningrad, Russia could resort to nuclear weapons.

There has also been renewed talk of the so-called Dead Hand, an underground system in the Urals that can launch nuclear weapons even if the country's political leadership has been eliminated. It is one of those "nice" Kremlin stories whose veracity cannot be taken for granted.

Nuclear weapons are, after all, Russia's last resort. It cannot defeat even Ukraine with conventional weapons, let alone prevail in a potential conflict with all of Europe. Before it comes to that, however, there are the so-called hybrid tools to try: sabotage, assassinations, election interference and so on. And, of course, brutal strikes against Ukraine's civilian infrastructure, along with disingenuous appeals to foreign countries to move their embassies out of Kyiv.

The aim is to frighten Europe into abandoning its support for Ukraine or at least scaling it back. Putin understands very well that if European support for Ukraine continues, it will be almost impossible for him to subjugate the country.

A very dangerous period lies ahead. Russia may be tempted to make some move against Europe before next month's U.S. congressional midterm elections. Those elections could significantly change Washington's hitherto lenient approach toward Russia.

World.title: Lights not out on Tallinn's War of Independence Victory Column, but being replaced
World.content:
The lights recently being off on Estonia's War of Independence Victory Column in Freedom Square in Tallinn has a simple explanation.

While rumors have swirled that the column, unveiled in June 2009 and commemorating the 1918-1920 Estonian War of Independence, is due a major overhaul, this is not the case.

Ando Voogma, portfolio manager at the Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) told ERR the reason the column is not currently fully lit is because lighting replacement work is underway.

"Every technical system has its own lifespan, and this is the the case with the current elements too — their lifespan is practically over, some of the light sources have burned out, some have dimmed, and we are now replacing them with new ones," he said.

No further work is required, he said. "The previous owner replaced some glass elements. But I don't know of any major renovation having been done, and at the moment we have no need for major repairs. The current issue is replacing the light sources."

While in its early years the column had some teething problems and frequently needed minor works, things have settled down since then, Voogma went on.

"There are isolated issues from time to time, for example with the cladding on the outside of the column. As with any structure, we have to keep the whole in order, and that's part of routine maintenance and upkeep," Voogma said.

The column is nearly 24 meters high and is made up of 143 glass plates, topped off with the Cross of Liberty. It is the focal point of commemorative events such as the Independence Day military parade every February 24.

World.title: Gallery: Decades of wild mushroom photography on display in Saaremaa
World.content:
On the Western Estonian island of Saaremaa, nearly 300 photographs are now on display at a local nature center, spotlighting decades of work by mycologist Vello Liiv.

The exhibition at Viidumäe Nature Center opened Sunday, and unlike most mushroom displays, may remain open to visitors for a year or more.

"Look, there they are," Liiv remarked in passing when he spotted mushrooms growing beside a tree stump outside the center.

"When you've spent nearly half your life walking with your head down, you can't really start looking up anymore," he quipped. "You keep seeing the grass and that part of the forest floor."

Still, the nearly 300 photographs on display represent only a small fraction of the mushrooms he has photographed over more than half a century. The University of Tartu's collections, he noted, contain around 3,000 species.

The Viidumäe exhibition is both artistic and scientific in nature, said artist Anna Talvi, who worked on the display.

Vello Liiv's new wild mushroom photo exhibition at Viidumäe Nature Center in Saaremaa. October 2026. Source: Margus Muld/ERR

"The way Vello photographs these mushrooms is beautiful in its own right," Talvi said. "But he also photographs and arranges them in ways that most clearly highlight each species' unique characteristics."

Liiv said he has never deliberately tried to make mushrooms look beautiful. Many of the species he has photographed, however, are ones he has only ever encountered once.

"Oh, there are so many of them," he said. Of the roughly 3,000 species, he estimates he has seen, photographed and identified about 2,500 only once before adding them to a herbarium.

The mushrooms people typically recognize as mushrooms, he added, actually only make up a much smaller bunch of around 300 species.

World.title: US gives Estonia 13 reconnaissance drones to boost border security
World.content:
The United States has provided Estonia with 13 Skydio X10D drones to help the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) monitor hard-to-reach areas along the country's borders.

U.S. Ambassador to Estonia Roman Pipko and PPA Deputy Director General Veiko Kommusaar signed the transfer agreement for the 13 small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS) at Tallinn's Miinisadam Naval Base on Monday.

Following the signing, PPA personnel conducted a demonstration flight for the officials.

Skydio X10D drones are small enough to be carried by hand, can be launched quickly and are equipped with both daytime and thermal cameras, allowing officials to monitor hard-to-reach areas around the clock, the U.S. Embassy said in a press release.

"These transfers represent both the U.S. commitment to Estonian security and the expertise that our Estonian partners bring to their work every day," Pipko said.

"I believe continued cooperation in this area will strengthen both of our borders and make our two countries safer," the ambassador continued, adding that U.S. border officials could learn from their Estonian counterparts.

The transfer of the drones was funded by the U.S. State Department's Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL), with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) implementing the program.

Drone demonstration at Miinisadam Naval Base in Tallinn. Source: U.S. Embassy Tallinn

World.title: Iraq plans to purchase large oil tankers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil has announced plans to secure funding for the purchase of new tankers—a move intended to bolster export operations and maximize revenues.

This initiative comes amid the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz and shipping disruptions in the Arabian Gulf. However, experts have raised questions regarding the project’s economic viability, cost, and timing, as well as its actual capacity to safeguard Iraqi exports during times of crisis.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Saturday that the ministry is coordinating with the government to secure the necessary funds to purchase oil tankers for the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC), enabling the firm to carry out crude oil transport operations.

Khudair noted that the ownership of such oil tankers would bolster exports, ensure economic viability, and maximize financial returns.

The IOTC once owned 23 tankers before its fleet dwindled over the past few decades due to wars, sanctions, and the suspension of modernization efforts.

Iraq’s current fleet is limited to six small-capacity tankers used primarily for transporting petroleum products and lacks supertankers for crude oil.

The Ministry of Oil is looking to acquire modern tankers with a capacity of two million barrels to enhance Iraq’s maritime transport capabilities and facilitate the transportation of a portion of its oil shipments.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament to discuss 2027 budget with $48.8 billion deficit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s parliament is about to start official deliberations on the 2027 federal budget, which has a significant 64 trillion Iraqi dinar ($48.8 billion) deficit.

Following the exclusion of a 2026 budget due to enormous political and economic challenges, the Iraqi Ministry of Finance has expedited the 2027 draft to meet the deadline for parliamentary submission.

The new budget’s total expenditure is projected at roughly 200 trillion Iraqi dinar (approximately $152.6 billion), matching previous record-high spending levels.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

Oil valuations in the new budget are based on a cautious benchmark price of $60 to $70 per barrel.

Earlier this year, regional military tensions prompted Iran to temporarily close the Strait of Hormuz, negatively affecting Iraqi oil exports.

At peak times of the crisis, Iraq’s monthly export volumes fell by almost 80 percent, resulting in tens of billions of dollars in lost income and a major public-sector salary issue.

Despite liquidity concerns, the Iraqi government is sustaining massive fixed expenses, including plans to permanently transfer almost one million contract workers and daily wage earners to permanent public service positions.

Additionally, tensions remain over allocations for the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG). According to reports, Erbil seeks a 14 percent share of the national budget based on recent census figures.

The Parliamentary Finance Committee is holding extensive preparatory briefings to look over non-oil income files, currency value, and social safety nets before the final document goes through its first reading.

World.title: German airlines to resume direct flights to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport revealed on Sunday that German airlines will resume direct flights to Baghdad International Airport, operating four weekly flights from Berlin and Dusseldorf.

The ministry said in a statement that Eurowings, a subsidiary of the Lufthansa Group, has announced that it will operate four direct weekly flights to Baghdad: two from Berlin and two from Dusseldorf.

The service, which is set to begin on December 10, 2026, reflects the growing confidence in Baghdad International Airport and the development of Iraq’s air transport sector.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to improve compliance with international criteria that apply to the national airline and Iraqi airports, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The development follows visits by specialized technical and operational delegations to Baghdad International Airport over the past three months to inspect the airport’s procedures and systems.

The visits ensured the airport’s compliance with international standards for security and operations, with the ultimate goal of meeting all flight operations requirements.

The decision represents a crucial advancement in enhancing the presence of European airlines within the Iraqi market.

The decision marks a big step toward increasing the operation of European airlines in the Iraqi market. It opens up new opportunities for European airlines to explore establishing more direct services to Baghdad.

German passenger airlines last flew to and from Iraq in the early 1980s. The new development signals the restoration of passenger services between the two countries. In addition, more than ten German companies have requested to operate flights to Iraq.

World.title: India tops Iraq U-17 Women 14–0 in Asian Cup qualifier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNew.com) – The Iraqi U-17 Women’s National Football Team endured a difficult opening fixture in the AFC U-17 Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers on Monday, October 5, 2026, falling 14–0 to India in their Group E curtain-raiser at the MP Selayang Stadium in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

The Indian side established early attacking dominance, concluding the first half with a commanding 7–0 advantage before adding another seven unanswered goals in the second period.

The encounter was disrupted in the 64th minute—with the scoreline standing at 9–0—when match officials enforced an extended weather stoppage due to heavy thunderstorms and lightning activity around the stadium perimeter before play resumed.

Despite the setback, the young Iraqi squad is preparing for two crucial remaining group fixtures as they continue their qualifying campaign:

Matchday 2: Facing tournament hosts Malaysia on Thursday, October 8, 2026, kicking off at 4:00 PM Baghdad Time.

Matchday 3: Concluding group play against Syria on Sunday, October 11, 2026, scheduled for an early morning kickoff at 10:30 AM Baghdad Time.

The coaching staff will focus on tactical adjustments and defensive organization to regroup the squad ahead of Thursday’s match against Malaysia.

World.title: Nujaba leader defies Baghdad arrests over US flag desecration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Akram Al-Kaabi, Secretary-General of Harakat al-Nujaba, voiced defiance against the Iraqi federal government following the arrest of several youths who desecrated the American flag during Sovereignty Day celebrations in Baghdad.

In a video published to his personal account on X (formerly Twitter), Al-Kaabi appeared walking across a U.S. flag spread on the ground, accompanied by the caption: “Your crimes are beneath our feet.”

The visual gesture followed a formal statement released by Harakat al-Nujaba on Sunday, October 4, demanding the immediate release of the detainees.

Abdul-Qadir Al-Karbalai, the movement’s military deputy, denounced the arrests in a post on X, characterizing the detention of demonstrators as a “dangerous precedent” that the group refused to tolerate.

The security crackdown originated during Sovereignty Day parades marking the full withdrawal of International Coalition forces from Iraq.

The Joint Operations Command confirmed the apprehension of individuals who trampled the American flag during a public procession in Baghdad, acting upon directives issued by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi.

The Prime Minister ordered the formation of a formal investigative committee to probe the incident and enforce legal standards governing public parades, coming as his administration pursues a comprehensive state monopoly over arms and works to balance foreign relations following the coalition’s departure.

World.title: US dollar surges past 160,000 IQD in Baghdad and Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar surged past the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency exchanges on Monday, October 5, 2026, marking a sharp escalation in exchange volatility and setting fresh multi-month highs across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

The rapid upward movement widens the spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s statutory official rate of 131,000 dinars per $100 to over 22.5 percent, reversing last week’s brief stabilization.

Daily market data showed that wholesale and retail exchange bureaus in Baghdad posted cash selling rates at 160,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 159,500 dinars, registering an increase of approximately 3,000 dinars compared to Thursday’s close.

In Erbil, the commercial capital of the Kurdistan Region, parallel desks quoted selling rates at 160,150 dinars per $100, while buying bids held at 159,750 dinars. In the southern trade center of Basra, greenbacks traded slightly lower but approached the barrier, with selling figures quoted at 159,500 dinars per $100 alongside buying offers at 159,000 dinars.

The sudden rally across domestic currency trading floors comes amid renewed cash-procurement pressure from private commercial merchants and wholesale importers securing foreign exchange outside the official electronic platform.

Currency traders in Baghdad note that heightened regional market friction and temporary lulls in physical greenback distribution have driven rapid retail speculation, pushing exchange rates past psychological resistance levels despite official regulatory efforts to anchor market liquidity.

World.title: Iraqi Line to resume Gulf maritime route after 50-year hiatus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport announced on Monday, October 5, 2026, that the state-owned commercial carrier “Iraqi Line” is preparing to resume regular maritime operations across the Arabian Gulf after a hiatus exceeding 50 years.

According to an official statement, the national carrier’s maiden voyage is scheduled to depart on October 15, 2026, from Jebel Ali Port in the United Arab Emirates bound directly for Umm Qasr Port in southern Iraq.

The ministry stated that the reactivation of the shipping lane was initiated under the direct instructions of Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani as part of a ministerial agenda aimed at revitalizing national shipping assets and asserting sovereign maritime presence in regional trade routes.

The scheduled October 15 service marks the formal re-entry of the Iraqi flag carrier into Gulf container shipping lanes, establishing a state-backed logistical alternative for domestic merchants importing bulk goods and containerized freight.

The Transport Ministry emphasized that re-establishing the Iraqi Line serves to expand cargo volumes channeled through federal ports, stimulate bilateral trade with neighboring Gulf economies, and integrate domestic shipping fleets into regional supply chains.

Ministry records noted that the last scheduled commercial voyages executed by sovereign Iraqi cargo vessels across the Gulf took place in the mid-1960s, framing the upcoming Jebel Ali–Umm Qasr service as a milestone in the institutional modernization and operational recovery of Iraq’s commercial maritime sector.

World.title: Colts top Commanders in NFL London game
World.content:
Los Angeles – Indianapolis running back Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns as the Colts defeated the injury-hit Washington Commanders 30-13 on Sunday in the NFL’s latest foray in London.

Taylor had ample opportunity to unveil his London-themed celebration, miming sipping tea after finding the end zone late in the first half at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and again early in the third quarter to give the Colts a 17-6 lead.

“I just think that any time we have an opportunity to put a great product on the field and showcase the game that we love (to) fans all across the world, on the international stage, we always try to put our best foot forward,” Taylor told NFL Network.

“The crowd was electric, the energy was amazing and I can’t wait to come back to London.”

The Commanders, already missing star quarterback Jayden Daniels with a dislocated left elbow, saw veteran backup Marcus Mariota depart with a right knee injury in the opening minutes.

Mariota — who led Washington to an upset win over the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks last week — was replaced by rookie seventh-round draft pick Athan Kaliakmanis.

Kaliakmanis came up with some impressive plays, connecting on passes of 48 and 47 yards, but had an 87-yard TD nullified by a penalty.

The contest was one of nine NFL international games this season and the first of three in London this month.

It launched a Sunday slate that will feature the Las Vegas Raiders hosting the Kansas City Chiefs in a battle of unbeaten AFC West division rivals.

The Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers also put their perfect 3-0 records on the line.

Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen takes a historic rushing touchdown streak into the Bills’ home game against the New England Patriots.

With two rushing TDs in each of the first three games, Allen became the first quarterback to rush for multiple touchdowns in three straight games.

He could become the first player in NFL history — regardless of position — to record multiple rushing TDs in four straight games to start the season.

The 49ers host the Denver Broncos and the Vikings host the Miami Dolphins.

World.title: 'World is an age of flux, but India will rise to challenges': S Jaishankar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister

on Monday said the world is in âan age of flux,â but asserted that India has demonstrated its ability to ârise to the challenges.â

Jaishankar made the remarks during an interactive session on the third and final day of the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in the capital.

He shared the dais with Singaporeâs former foreign minister, George Yong Boon Yeo, during the concluding session of the event.

Asked how he viewed the challenges ahead amid growing geopolitical uncertainties, the external affairs minister outlined his assessment of the evolving global landscape.

âWe know that this is going to be an age of flux, as you call it. It is going to be turbulent and volatile, with uncertainties.

We are seeing two major conflicts, along with other frictions. As I said, there is pressure from non-market factors and tariff volatility,â PTI quoted Jaishankar as saying. He was referring to the Ukraine-Russia and US-Iran wars.

âTaking all of this into account, yes, these are choppy waters,â he added.

World.title: ‘Police can’t remain mute spectators’: Delhi HC dismisses pleas for fresh probe into 2019 Jamia violence
World.content:
The

on Monday dismissed petitions seeking an independent probe into alleged police brutalities against students during the December 2019 violence at Jamia Millia Islamia. The court observed that police cannot be expected to remain âmute spectatorâ when a gathering turns violent.

A bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain said the police did not enter the university premises at the outset when the assembly was peaceful, but intervened after the situation outside the campus escalated and the crowd moved into the university.

âThe police intervention, therefore, has to be viewed in the prevailing law and order situation which had developed at that time,â the court said.

âPolice cannot be expected to remain inactiveâ

The bench said the right to peaceful protest was not in dispute.

Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution protect freedom of speech and expression and the right to assemble peacefully without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions.

These rights do not, however, extend to causing any violence or destruction of property, it said.

âOnce a gathering ceases to remain peaceful and the circumstances disclose violence, commission of cognisable offences or a threat to life or property, the police cannot be expected to remain inactive or as mute spectator merely because the gathering is taking place within a university campus,â the court observed.





The petitions sought an independent judicial inquiry into the violence, an investigation into alleged police excesses and compensation for injured students.

âThe events of December 2019 undoubtedly generated considerable public concern and gave rise to serious allegations regarding the conduct of various stakeholders,â the court said.

The bench noted that protests on December 15, 2019, had escalated into violence around the university, including stone-pelting, burning of buses and other vehicles, damage to public property and attacks on police personnel.

The high court also noted shortcomings in the police response, referring to the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) inquiry, which found that the use of tear gas shells inside the university library could have been avoided.

It said a university was a place of learning and academic activity, and this âcrucial aspectâ must be considered while exercising police powers.

âThat consideration cannot, however, be taken to mean that the police are prohibited from entering a university campus in all circumstances,â the court said.

It added that university authorities should, wherever circumstances permit, be informed and consulted before police intervention. However, an immediate threat to life or property or a rapidly developing law-and-order situation may leave no time for prior communication or permission.

The court noted that criminal cases had been registered, an investigation conducted by the Delhi Police Crime Branch's Special Investigation Team (SIT), and charge sheets filed before competent courts. The NHRC had submitted its report in May 2020.

âNo subsequent incident or material has been brought to our notice to show that the violations of guidelines as alleged in these petitions have continued or have been repeated,â it said.

World.title: 'Fear of losing minority votes': MP CM slams Congress for silence on pilot Smit Machchhar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav on Monday slammed Congress for maintaining silence on Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who was seriously injured after his Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked him in the cockpit of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flydubai flight, saying the grand-old party feared losing minority votes.

"An Omani man attacked an Indian person (pilot Smit Machchhar) with an axe inside an aircraft flying to Israel, and the Indian man risked his life to save the lives of around 200 people. Such bravery is part of Sanatan culture, but Congress leaders are not praising Machchhar for fear of losing minority votes," Yadav said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Congress leaders hungry for votes should be ashamed of such behaviour," Yadav added.

Last week, Machchhar was attacked aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

Despite being seriously injured, he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing others to intervene and helping prevent the aircraft from being brought down. The plane was subsequently diverted safely to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

Earlier on Sunday, BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also attacked Congress and questioned why senior Congress leaders had not publicly acknowledged Machchhar's brave actions.

"For India, this is an occasion of great pride, but there are also some occasions that are a matter of shame. Not a single word, not a single post, and not a single press statement has come from the Congress family for Captain Smit Machchhar. This raises a serious question," Trivedi said.

Trivedi contrasted the Congress leadership's alleged silence with the response from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and leaders abroad, who praised Machchhar's act of bravery.

World.content:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Monday issued a âfact checkâ amid the controversy over reported changes to Form 6, calling Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhiâs claim that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had âchanged Form 6 illegally and unilaterallyâ misleading.In its response, the EC said the order for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar, issued on June 24, 2025, had received the unanimous approval of the Commission and was subsequently upheld by the Supreme Court in its judgment dated May 27, 2026.The poll panel also cited its Press Note No. 120 dated September 26, 2026, pointing to point 1(iii), which states: âThe declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.âThe EC's response came after Rahul alleged in a post on X that the CEC had changed Form 6 âillegally and unilaterallyâ, citing the recent Supreme Court observation.EC officials also clarified that Form 6 itself had not been changed, but that a declaration had been attached to the form under the Bihar SIR order, as quoted by PTI.The clarification came after the Supreme Court said it had not approved any modification to Form 6 used by the EC during the SIR exercise in various states.âAny modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When records are produced, we would like to see who has modified it,â a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said.Form 6 is the application used by eligible voters for inclusion in the electoral roll.The declaration was attached to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR, which began with the EC's June 24, 2025 order. The declaration sought additional details, including information about the applicant's parents.According to EC officials, the form itself remained unchanged, while the declaration was a separate document attached to it for the SIR exercise. Outside SIR, the forms prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 apply.The declaration was later withdrawn from the EC's online portals.The online version of Form 6 and the declaration also used a single OTP for both, rather than requiring separate OTP verification, which had led to suggestions that the declaration was part of Form 6.The EC also rejected claims that it had withdrawn its September 26 press note and shared the document to show that it remained available.

World.content:
NEW DELHI:

(SP) MP Dharmendra Yadav on Monday urged

leaders to refrain from making public statements on seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and instead raise the issue directly with SP president

.

His remarks came a day after Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge, Rajendra Pal Gautam, once again called for "

" for the grand old party in the state.

Dharmendra Yadav, Akhilesh Yadav's cousin, described the former chief minister as a "very large-hearted leader."

"I would tell my Congress colleagues, wherever they can win, they should not keep that point in front of the media. There is no need to keep it in the media. If they present it in the right way before our leader, then the entire country knows about our leader; he is a very large-hearted leader.

"We don't have any confusion. National president Akhilesh Yadav has the full trust of every leader, every worker, every voter of the Samajwadi Party. The BJP had won 312 seats that year. The Congress secured just seven seats in 2017, a tally that fell to just two when it contested the 2022 election on its own.

However, the SP-Congress alliance won 43 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha constituencies in 2024, with the SP winning 37 seats and the Congress six. The BJP won 33 constituencies, down from 62 in 2019.

World.title: 'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission.

Gavai said that a sitting judge should not have made comments on the ongoing row over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls as the matter is sub judice before the top court.

"Judicial propriety would not permit him to make any comment on the matter which is sub judice before the court," Gavai told news agency PTI.

Retired Delhi high court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also questioned Bhuyan's remarks.

Justice Dhingra said Bhuyan's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" and such comments should not be made at a public event when the issue is pending before the same court.

"He should have thought a thousand times before making such a statement," Dhingra said, adding that Justice Bhuyan did not know the full facts of the issue.

Justice R S Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan for calling the SIR exercise disenfranchisement and said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework.

"Whether you have a vote or you don't have a vote depends upon the statute. If you fall within the parameters of the statute, you have a vote.





If you don't fall within the parameters of the statute, you don't have a vote," Justice Sodhi said.

"I mean, these hardline thinking and these hardline statements, to my mind, are not a very mature way of looking at a thing, especially when you are supposed to be in a field which is supposed to be excellent in its rationalising," he said.

What Bhuyan had said

This comes a day after Justice Bhuyan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary" and a "negation" of the constitutional order.

While delivering the valedictory address at the 19th Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Justice Bhuyan said that the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and the other without voting rights, and no amount of "whataboutery" could justify such a process.

âIf any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary.

No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,â Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.

He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.

âNo authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,â he said.

This is not the first time that Justice Bhuyan has put forth his views on issues being discussed in the public domain.

Recently, NALSAR Hyderabad was in the news after a section of its students wrote to the vice chancellor, registrar and professors of the institution, opposing any proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest to the varsity's convocation.

World.title: Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Chirag Paswan once described himself as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "Hanuman". Six years later, the LJP (Ram Vilas) chief offered another approach of his politics: "I can stand up to my government .

.. I am in the alliance but I am not the BJP."

This distinction becomes relevant as he prepares to take his party into the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election. LJP(RV) has announced that it will contest the polls and is preparing for all 403 constituencies, while leaving open whether it will eventually contest alone or as part of an alliance.

We want this to take the form of a legal right for the youth. Wherever exams are cancelled, students should receive reimbursement for their travel expenses, arrangements for their accommodation, and provisions for their food. We have firmly presented this stance of the party on the floor of the House as well. Chirag Paswan

The UP move comes after a significant change in Chirag Paswan's political position.

In 2020, the undivided LJP broke with the NDA in Bihar, contested 135 seats and targeted Nitish Kumar's JD(U), while maintaining its support for PM Modi. Its slogan captured the strategy: "Modi se bair nahi, Nitish teri khair nahi." The party won only one seat, but its 5.66% vote share had a measurable impact on the results.

Since then, LJP(RV) has moved from being a marginal alliance partner to a more consequential NDA component.





It won all five Lok Sabha seats it contested in Bihar in 2024, giving Chirag Paswan a 100% strike rate, and in the 2025 assembly election it contested 29 seats under the NDA arrangement and won 19. The BJP and JD(U) contested 101 seats each, while LJP(RV) secured 29.
